enrichments.description:
The series follows the adventures of the main protagonist Aang and his friends, who must save the world by defeating Fire Lord Ozai and ending the destructive war with the Fire Nation. The series was originally slated for November 2004, but ended up airing on February 21, 2005. The show concluded with the widely lauded two-hour television movie on July 19, 2008. The show is available for purchase on DVD, Blu-ray, the iTunes Store, the Xbox Live Marketplace, the PlayStation Network, Amazon and YouTube. It is also available on streaming platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, the Nick website, and Paramount Global owned streaming platform, Paramount+. The show is occasionally aired on Nickelodeon's spinoff network, Nicktoons.

Avatar: The Last Airbender was popular with both audiences and critics, garnering 5.6 million viewers on its best-rated showing and receiving high ratings in the Nicktoons lineup, even outside its 6–11-year-old demographic. Avatar has been nominated for and won awards from the Annual Annie Awards, the Genesis Awards, and the primetime Emmy Awards, among others. The first season's success prompted Nickelodeon to order second and third seasons. The first part of a planned movie trilogy titled was released on July 1, 2010, and a produced by Netflix in partnership with Nickelodeon was released on February 22, 2024.

Merchandise based on the series includes scaled action figures, a trading card game, three video games based individually on each season, stuffed animals distributed by Paramount Parks, and two LEGO sets. The series' popularity spawned a sequel series, titled The Legend of Korra, which takes place seventy years after the original series, which released in 2012 and ran until 2015. In 2021, Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko came to helm a dedicated production studio with the primary goal of creating more stories and experiences set in and inspired by the universe spawned from the original animated series. Avatar Studios aims to release multiple movies and TV series following the legacy of the original show, beginning with a feature film, Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender which takes place roughly a decade after the original show, releasing on July 25, 2026, and a second sequel series, Avatar: Seven Havens releasing on October 9, 2026 both on Paramount+.

Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko began work on the series at Nickelodeon Animation Studios in Burbank, California. According to Bryan Konietzko, the program was conceived in the spring of 2001 when he took an old sketch of a balding, middle-aged man and re-imagined the character as a child. Konietzko drew the character herding bison in the sky and showed the sketch to Mike DiMartino. At the time, DiMartino was studying a documentary about explorers trapped in the South Pole.

entities.name: 46th Earth King
entities.description:
Strong-willed and imperious, the Earth King had little support from his people, and his reign was marked by many challenges to his rule which severely tested the Earth Kingdom's government.

The Earth Kingdom faced a rebellion led by Chin the Conqueror, a warlord from the country's far northwest. Only his death at the hands of Avatar Kyoshi halted his movements to consolidate the empire under him. The government's inability to deal with Chin's rebellion did, however, have repercussions. The massive losses the Earth Kingdom sustained led the citizens to realize many of the government's failures, and popular sentiment grew into the belief that the monarchy was outdated and did not support the people's interests. In Ba Sing Se, this belief led to a peasant uprising, with thousands storming the Upper Ring and destroying anything that represented the "old government". They eventually surrounded the Earth King's palace and demanded he be removed from his position.

Realizing he was unable to handle the revolt, the Earth King summoned Kyoshi to his court and ordered her to keep the populace in line. Kyoshi refused and requested that he listened to his people. Outraged by her audacity, the Earth King ordered her arrest, but the fully realized Avatar easily defeated his guards. Powerless against the might of the Avatar, the Earth King complied and had no other choice than to hear the peasants' complaints. In return, Kyoshi would protect his interests and Ba Sing Se's cultural heritage by training an elite force of earthbenders in the art of stealth, silence, and precision. This group became known as the Dai Li. With the Earth King's rule secure once more, he agreed to cooperate with Kyoshi in drafting a new constitution for the nation. This legislation transformed the Earth Kingdom into a constitutional monarchy, and greatly benefitted the country's poor. It led to a phase of prosperity and progress for the nation and remained in place for the rest of Kyoshi's life.

The Earth King had at least one child and was the direct ancestor of several later Earth Monarchs, including Kuei, the 52nd Earth King, and Earth Queen Hou-Ting.

entities.name: Aang
entities.description:
Shortly before the beginning of the Hundred Year War, Aang was frozen in an iceberg for a hundred years; he later emerged, still biologically twelve years old, into a world engulfed by war. The couple eventually married and raised a family of three children: Bumi, the oldest, a nonbender who became an airbender later in life; Kya, a waterbender; and the youngest, Tenzin, an airbender.

Aang was born to two Air Nomads in 12 BG. After selecting the Avatar relics from among thousands of toys, thereby inadvertently confirming his identity as the Avatar, he was taken away by the monks of the Southern Air Temple, who kept his position a secret from him. As an Air Nomad, Aang traveled extensively around the world. During his childhood, Aang was housed, raised, and educated at the Southern Air Temple, under the guardianship of Monk Gyatso, who served as his father figure, counselor, and tutor. After some time, he and several other young Air Nomad boys were taken to the Eastern Air Temple, where they each chose a sky bison as their lifelong companion. Aang approached his soon-to-be sky bison Appa and offered him an apple, which Appa accepted, thus marking the start of their deep and lifelong friendship.

Aang was always able to excel at any new bending moves he learned; at the age of six, he was a better airbender than children twice his age, and by the age of ten, Aang had proven himself to be better than his own teachers. He earned airbending tattoos and the status of an airbending master by the age of twelve for exhibiting prodigious talent with his native element and with his invention of the air scooter, making him the youngest airbending master in Air Nomad history at the time.

In his childhood, Aang also visited the other air temples, as evidenced by his obvious familiarity with the Western Air Temple, as well as cities in the Earth Kingdom, such as Omashu, where he developed a lasting friendship with the good-natured but eccentric Bumi.

entities.name: Adaki
entities.description:
Adaki was born to Adaro on Karr Lok Island in the Fire Nation His family traditionally worked as fire-fishers, using their firebending to attract fish to their boats at night. Adaki's father Adaro was quite proficient at this work, regularly impressing the young boy.

As Adaki grew up, he went to Karr Lok Island's school, Sunray Academy, where he made three friends: Jiyung, Aera, and Sujun. He came to adore the "Flame Throwers", a youth team of local firebenders who had won the nationwide bending competition. Adaki sought to emulate his father and the "Flame Throwers", hoping to become a more powerful firebender.

When he was eleven, Adaki began to help on his father's fishing boat. One night, he was allowed to act as the boat's firebender and tried to create a fireball which would attract a swarm of sardines, but the pressure of doing well as well as the poor weather conditions hampered the boy's efforts. His fireball was fairly weak and ineffective at attracting fish until his concentration was completely broken when a small winged animal temporarily landed on his shoulder, scaring him. At the urging of the other fishermen, Adaro subsequently took over from Adaki, quickly producing an effective flame and ensuring their tour's success.

Adaki was left frustrated about his inability to help his father, despite the latter consoling him. On the next day at school, the boy slept during Sifu Saruzo's mediation class due to his exhaustion. Afterward, he shared his experiences with his friends. The group were disrupted when they heard of a firebending match at one of the school's training rooms.

entities.name: Aera
entities.description:
Aera was born on Karr Lok Island of the Fire Nation. She was raised by her grandmother and lacked her left arm below the elbow, hindering her as she began to learn how to use her bending abilities. At first, Aera was trained by her grandmother on the beach near their house, focusing on leg-based firebending techniques. She struggled with traditional forms which usually required two arms.

Aera initially had difficulties in making friends, and often felt isolated despite her strong bond to her grandmother. As a result of her disability, she was occasionally bullied by a group of older children consisting of Tearan, Moriko, Akito, and Botan. The bullies observed her firebending training and mocked her whenever she made mistakes. Hoping to get better, Aera began to train with her shortened left arm at night, producing a delicate fire ribbon but nothing else.

One day, Tearan, Moriko, Akito, and Botan followed Aera and cornered her until a feral cat bat intervened. The animal protected Aera and drove the bullies away. Aera soon realized that Buddy loved the quick-moving fire ribbon which she could create with her disabled arm. Encouraged by the animal's positive reaction, she began to train with him at night and gradually mastered a unique technique, capable of controlling the fire ribbon in a precise way over a long distance. She often entertained Buddy by bending the ribbon in unpredictable ways.

Aera eventually began to attend the island's school, Sunray Academy, where she finally made three more friends: Adaki, Sujun, and Jiyung. She enjoyed teasing her friends, often surprising them by sneaking up on them. As cat bats had a poor reputation as dangerous pests, Aera initially did not dare to reveal her friendship with Buddy to Adaki, Sujun, and Jiyung. She assumed that they would reject her animal comrade.

entities.name: Afiko
entities.description:
Born in the Southern Air Temple, Afiko was seemingly normal growing up, but he grew jealous when Aang's identity as the Avatar was announced. Envious, Afiko betrayed his people by revealing the temple's location to the Fire Nation.

Fire Nation soldiers stormed the temple and slaughtered the other monks, but they were too late to catch Aang, who had run away from home shortly before the assault. Afiko was instrumental in engineering the genocide of his fellow Air Nomads, earning a place as Fire Lord Sozin's close adviser. He also seemed to have aided Sozin in attacking the Earth Kingdom, in that he is often shown blocking or dispersing earthbending attacks and attacking earthbenders. The traitorous monk died long before Aang's return and the subsequent undermining of all Afiko's work. In the end, despite his loyalty to the Fire Nation and his achievements, historical records indicate that Afiko met his demise in the war's fifth year, as Fire Lord Sozin had him killed for being a traitor.

entities.name: Aika
entities.description:
Aika grew up in Suki's village on Kyoshi Island during the late Hundred Year War. She experienced Team Avatar's visit and Zuko's raid on Kyoshi Island in 99 AG, helping to rebuild her home village afterward. When the leader of her Kyoshi Warrior team, Suki, asked her comrades whether they were willing to venture to the Earth Kingdom mainland to help others just as Avatar Aang did, Aika volunteered alongside Rie, Fume, and Mira.

After leaving their home per ship, one of the team's first destinations was Razor Reef in the southern Mo Ce Sea. There, the group sought a local martial arts master named Tidao, only to discover that the latter had long left the location. Yet they used the opportunity for a friendly sparring session with some local adventurers who were guarding an archaeologist, Wen, at Razor Reef. They then continued their journey to the mainland.

Once on the mainland, the group sought contacts to the Earth Kingdom Army. A fisherman claimed that they could find the military at Pebble Pond Village, offering to sell them ostrich horses as mounts for the journey. When he questioned the value of the group's Kyoshi Island money, Aika and Mira exchanged annoyed glances at his dismissive attitude. As Rie told him about their identity as Kyoshi Warriors, however, the fisherman was horrified due to hearing tales of the warriors' brutality, and gifted them the ostrich horses before running away. Unlike the rest of her comrades, Aika was unfazed by the man's reaction and instead more interested in a fish he had left behind.

Suki's group subsequently journeyed to Pebble Pond Village. On the way, Aika intensely prepared her weaponry, sharpening her sword so much that Suki commented on it. Aika countered that the Fire Nation had certainly improved their armor, feeling that they all had to prepare themselves for this.

entities.name: Aiko
entities.description:
Aiko was a born into a family with a proud martial tradition, as her ancestors had traditionally served as protectors for many generations. When the Hundred Year War erupted, however, the family's values began to shift; the clan increasingly regarded it as their duty to not just shield Jasmine Island at home, but to venture across the world to fight the Fire Nation's tyranny to prevent its aggression from ever reaching their home. As Aiko grew up, she saw her aunts and uncles, her parents, and finally her older siblings leave the island to fight in the Great War. The family's actions were not uncommon. Over the course of the Hundred Year War, it had become normal for Jasmine Island protectors to ultimately leave their home to fight as volunteers against the Fire Nation.

Eventually, Aiko was left as the oldest member of her family who still lived on Jasmine Island. Her relatives had charged her with protecting her little brother Chiyo. Though she resented being left behind, Aiko saw it as her duty to honor her oaths. and together worked out a plan to stop Yueya. This culminated in a battle where Aiko and her friends defeated the admiral, helping to save their home.

Aiko was a dutiful person who strove to protect her home and family at all costs, a duty which had been honored in her clan for generations.

Aiko was a fairly powerful firebender, capable for creating short bursts of superhot flames. As a result of her deep devotion to the protection of others, Aiko was skilled in taking hits intended for others.

entities.name: Ailani
entities.description:
Ailani was the daughter of Foggy Swamp Tribe immigrants. She grew up adapting traditional waterbending to grow crops in urban environments. She saw firsthand how these community gardens sustained public health when rapid development and industrialization complicated access to fresh produce or medicinal herbs. Ailani quickly earned the fondness of her fellow citizens throughout the city, and they encouraged her to vote for public office.

Ailani chose to run for mayor of Republic City, although the position historically was little more than ceremonial, while the United Republic Council, and later the president, held the real power over the capital. Ailani was determined to change the state of affairs throughout her campaign. She was the clear victor in the mayoral election, having successfully garnered support across the city by establishing herself as just another citizen, without wealth or long-standing political connections. In particular, she represented real changes, which were in opposition to the interests that President Raiko represented. Despite extensive popular support, she came to office without allies in the political establishment. As a result, she knew she had to maintain her popular support to survive, and sometimes adjusted her beliefs to maintain that support.

Ailani was an outspoken critic of corporate influence in government. She had a political rivalry with President Raiko, but she continued to butt heads with President Zhu Li Moon, whom Ailani thought was a technocratic shill too close to corporate interest. Ailani and Zhu Li typically clashed wherever public support was at stake. Ailani was always in favor of moves to keep her in line with the popular option, even when the president believed the choices in question would end up doing more harm than good. As presidential aide, Bolin took it upon himself to mend some of the fences between Ailani and Zhu Li, as the earthbender liked and respected both leaders and their ideals, and thought Republic City would be better off if they worked together. The mayor continued to constantly seek allies who share an anti-establishment view in politics, and she was interested in people even if she was the target of their confrontational energy. In the long run, Ailani wanted to run for president herself, though it was not her main focus just after Zhu Li's inauguration, as the next election was still years away.

Ailani's work to grow crops in the city was also built upon by others, with the initiatives being featured in the Four Nations Fair downtown.

entities.name: Air Acolyte woman
entities.description:
When Pema went into labor during the Equalist attack on Air Temple Island, the Air Acolyte woman quickly brought her inside to give birth. As Pema began to worry for her children, the woman reassured her that Jinora, Ikki, and Meelo were safe in the room next to them and that there was nothing about which she should worry. Thanks to the Air Acolyte woman, Rohan was born with no complications. She stood by quietly as Tenzin and his family gathered to see the baby.

As more Equalist airships approached, she fled the island along with Tenzin's family and another female Air Acolyte, guiding her own flying bison.

In 174 AG, she was among the last group of citizens in Republic City to be evacuated during the invasion of the United Republic of Nations. As they became stranded at Central City Station when the train lines were cut by the Earth Empire, she and the other evacuees sat and waited, bored as Pema attempted to entertain them with old airbender songs. When Prince Wu arrived with two badgermoles, she followed the creatures as they tunneled a way for the evacuees to escape underneath the city.

entities.name: Air Nomad boy
entities.description:
This boy, along with Aang, was among the children who went to the Eastern Air Temple to choose a flying bison.

He was also present when Aang taught his friends an airbending technique called the air scooter and was the first to try. He successfully created the scooter, but fell on his back when he attempted to ride it. After practicing for some time, he finally mastered the trick and even created a game with his friends; however, when Aang came to play with them, the boy told him he could not, saying that because Aang was the Avatar, his team would carry an unfair advantage. This exclusion from his friends prompted Aang to sadly walk away, while this boy asked the others who wanted Jinju on their team.

This boy was killed with the rest of the Air Nomads during the Air Nomad Genocide when the four air temples were attacked by the Fire Nation.

entities.name: Air Nomad pilgrim
entities.description:
In their youth, the pilgrim ventured to the Northern Air Temple with the intention of meeting Laghima, who had already become famous as a philosopher and poet. From the air temple, an Air Nomad used their glider to fly to a nearby mountain, where the guru had opted to live alone.

As the pilgrim touched down near the mountain's peak, their papers and writing utensils were scattered by the wind. The traveler panicked for a moment, but after collecting everything, they walked up the remaining way. There, an airbender met Laghima, who agreed to entertain their questions regarding wisdom as the pilgrim sat down nearby, writing down his words.

Eventually, however, the Air Nomad pilgrim paused writing, noticing that the guru was doing something. To their amazement, the pilgrim saw Laghima slowly levitate upward. As the guru told the visitor that "wisdom is formless, for only the wind remains when all else is gone", he flew into the sky. The resulting wind scattered their papers once more, yet this time a pilgrim remained fixated on the guru's achievement of having discovered the secret to weightlessness.

The story of how the pilgrim met Laghima and the answers he gave them were recorded in at least one edition of a book, Poems of Laghima, which remained widely read across the four nations for thousands of years.

entities.name: Aisha and Layla
entities.description:
Aisha and Layla were born into a family of medical professionals in Ba Sing Se. Their mother Jan was a doctor who ran the Hu Yuan Apothecary, with the building also acting as the family home. They had a younger brother named Xuan. In their early youth, Aisha and Layla would force Xuan to play dress-up with them. As a result, he became able to easily braid their hair. When their father left Ba Sing Se to journey to Taku in an effort to find a cure to a fever affecting refugees, he asked the three siblings to look out for each other. Tragically, their father never returned, as he was killed when his caravan was attacked by the Fire Nation military on the way to Taku.

At some point, Dr. Jan decided that Layla would take over Hu Yuan Apothecary in the future.

After the Fire Nation takeover of Ba Sing Se, Layla and Aisha hid in the ruins of Hu Yuan Apothecary with other Silver Fangs members. When Jin snuck into the ruins to find Dr. Jan and began being treated by Xuan, Layla walked in on them, initially mistaking Jin for an unwanted trespasser. When she realized that Jin and Xuan were acquainted, she began to tease Xuan for getting close to a girl, before getting a pair of her shoes for Jin to wear. When she learned that Xuan was going out to treat Gong-gong, she worried over his safety with the Fire Nation military prowling the city.

Layla seemed to enjoy teasing her younger brother. She worried about his safety when she learned he would be venturing out into Fire Nation-dominated territory, but still let him go, simply asking Jin to take care of him.

entities.name: Aiwei
entities.description:
In 171 AG, a few weeks after Harmonic Convergence, Aiwei personally greeted Avatar Korra and her companions, who had come to Zaofu in search of a new airbender. When Korra claimed that she and her three friends were the only ones to have arrived, Aiwei detected that she was lying. However, he did not call her out on that until after they met with Suyin, at which point Korra was forced to confess that they came with Republic City's Chief of Police, Lin Beifong.

The next day, Aiwei approached Lin as she was hassling two guards who were chitchatting. He noted that she was visibly stressed and offered the business card of an acupuncturist to help resolve her issues. Subsequently, Aiwei would meditate into the Spirit World and confer with his fellow Red Lotus member Zaheer, passing on Korra's current location at Zaofu to the criminal airbender after he had failed to find the Avatar in Republic City.

Aiwei later attended Opal's farewell dinner, seated next to Mako. Upon hearing him express disgust over his seat, Aiwei realized Mako was referring to being placed to him, and knew he was lying when the firebender suggested otherwise.

After Opal's departure for the Northern Air Temple, Aiwei secretly helped Zaheer and his gang infiltrate Zaofu through a secret passage in his house, yet the criminals failed to capture the Avatar. Once the gang had fled the city, Aiwei, maintaining his facade, gave Korra an antidote to the shirshu venom she was sedated with. As everyone concluded that Zaheer's gang could not have entered the city without inside help, Aiwei began questioning all the guards, even Suyin at Lin's request. Eventually, he declared that one guard was lying, Hong Li, and investigated his house with Team Avatar. There, they found evidence that Aiwei had planted to further incriminate the guard, including a message from Zaheer's gang for a rendezvous, and a logbook of guard movements and schedules. Though Team Avatar wanted to confront him, Aiwei declined, claiming that they should let the guard sweat.

entities.name: Akanah
entities.description:
Before the Dragon Flats Reform School was established, Akanah was a local teacher in the borough. When socialite Ruo Ling announced she wanted to spend money on a school for some of the city's worst students, Akanah agreed to build and govern the school with her. Akanah was aware that Ruo Ling simply wanted to use the project to bolster her celebrity status and dodge taxes. However, she realized that the plan would still give her access to Ruo's resources, with an opportunity to truly build an institution of value for Dragon Flats.

Akanah did not have enough funding from Ruo to spend on everything, and looked to spend what she could on renovating important aspects of the school building. She wanted to tear down the vining kudzu covering the school, but Ruo thought it made it look distinguished. Akanah used the funds to hire the best teachers she could find. Many of the teachers she found were ostracized or exiled from other academies, not out of incompetence, but because they protested poor conditions, or made an enemy of a wealthy parent. Akanah was able to quietly direct some of Ruo's money from vanity projects to real improvements to the school, such as using the funds she promised would spend on a large monument to the founder to go to hiring teachers for two new classrooms instead.

Eventually, part of the school's main building collapsed in the night. Although nobody was hurt, the incident left the school significantly damaged. It was not the sort of damage that Akanah could look to a few earthbenders to fix easily, since the school's plumbing and electrical wiring had also been dramatically compromised. The sort of construction expertise needed to fix the school were far beyond the headmistress's budget. Without more yuan, they could not go on running the school. Akanah knew that Ruo was not going to shell out more money than she absolutely had to, especially because the school was already behind in building the socialite's latest vanity project.

Many suspected that the collapse was a result of Terra Triad sabotage, as the situation left the school vulnerable to the exact sort of sabotage that Steely Ning could benefit from. A triad representative came to meet with the headmistress to offer their help and support, but Akanah knew that any money they offered would come with endless strings attached. She was in need of help from those that could help her find money, and who could help protect the school from further triad sabotage.

entities.name: Akataa
entities.description:
Akataa joined the protectors' ranks at an early point in their life and trained in accordance to the group's traditions. Over the course of the Hundred Year War, however, it had become normal for Jasmine Island protectors to ultimately leave their home to fight as volunteers against the Fire Nation. As a result, Akataa's older trainers also left, passing the responsibility of training and commanding the remaining, younger protectors to Akataa.

Over time, Akataa became one of the most experienced warriors on the island. and together worked out a plan to stop Yueya. This culminated in a battle where Akataa and their friends defeated the admiral, helping to save their home.

Akataa was a warm and friendly person, making it occasionally difficult for them to make hard and assertive choices as a leader. When they overcame their doubts, however, Akataa was an inspiring and diplomatic person who was well suited to bear both the burdens as well as triumphs of leadership.

Besides their substantial leadership talent, Akataa was also a highly skilled nonbending martial artist. Their fighting style was based on Jasmine Island's traditional combat techniques and consisted of dance- or flow-like strikes and parries using a staff with weighted baskets on either end.
entities.short_description: Akataa joined the protectors' ranks at an early point in their life and trained in accordance to the group's traditions. Over the course of the Hundred Year War, however, it had become normal for Jasmine Island…

entities.name: Akemi
entities.description:
Akemi grew up poor and unhoused on the streets of Tin Town, a community of outcasts and unhoused people. His business started with him smuggling fresh food in, as Tin Town had a market hungry for reliable nutrition. He then expanded his ring to include exotic and endangered offerings for Republic City's rich and eclectic. This included glowing lobster crab, cactus juice, and turtle duck shell.

Akemi now carefully monitors every agricultural pipeline coming in and out of Republic City. He has contacts with hundreds of vendors and is clever with his business. He has increasingly been locking horns with the Badgermole Triad, a ragtag group of street rats who see the badgermole tunnels as theirs. While the triad mostly tried to run automobile races in the tunnels, they increasingly began to believe that they must oust Akemi to survive. The Badgermole Triad's leader, Hibiki, tried to actively quash Akemi's smuggling ring. Akemi has grown increasingly annoyed at the triad's incursions, and hates that he is being outsmarted by children a quarter of his age.

Akemi was vengeful, whip-smart, and extravagant. He loved to make an example out of his enemies, and to look good doing so. He was frustrated to no end by the Badgermole Triad, as he hated being outmaneuvered by children, and he struggled to keep his composure whenever he was reminded of this fact. Akemi would go to extraordinary lengths to kneecap any potential disruptions to his enterprise.

Akemi was ambitious, and wants to ultimately own Republic City from the shadows. He believed that food is the way to achieve this, as his impoverished origins led him to believe that a good meal is the best way to control someone.

entities.name: Akuudan
entities.description:
Akuudan was originally from the Southern Water Tribe, He displayed the genetic quirk shared by several members of the royal family who were born with only one arm. As a highly capable fighter as well as a relative to the chief, Akuudan served in a high-profile, secretive military capacity for the Water Tribes that involved direct orders from Chief Oyaluk in the Northern capital of Agna Qel'a. At some point, he met and married Tayagum, a fellow warrior who hailed from the Orca Islands. They modified the traditional custom of giving a hand-carved necklace by both wearing betrothal armbands; Akuudan made Tayagum use all of his failed attempts at carving to use as stones on his own armband.

During the Platinum Affair, Akuudan and Tayagum served as expedition quartermasters, escorting the Water Tribe's payment of platinum ingots to General Nong under diplomatic pretenses. However, they were run down by Earth King Feishan's forces at Llamapaca's Crossing, along with the platinum they were guarding. The Water Tribe ambassadors could not get them released right away, and eventually, they stopped trying. The two warriors were disavowed by Oyaluk, and were only freed when Avatar Yangchen personally took it upon herself to negotiate amnesty for them. The husbands became firm allies of Yangchen, believing her to be a person who would help others without question. After being freed, they came to run a Water Tribe inn located in the shang city of Jonduri which could act as a safe house for the Avatar's allies.

In year 17 of the era of Yangchen, Akuudan was introduced to Kavik at the inn when his husband picked up Yangchen's spy that she would be using in Jonduri, and had to smash his face into a hard surface so that he would not be recognized by Harbormaster Lee. Akuudan was shocked and went to bone set, jamming the wooden rods into Kavik's nostrils to realign his breathing passages. After Kavik woke up, Akuudan and Tayagum had a meal prepared for Kavik so that he could regain his strength. The young man started openly speculating about their past, wondering if they were Northern guard or Thin Claws, and both were dismissive. They explained that they thought Yangchen was too trusting, to the astonishment of Kavik, who thought she had no connection to her Air Nomad ways. They explained their past and what Yangchen had done for them, and how they followed her out of a deal, rather than her being the bridge between humans and spirits. Kavik explained his plan to steal information from Jonduri and how he had done this before in Bin-Er, but Akuudan and Tayagum warned him of Zongdu Chaisee's overwhelming influence in Jonduri compared to the other shang cities. They told him that they had been playing the game much longer than him, but Kavik pointed out that one of them would have to break their assistant's nose tomorrow so that Lee would not suspect anything. Akuudan growled that he would do it, and slammed his fist on the table.

entities.name: Amak
entities.description:
Amak hailed from the Northern Water Tribe's capital Agna Qel'a, and was the brother of the renowned master healer Atuat. He became proficient as a hired killer, excelling in disguise, poisoning, and combat. Around 306 BG, he left his home and began working in the Earth Kingdom, During these conspiratorial conflicts, Amak found employment for a lesser prince in Ba Sing Se. This nobleman consequently jumped from the eleventh to the fourth place in the line of succession, as several members of the Earth Kingdom's royal family unexpectedly died. Amak was eventually hired by Jianzhu to train the false Avatar Yun in waterbending. although his poison training with Yun did not progress very far.

Serving as Yun's waterbending teacher, Amak and his charge spent quite some time together during their regular training sessions. Although Amak did not hold back during those sessions and regularly rendered Yun bloody and mussed at the end of them, he held Yun's respect and was lauded by him for being his favorite teacher next to Jianzhu. Amak's style placed more emphasis on the functionality of bending than its form.

Amak was present at Yun's attempt to make peace with the Fifth Nation, albeit in disguise as Tagaka had demanded that there be no waterbenders present. As such, Amak had donned himself in Earth Kingdom garb and even used spidersnake extract eye droplets, a very rare and expensive substance, to turn his eyes green. As the negotiations turned sour, however, Amak was recognized by Tagaka as a fellow Water Tribe member and promptly impaled with an icicle.

The training with the waterbending master was very useful to Yun in several cases. One such instance was when it helped him overcome the effects of the incense Jianzhu had drugged Kyoshi and him with, rendering them unable to move. Amak had also instructed Yun which parts of his body he could sacrifice in a fight and still be able to survive, knowledge that the earthbender put to use in his battle with Father Glowworm. After defeating and eating the spirit, Yun performed the checks Amak taught him to when he came into contact with potentially deadly toxins.

entities.name: Amihan
entities.description:
When several groups of foreigners landed on Lambak Island in 66 BG, Amihan happily fought against them as well as her former comrade Malaya, a local scout who opposed Ulo. In the process, the airbender also became a major enemy of Avatar Roku and Gyatso who were among the foreign intruders. Ultimately, the airbender was defeated by Malaya and Gyatso, but managed to escape and went into hiding.

Amihan later returned to become chief herself, waging a brutal but ultimately failed rebellion against the island's Fire Nation occupiers.

Amihan was born into the Lambak clan, However, Amihan was the last clan member known to possess the power over air. She eventually became a member of the clan's scouts, an elite group that was supposed to patrol the island to keep their community safe. At one point, Amihan also tamed a gorilla tarsier as companion and mount.

In her role as a scout, Amihan spent much time in isolation in the wilderness. This may have had a detrimental impact on her mental state and contributed to her sadistic tendencies. After Malaya also became a scout, she would occasionally work with the airbender, but the two never developed a good relationship due to their different personalities. At one point, Amihan warned Ulo that Malaya would never be reliable as a scout due to her curiosity, but the chief dismissed her warnings at the time.

entities.name: Amon
entities.description:
Claiming to be an innocent nonbender to whom the spirits granted the ability to remove a person's bending permanently, a power previously demonstrated only by the Avatar, Amon gained the confidence and support of many people with the same ideals. However, when the complete conquest of Republic City by the Equalists became imminent, Amon's true identity was exposed to the public by Avatar Korra. In actuality, he was a prodigious Northern Water Tribe bloodbender, son of the escaped crime boss, Yakone. Alongside his younger brother, the former councilman, Tarrlok, Amon was unknowingly shaped by Yakone to be a tool for his revenge against the Avatar. With his identity exposed and his followers deserting him, Amon fled the city with Tarrlok, but the latter ignited the fuel tank of their speedboat, killing them both.

Noatak was born in the Northern Water Tribe to Yakone and his wife, as the older brother of Tarrlok by three years. Growing up, he was a good-natured child who always looked out for his younger brother and wanted everyone to be treated fairly and equally.

When Noatak and Tarrlok both discovered they were waterbenders, Yakone trained them ruthlessly to develop their skills. While Noatak was a natural, Tarrlok struggled to progress as quickly and was often verbally abused by Yakone as a result. Noatak initially stood up for his brother, but stopped when Yakone ordered him to never talk back.

When Noatak was ten, Yakone took his sons on a supposed hunting trip far from their home, where he revealed his true identity as a Republic City criminal and explained to them the power of bloodbending. Claiming that their family had the strongest line of bloodbenders in history, he expressed his intent to make his sons bloodbenders of the highest caliber in order to exact his revenge against Avatar Aang for stripping him of his bending. Yakone trained the boys secretly during every full moon to use their bloodbending on animals, such as yaks and wolves, until they were able to bloodbend without a full moon. Noatak reveled in his newfound power, eventually mastering Yakone's unique psychic bloodbending technique by the time he was fourteen. As a prodigy, he carried the burden of all his father's expectations and demands. Over the years, he became cold and detached.

entities.name: Amrita
entities.description:
As a lieutenant of Jargala Omo, Amrita performed well as a mobster in the Creeping Crystal Triad. However, her real dream was always to leave her life of crime and break into the mover industry as a director. Amrita had been enamored with movers since the first one she saw, and she started looking for a way in, however she could get there.

When the triad gave a loan to Hongmei to start his own mover company, Amrita kept an eye on him as a source for more "fruitful" business endeavors. However, Hongmei did all he could to cut ties and keep Amrita out, which she took personally.

Despite her continued efforts, Amrita had not been able to push her way in to control any mover company. Those that would accept her overtures of aid were too small or unimportant to satisfy her ambitions, and those that were both successful and big were not willing to shackle themselves to the Creeping Crystal Triad and Amrita. Varrimovers International ended up being in just the right position for Amrita, as while it had major clout as a studio, it ended up having serious budgetary problems. Because of his prior history with the triad, and the desperate state of affairs at the mover company, Hongmei was Amrita's best chance to get everything she wanted and had promised to Jargala.

However, the triad's leader was tired of Amrita and her mover obsession. Jargala ordered Amrita to come back with something real and profitable within a month, or she would move the lieutenant to a different district and see if the Creeping Crystal Triad could muscle in on something more lucrative, like the waste disposal industry. After Jargala's ultimatum, Amrita met with Hongmei as the studio prepared for its new big, flashy mover, Sengo: Lady of the Winds. Amrita made it clear to him that he would be accepting Creeping Crystal yuan in exchange for a percentage of the mover's success, in order to satisfy Jargala. Amrita also demanded that she become an executive producer at Varrimovers International to satisfy her own ambitions. Hongmei refused these terms, but Amrita was ready for this. Knowing that the mover company was in a desperate position and that the scheduled premiere was the last shot at making Sengo a success. She therefore thought that she just had to put enough pressure on the executive to make him think that he wouldn't finish the mover in time, as she was absolutely sure he would break.

entities.name: Anada
entities.description:
Anada was born in the Fire Nation and was orphaned as a baby. She was initially raised by her grandmother, but when she could no longer take care of the child, Anada was given over to the Air Nomads and raised as one of their own. She lived in a time when the Air Nomads were more involved with the worldly affairs of the other four nations than they had been previously.

Anada became a great engineer, whose innovative designs created the Fire & Air Center of Learning, which celebrated the support of Air Nomad teachings by the Fire Nation nobility. This allowed her the chance to return to the nation where she was born and reunite with her beloved grandmother. However, shortly after arriving at the center, work halted when the Guiding Wind began to interfere and the Fire Nation military guard seized control of the site.

Anada being a nonbender made her a rarity in Air Nomad society, but she made up for it with her innovative mind. She became a brilliant engineer, renowned among the Air Nomads and the Fire Nation.

entities.name: Analay
entities.description:
Analay was one of the four benders that Yahshi scouted for Team Avatar. After showing off her unique shadowbending abilities and tickling Avatar Aang with shadows, the gang began to discuss whether or not to recruit her. However, just as they were about to announce their decision, Analay and the three other benders left to start their own group after deciding that they did not like being judged.

Analay is a shadowbender capable of fashioning her shadow into weapons such as whips to bind people from a distance. She is also capable of creating shadow constructs that she can control using her abilities, as she created a shadow wolf with which she travels.

entities.name: Andal
entities.description:
Born in the 60s AG she fought in several battles against the Fire Army.

By late 99 AG, Andal had set up headquarters in Pebble Pond Village, planning a military operation against a Fire Army outpost commanded by General Yuze. As she did so, the officer was surprised upon being informed that a squad of Kyoshi Warriors had come to Pebble Pond Village, requesting to join the Earth Kingdom Army. Andal gave the group an audience, where the officer mixed mild criticism of Kyoshi Island's non-intervention in the war up to this point with praise for the evident eagerness of the young warriors. The general particularly praised the squad's leader, Suki, and offered the group a place in the local army unit. The Kyoshi Warriors agreed to the offer.

On the next day, Andal readied the troops for the attack on Yuze's outpost. Expressing a conviction that victory would be theirs this time, the general was approached by Suki who requested that one young child soldier, Bun, be left at the camp during the upcoming operation. Hearing Suki's concerns about Bun lacking martial abilities, Andal countered that the boy was eager to fight but allowed him to decide for himself. The officer watched in satisfaction as Bun reprimanded Suki for trying to keep him out of a battle, lauding his fighting spirit as "very honorable". Afterward, Andal also demanded that the Kyoshi Warriors swap their traditional outfits and weaponry for standard army equipment, firmly stating that all soldiers had to fight in a uniform way as "one boulder is deadlier than a handful of pebbles". She told her young aide to provide the warriors with the items in question.

After all the soldiers, including Suki's squad, were ready, Andal personally led them toward the frontline. On the way, the advancing troops ran into a retreating contingent of wounded Earth Kingdom soldiers. The general praised these survivors before continuing the advance. Upon seeing that Suki's squad had stopped to provide additional medical aid to one heavily wounded soldier, Andal demanded that the Kyoshi Warriors close ranks. When Fume argued that this soldier needed more immediate aid and expressed doubts about the capacities of the field hospital at Pebble Pond Village, the general repeated her order more forcefully before moving on.

entities.name: Andal's aide
entities.description:
In 99 AG, the general's headquarters in Pebble Pond Village was visited by Suki's team of Kyoshi Warriors. As Andal gave the newcomers an audience, the aide provided her superior with tea and observed in silence. On the next day, the aide accompanied Andal as the general observed her troops assembling for an upcoming offensive. When Andal ordered the Kyoshi Warriors to take up Earth Kingdom Army equipment as they had joined her unit, the aide wrote down the general's order for the supply of new uniforms and weaponry to Suki's team.

The aide accompanied Andal to the frontline, and later noticed when Suki's team organized a unsanctioned raid against Yuze's outpost. She reported this to her superior, allowing Andal to exploit the Kyoshi Warriors' actions and achieve a victory over the Fire Army.

Andal's aide was quite stoic when on duty, taking her position very seriously.

entities.name: Aniki
entities.description:
Aniki was a child when she had to flee Grey Wolf Village in the Southern Water Tribe with her friend Teek and her baby brother Minaq strapped to her back. Her home was attacked by Fire Nation soldiers looking for waterbenders, and Minaq had shown a proficiency for bending at an early age. Aniki knew she could never return home, otherwise she would lose her brother and endanger her family, so the only thing she could do was keep moving.

The group left the Southern Water Tribe for the other nations, and eventually came to the Fire Nation itself. In 95 AC, when they came to the Fire Nation Capital, Teek told Aniki about a scroll that could expose the Fire Nation for what it was. Aniki thought it was a terrible idea to break into the Dragonbone Catacombs for this scroll, but decided to do it anyway to protect Teek, and to get revenge on the villains which had taken so much from her.

Aniki was always put together. She had broad shoulders and a warm smile.

Aniki was a proficient fighter and wielded a cable-backed bow.

entities.name: Animal control officer
entities.description:
The animal control officer captured Momo and three pygmy pumas and attempted to sell them to a butcher, who intended to use them as food. However, before this deal was finalized, Momo was able to open his cage, as the animal control officer had left the key in the lock, and escape along with the pygmy pumas, whom he freed as well. The officer and butcher soon returned to the cells to find them empty.

entities.name: Anri
entities.description:
Anri always dreamed of joining the circus, and joined the Flying Koi Carnival. She was always seen accompanied by her trained elephant rat, Lulu. Despite her proximity in age to Maolo, she joined the carnival as his apprentice, and used her earthbending skills to manipulate colorful clays during his waterbending performances.

She later graduated to being Maolo's partner-in-crime, but she hadn't been able to shake her image as a doting apprentice. Unlike Maolo, Anri was completely sold on Ringmaster Peng's mission to steal from rich customers to feed the poor in the Lower Ring, despite how ruthless he had become, and despite Maolo confiding his worries in her.

Anri was guided by her drive to make a name for herself.

Anri was both a skilled earthbender and a talented artist. Her signature earthbending technique whenever she got into a fight was being able to pin her foes with a column of earth.

entities.name: Anwat
entities.description:
Born as a sandbender, Anwat was among the tribespeople whose families had settled down in Liyuan. In his childhood, Anwat's grandmother taught him how to use various plants of the Si Wong Desert to create medicine. Once he was an adult, he joined Liyuan's ad hoc militia under Bai Yin Du who implored all militia members to use traditional earthbending instead of sandbending, believing the former to be superior.

When Kya came to Liyuan in the 130s AG to teach modern medical techniques to the locals, Anwat was among her pupils. During her first lesson, Anwat revealed his knowledge on traditional Si Wong healing and was encouraged by Kya to share his skills with the class. Over the following time, he attentively attended the waterbender's lessons.

One day, however, Kya's lessons were disrupted by an alarm, as raiders had arrived at Liyuan's eastern fields. Like other locals, Anwat rushed to the fields to take up arms against the attackers. He and the rest of the militia battled the attackers. Ultimately, the raiders successfully stole one of Liyuan's crucial water tanks and escaped on their sand-sailers. To pursue them and recapture the water, Bai Yin declared her intention to recruit more benders into the militia from the surrounding pro-Earth Kingdom clans. As one of the few militia members who had not been wounded in the clash, Anwat was selected to accompany this mission.

Anwat, Bai Yin, Tsetseg, and Kya subsequently moved to a traditional Si Wong meeting place with two sand-sailers. They managed to recruit a young sandbender, Dorzhi. The group continued their journey until evening, when they set up camp at a small stone overcrop. They were surprised by a rattle jackal which promptly attacked, biting Dorzhi and injecting its venom. The rest of the group managed to fend off the creature and they fled onto their sand-sailers, returning to the open desert. Kya attempted to heal Dorzhi but discovered that her waterbending was blocked. In response, Anwat suggested muri bean leaves as an alternate treatment, having learned from his grandmother that this plant could serve as an antidote for rattle jackal bites. While Dorzhi suffered growing pain and fever due to the venom, Anwat managed to gather some leaves from the surrounding desert. The group was able to create ad hoc medicine and successfully cared for the young sandbender, though the boy remained deeply weakened.

entities.name: Aoma
entities.description:
Aoma was born to the village captain of Yokoya and her husband around 312 BG. As a result, she was the ideal age to be the possible successor of Avatar Kuruk. When masters Jianzhu and Kelsang visited Yokoya in 305 BG, Aoma was among the Earth Kingdom children presented with the Avatar relics, but she failed the test, much to the annoyance of her mother.

Growing up, Aoma learned some basic earthbending techniques to help her parents with the farm work. Over time, she came to bully Kyoshi, an orphan who had become a servant at the Avatar mansion that had been built in Yokoya to house Yun, the earthbender identified as Kuruk's successor. Aoma was jealous of Kyoshi's friendship with Yun and the comparatively good life she had at the mansion, while she had to toil on her parents' fields. Her anger at Kyoshi only increased as Aoma developed a crush on Yun. Aoma had physically harmed Kyoshi with a rock on many occasions in her youth.

In 296 BG, Aoma and her friends Suzu and Jae held up Kyoshi outside the mansion as she was delivering a jar of pickled spicy kelp. Using her earthbending, Aoma took the jar from Kyoshi and floated it in the air while taunting the servant. Realizing that this was a chance to get into contact with Yun, Aoma declared that she would "help" Kyoshi by transporting the jar to the Avatar mansion. This plan fell through, however, when the group was stopped by Rangi, Yun's bodyguard and a friend of Kyoshi. Aoma first attempted to make excuses and use her charm in order to convince the firebender to let her through, but Rangi remained unswayed and ordered them to leave the grounds of the mansion. Angered, Aoma launched the jar far into their air in defiance of Kyoshi and Rangi before fleeing back to the village.

Aoma was a selfish and unsympathetic individual. She frequently harassed Kyoshi throughout her youth; on one occasion she did so out of jealousy due to the fact that Kyoshi was close to Yun. Aoma was also defiant, such as when she tossed the clay vessel that Kyoshi had carried high into the air when Rangi confronted her for bullying the servant girl. She was also entitled, dismissing the fact that at least seven local boys had developed a crush on her, as "those village boys have got nothing on Avatar Yun".

entities.name: Appa
entities.description:
When Appa was still a young calf who lived around the Eastern Air Temple, young airbenders were allowed to meet their future companions, who would bond with them for life. The herd's mother willingly directed her calves to meet the young monks. Aang came forward and offered an apple to Appa, and the two became best friends almost immediately afterward.

Just before the Air Nomad Genocide, Aang heard that the monks were going to separate him from Monk Gyatso and subsequently decided to run away, using Appa as his mode of departure. Appa did not know where he was going, only that he was leaving the air temples.

Aang flew Appa over the ocean, at which point they were caught in a vicious storm which pushed the two underwater by stirring up the wind and the waves until Aang lost consciousness. Faced with a life-or-death situation, the young Avatar entered the Avatar State and froze himself with Appa in an iceberg, the latter was stuck in hibernation along with Aang for one hundred years.

The pair were discovered by Katara and Sokka. After this, Appa became the group's main form of transportation in their quest to help Aang master all four elements throughout the world. He appeared in most of Sokka and Princess Yue's dates, tried to steal food with Momo in the Foggy Swamp, and became a beloved friend for all members of Team Avatar.

entities.name: Appa's mother
entities.description:
Appa's mother appeared to her son in a dream when he was feeling alone: She was flying along at the Eastern Air Temple with her five calves circling around her, heading toward Sister Iio and several Air Nomad children, among whom stood Avatar Aang. She nuzzled her children tenderly before willingly directing them to the platform where the Air Nomad boys were awaiting them.

entities.name: Aputi
entities.description:
A nonbending native of the small, independent Jasmine Island, Aputi came to disdain her homeland's traditional elites and authority figures such as the Jasmine Island protectors for a variety of reasons. As a result, she became part of the state's developing anarchist movement after the Hundred Year War. When some anarchists under Isonash banded together and formed a group dubbed the "Autumn Leaves", Aputi joined their ranks to help reform Jasmine Island's system on anarchist principles.

Meanwhile, new elections for the island's ruling council were announced, causing various political factions including the Autumn Leaves to bitterly feud in an attempt to gain the electorate's support. Amid this growing political crisis, White Lotus anarchist Xai Bau visited the island and secretly forged connections with islanders who were inclined to revolutionary change, including Isonash and a few others. As a rising star among the Autumn Leaves, Aputi was also allowed to meet Xai Bau, but she was disgusted by the latter's support for violent revolutionary acts.

Aputi was horrified as the Autumn Leaves increasingly moved toward Xai Bau's belief system even after the radical philosopher had left Jasmine Island. At the time, she also expressed her dislike for Xai Bau and told the protectors that the militant had departed the island weeks or months ago.

Aputi mainly saw any political activity as means to find and address problems, regarding an anarchist system as effective to achieve this goal. Thus, she had little sympathy for Xai Bau's extremism, deeming it to be unconstructive and just harmful to Jasmine Island's people. Regardless, she was a "true anarchist" and disliked traditional authority figures, viewing them as both prideful and incompetent.

entities.name: Ara
entities.description:
Ara was born into the Fifth Nation, and her early life was difficult due to her pirate parents being neglectful. After coming of age, she joined the ranks of the pirate nation, but she always felt uncomfortable unlike her parents who relished their criminal lifestyle. After the Fall of the Fifth Nation in 296 BG, Ara took the opportunity to abandon the remnants of the pirate coalition. As a refugee, she migrated to the small state of Jasmine Island, where she embraced the local culture and people. Resolving to build a new life for herself in accordance with her true wishes, she joined the local security forces, the "protectors".

Ara's new life truly started when she took part in a formal tea ceremony in an temple at Jasmine Island's coast, where she and four others —Joh, Fu Karaq, Revik, Yarru— had gathered with the protectors' leader Chidaw and an elderly talekeeper named Siarruk. In this ceremony, they officially joined the protectors. Later that day, the five new protectors opted to celebrate their new status together, and took a small fishing boat on a joyride. Eventually, they spotted a large warship approaching Jasmine Island, followed by a smaller vessel. To the group's shock, the large ship was manned by Fifth Nation corsairs under Tagaka, while the smaller ship was attacking them under the leadership of famous Fire National Hei-Ran. After making contact with the latter, Ara and her comrades hurried back to Jasmine Island to warn the locals of the upcoming pirate raid.

The group and the other protectors subsequently fended off a first landing led by a pirate scout force under Erchtei. Indeed, Ara and her comrades fought hard in the subsequent battle, even battling Tagaka herself and helping to defeat Erchtei, though both managed to escape. The group also discovered that another protector, Mirlon, had defected to the Fifth Nation and assisted the raid. They confronted the turncoat.

Ara and her comrades subsequently helped to decide what the Jasmine Islanders should do with the pirates captured during the failed raid. They also tried to mediate in an unexpected dispute between Hei-Ran and the rescued Tei Eesoni.

entities.name: Arik
entities.description:
At Fort Bosco, Arik led Korra and Asami onto an airship for transportation to Ba Sing Se and took them to the prison hold, where he secured a muzzled Korra wearing a straitjacket against the wall. He proceeded to tie Asami down to the floor as ordered, though was convinced by the engineer to do so to the railing instead, reasoning that as long as she was tied up, it would not make a difference. When Korra asked for some water, Arik denied her, stating clearly that they would do everything possible to keep her away from the elements that they could; she was not to be released before reaching the Earth Kingdom capital. He left to resume his position outside of their prison cell.

Five minutes later, Arik responded to Korra's distress call, who claimed something had happened to Asami. As he peeked through the door's peephole, he was knocked out from behind by Asami, who stole his keys and freed Korra.

After the ship had crash-landed in quadrant four of the Si Wong Desert, Arik crawled out of a hatch on the roof and snapped at Korra when the Avatar asked about the crew's well-being, blaming the two girls for knocking him out. However, upon witnessing a creature roaming around in the sand, he was quick to let go of his animosity and work together with their captives to fix their aircraft.

As their endeavor proved to have been a success with the start of the airship's engine, Arik excitedly threw his hands in the air, only to run for his life moments later when a sand shark emerged from the sand and destroyed the vessel. Realizing that all their supplies had also been destroyed and that they were an easy target for the creature, Arik panicked, though was ordered to get a hold of himself by his captain. When Asami suggested making a makeshift sand-sailer of the remaining metal, Arik and his fellow crewmen were instructed to gather all necessities.

entities.name: Arnook
entities.description:
Nominally, Arnook was also the formal chief of the Southern Water Tribe, but by the time of his reign, the North had already lost contact with the South Pole continent for decades. When Team Avatar reestablished these relations, Arnook sent waterbenders and resources to the South in order to help rebuilding the devastated Southern Water Tribe. By doing so, he not only saved the South, but also restored the union of the Water Tribes.

In his youth, Arnook trained to be a warrior, and he later became the chief of his tribe after his father passed away around 80 AG. He married the daughter of a tribal chieftain, and in 84 AG, they had a daughter together. However, their daughter was gravely ill, and desperate to save her life, Arnook prayed to the Moon Spirit. He took his infant daughter to the Spirit Oasis, where the mortal form of Tui, the Moon Spirit, dwelt along with the Ocean Spirit. He placed his daughter in the water under the full moon, and her hair turned white as she was revitalized by a measure of the spirit's own life force. In honor of Tui's intervention, his wife named their daughter Yue, for the moon.

At Yue's birth, Arnook had a spiritual vision of his daughter; he learned that when she grew to maturity, she would become the reincarnation of the Moon Spirit.

When Aang and the rest of Team Avatar arrived at the Northern Water Tribe's capital of Agna Qel'a, Arnook was happy to have the Avatar present as an ally. He introduced him to Master Pakku, his waterbending teacher. Katara hoped to learn from Pakku as well, but he refused, as it was not customary for women to be taught combative waterbending in the Northern Water Tribe. Later, Pakku refused to teach Aang after catching him teaching Katara waterbending. Katara begged for Arnook to have Pakku teach Aang again, to which Arnook said it was Pakku's decision alone whom to teach. However, this problem was resolved when Pakku agreed to teach Aang and Katara after he found out that Katara was the granddaughter of Kanna, the love of his life.

entities.name: Asami Sato
entities.description:
Asami was born at Republic City in 152 AG.

When Asami was six, her mother was killed during a break-in and robbery of their mansion by the Agni Kai Triad.

At the age of fourteen, Asami witnessed an important business deal between her father and Wonyong Keum. However, during the deal, Wonyong left, creating a resentment for him that would last Asami later into her life. By her teenage years, Asami began to actively involve herself in Future Industries as an inventor and businesswoman.

Sometime after Avatar Korra's arrival in Republic City, Asami accidentally ran into Mako with her moped when he suddenly crossed the street to catch a trolley. Feeling guilty over the accident, she apologized and, after recognizing him as the captain of the Fire Ferrets, invited him to dinner at Kwong's Cuisine. During dinner, she learned of the Fire Ferrets' financial situation and, as a big pro-bending fan, convinced her father to sponsor the team through Future Industries. Their relationship continued to grow afterward.
entities.short_description: Asami was born at Republic City in 152 AG.

entities.name: Ashō
entities.description:
Ashō wrote a travelogue about his many adventures. It told of meeting exotic people and fantastic spirits along the way, and was written in a humorous and bawdy manner.

In one case, Ashō wrote of being hired to investigate the case of an entire ship with a crew of over two hundred vanishing. He followed the clues to the Fire Islands' Sibuyan chain, where he encountered dense fog in the middle of the sea. He said that his ship sailed into a massive rock that nobody had seen, and that he washed ashore on a mountainous island.

Ashō claimed that he found a village nestled in a valley after wandering through the island for several days. He told of the locals treating him like a king, as they had never seen anyone from the outside world before. Ashō wrote that the island was home to all types of benders, and that they possessed legendary skills which were a thousand times stronger than anything he had seen before. He said the chief offered to teach him how to strengthen his own firebending, until he was caught sleeping with the chief's daughter. The account ended with Ashō barely escaping the island with his life.

Conversely, another author researched Ashō's stories and discovered that many of his claims were outright lies or otherwise only partially true. In particular, it was truth that benders from a Sibuyan chain island were capable of abnormally powerful feats, but that these were restricted to a specific cave. This writer subsequently penned a text titled A Correction in Response to the Many Dangerous Falsehoods Perpetuated by the Dishonest 'Traveler' Supposedly Named Ashō.
entities.short_description: Ashō wrote a travelogue about his many adventures. It told of meeting exotic people and fantastic spirits along the way, and was written in a humorous and bawdy manner.

entities.name: Ashoona
entities.description:
He served for a long time as zongdu, and increasingly suffered from health issues as he became elderly, including loss of concentration and repeated bouts of illness. Compared to other shang leaders, Ashoona was viewed as a "kindly" figure.

In the convocation between zongdus and world leaders in year 16 of the era of Yangchen, Ashoona played Sparrowbones with Iwashi, and was trounced so badly that he refused to touch a tile afterward. Increasingly suffering from illness, Yangchen believed that Ashoona was unlikely to be a player in the political game around the Unanimity crisis.

In the late year 17 of era of Yangchen, Ashoona arrived in Taku for the yearly convocation just after recovering from a lingering illness. When Yangchen arrived at the council hall, Ashoona was sitting in a place of prominence with Iwashi and Chaisee, and raised a hand in greeting to the Avatar.

When the day's meeting reached a midway lull, Ashoona began to forget details about certain clauses, with Chaisee snapping at him to make a "yea" or "nay" vote. Ashoona stated that he had lost track of the contract, and asked to start the contract over. When the merchants in the hall began to groan, Yangchen's companion, "Master Lio", began to speak unprompted to the zongdu, informing Ashoona that there was a three in ten chance of a tremendous risk, weighed against a seven in ten chance of a paltry reward, recounting the specific number of ingots Ashoona would lose or gain. Ashoona asked if Lio had kept a running tally, to which he stated that he had only kept a mental record of his calculations. Iwashi's accountants verified Lio's figures, and the Avatar's companion bowed deeply before Ashoona, apologizing for his impertinence, while stating that he did not want a business partner mistakenly enter a poor deal. He also made an intentional reference to Sparrowbones as he did so, intentionally attracting the attention of Iwashi. Ashoona offered his thanks to Lio, appreciating his honesty.

entities.name: Ashuna
entities.description:
Ashuna often made batches of blubbered seal jerky which she offered to members of her tribe, most of whom were not fond of the dish. In 92 AG, Ashuna offered Katara some jerky and the latter broke a tooth given how tough the meat was to chew.

In 102 AG, Nutha brought up the subject of Auntie Ashuna's cuisine while reminiscing about childhood stories with Niyok and Katara, prompting the latter to recall how she broke her tooth trying to eat her blubbered seal jerky.

When Katara and Sokka arrived in Harbor City, Ashuna was spotted in the crowd by the siblings as she was selling her seal jerky from a cart. As they joyously reunited, she told them how her business had been steady and that she was now living with several other elderly people in a grand building after her hut had been torn down as part of the village's modernization process. She enthusiastically offered Sokka some of her seal jerky, noting that it had been ages since he had tasted her secret recipe, before shouting out to the rest of the tribe and announce the return of the siblings.

entities.name: Atka
entities.description:
Originally an Earth Kingdom healer, Atka was mentally broken when her entire home village was wiped out by the Northern Pox. Consumed with endless hatred for the people of the Northern Water Tribe capital Agna Qel'a who had refused to provide medical aid to Atka's people, she became determined to single-handedly wipe out the city. To do so, she became the assassin of Minister Huaji of Omashu, thereby acquiring special ingredients to craft a spirit-infused poison. After years of murderous tests in the Northern Water Tribe's hinterlands, Atka unleashed her poison in Agna Qel'a in 63 BG, killing many people including Chief Tiguaa. However, her rampage was stopped by Avatar Roku's team.

Originally born at a poor village in the Earth Kingdom under a different name, while staying very close to her family. Atka also had a boyfriend whom she wished to marry. Besides her medical activities, she trained her earthbending to some degree.

Her life was upended when traders accidentally infected her village with the Northern Pox, an extremely deadly disease. Even though Atka proved to be immune to the illness, the rest of the villagers began to waste away. The healer knew that a remedy for this pox existed, horded by the Northern Water Tribe which controlled the ingredients' supply. The healer ventured to the tribe's capital of Agna Qel'a and pleaded her case before Chief Tiguaa and his council. The Northerners were unmoved, however, as many settlements suffered under the pox and the remedy was valuable. As Atka could not offer enough money for even a few doses of the medicine, she was turned away.

Atka returned to her village and continued to care for her people, but without the remedy she was powerless to stop the pox's progression. Ultimately, her entire family, her boyfriend, her neighbors, and everyone she knew died a slow and gruesome death. In accordance with her village's customs, she individually buried every single villager without earthbending, instead using her bare hands to dig the graves and lay the dead to rest. These experiences resulted in a mental break and a fundamental personality change within Atka; she became consumed by the singular desire to take revenge on Agna Qel'a, the city which had condemned her people to death out of greed.

entities.name: Atuat
entities.description:
Atuat was born to a Northern Water Tribe family in Agna Qel'a, and was the sister of Amak, a waterbending master who later became an assassin for hire. During the fall of the Fifth Nation in 296 BG, her brother was killed by the pirate queen Tagaka. Atuat knew that her brother would not die a peaceful death, and considered his demise to be far more honorable than what he was doing before.

Weeks later, the firebending master Hei-Ran arrived at Agna Qel'a with her daughter Rangi after being grievously poisoned by Jianzhu. Atuat considered Hei-Ran to be nearly dead on arrival, and claimed to have "picked the shroud of Death itself" to heal the firebender.

After a year, Hei-Ran had recovered enough to return to the Fire Nation for the Festival of Szeto, with Atuat accompanying her as both a personal healer and honored guest. During a garden party at the royal palace, Hei-Ran introduced her to Avatar Kyoshi, who voiced her condolences for Amak's death. When Jinpa displayed a feat of airbending to lift himself off the ground without creating blasts of wind, he asked to lift a volunteer at the party, and Atuat excitedly accepted the offer.

When Kyoshi made a great diplomatic faux pas at the party, Hei-Ran partially blamed herself for being distracted by Atuat's antics. While Rangi and Hei-Ran tried to smooth over the situation with Fire Lord Zoryu, Atuat finished a skewer of meat, voicing that she had not offended anyone, and that she found everyone else's behavior imprudent and shocking. Atuat listened intently to Fire Lord Zoryu's explanation of the rivalry between him and his half-brother Chaejin, and cautioned him from talking about conflict as if it was an inevitability. At the end of the conversation, Atuat caught Hei-Ran as she started to wobble. The former headmistress declared that she needed to stay with the adolescents, but Atuat adopted a harsh tone due to Hei-Ran backtalking her on a health related matter.

entities.name: Aupilaarjuk
entities.description:
As courier, Aupilaarjuk was responsible for carrying messages between the North and the South. Her job carried risks, as she often carried messages that others did not want to arrive at their destination, and because the distance between the two tribes was so vast, with much opportunity for things to go wrong. She also occasionally worked as a courier for the Order of the White Lotus, but only spoke of that relationship to a trusted few individuals. Whenever the White Lotus hired her to make a delivery, it was because that delivery was of extreme importance, and would result in disaster if it fell into the wrong hands.

After the Camellia-Peony War, she received a job of utmost importance, and she ferried messages between the lesser politicians of the two tribes working to support the south and defend against pirates.

entities.name: Aye-aye spirit
entities.description:
After being banished by the Chou family into the Spirit Wilds, Wan stumbled upon the Spirit Oasis which the aye-aye spirit guarded and noticed several trees bearing fruit on the island. Hungry and in need of a place to rest, Wan made his way toward the oasis, though quickly found his path blocked by the spirit, who appeared out of nowhere and denied him access. Wan attempted to reason with the spirit, but to no avail and resolved to use firebending in an attempt to ward him off. This act only enraged the aye-aye spirit, who teleported to grab Wan from behind and threw him aside, reasserting his decision before returning to his post.

Shortly after, the aye-aye spirit began granting access to a parade of spirits and caught Wan disguised as a bush spirit, recognizing his distinct human scent. He ordered Wan to leave once more, refusing to give him directions to the other lion turtle cities. The aye-aye spirit witnessed Wan leave and later saw him fend off a group of hunters in an attempt to protect a captured cat deer. After Wan had been cornered, the spirit possessed one of the hunters, prompting the other to flee in fear. He carried Wan to the oasis, where the spirit waters healed him of his injuries. When the other spirits agreed with Wan's decision to stay in the wilds to learn the ways of the spirits, the aye-aye spirit initially disagreed, but eventually relented.

Over the next year or two, the aye-aye spirit developed a close friendship with Wan and was present to watch Wan master his firebending skills by learning the Dancing Dragon from a white dragon. Together, the two of them protected the oasis from trespassers until Wan's departure to find the other lion turtle cities. Before Wan left, the aye-aye spirit told the young man that he was proud to call him his friend.

About a year later, a gathering of spirits led by the aye-aye spirit came into conflict with Jaya and other citizens from Wan's old city. When Wan intervened, the aye-aye spirit was happy to see him, believing he had arrived just in time to drive away the settlers. Though Wan attempted to mediate the situation, his efforts proved to be futile. The negative energy generated by the standstill allowed Vaatu to turn the aye-aye spirit and the other spirits dark. As the firebenders provoked the dark spirits with a single fireball, the aye-aye spirit ordered his fellow spirits to attack, but both sides were kept at bay by the efforts of Wan and Raava. The aye-aye spirit briefly reverted to normal when Wan merged with Raava, creating a positive-energetic barrier of all four elements between the two groups. However, as Wan was being carried away after caving under the strain Raava's presence put on them, the aye-aye spirit again succumbed to Vaatu's dark energy and attacked, slaughtering all the settlers with his fellow spirits.
