entities.name: Ayunerak
entities.description:
Ayunerak was originally from the Northern Water Tribe. At some point, she joined the Order of the White Lotus, and became a very high-ranking member of the Order. She read White Lotus reports from the Western Air Temple during the childhood of Avatar Yangchen, and learned about the young Avatar's extremely intense memories of her past lives.

Long before the beginning of the shang system, Ayunerak established a shelter and food kitchen within the Inner Corridor of Bin-Er - the city's future International Quarter - that provided meals to the unemployed workers of the city. She also became acquainted with Tayagum, who was once one of Chief Oyaluk's most trusted warriors. She later watched Bin-Er double in size due to mass migration to the shang cities, continuing to maintain the customs the customs of Water Tribe hospitality during that time.

By year 17 of the era of Yangchen, Ayunerak had gotten to know Kavik, a young man who lived in the Water Tribe Quarter, with the two of them having previously talked about Kavik's breakup with an individual named Meihua. Ayunerak also read reports about Yangchen's actions as a fully-realized Avatar; she came to see the younger woman as amateurish, believing she did too many things herself during an operation and expected results too quickly.

One day, Ayunerak opened the door to Kavik, noticing a dopey grin on his face. Much to her surprise, Kavik gave her a large amount of money as a donation to her shelter, before telling her to visit her 'cousins' in Port Tuugaq. He gave her a nuzzle on the cheek before running back around the corner. Ayunerak did go to Port Tuugaq soon after receiving Kavik's money, as she had heard reports from the White Lotus of bright lights and loud noises along the tundra around the city.

entities.name: Azula
entities.description:
Azula found Aang and Katara, along with Zuko and Iroh during the Fire Nation's occupation of the city Omashu. She was about to capture them all, by having Mai attack them with her daggers. However, before her plan could be executed, Aang used his airbending to whiff up a cloak of smoke, enabling them all to escape.

Azula encountered Aang again, ambushing the Avatar when he was trying to free King Bumi. The Fire Nation princess tried to thwart Aang's efforts by hurling fire at him. However, the Avatar eluded her once again, when he managed to cut the rope holding Bumi's cell, making his escape with the king down the cart ramps. She pursued him, but soon stopped once he neared the bottom, unable to keep up with the agile airbender.

When Team Avatar arrived at Ba Sing Se after Aang's training, they discovered a giant drill attempting to break through the city's walls. They infiltrated the mechanism, where, once inside, Katara and Aang severed the pillars of the drill with waterbending, before going to the top of the drill to fight Azula. As the battle ensued, Azula remarked that Aang's skills had improved since they last encountered one another. Zuko soon appeared, prompting the princess to ask her brother for his opinion and the two siblings proceeded to fight Katara and Aang. Azula remained the dominant fighter until Zuko threatened to burn Katara and suffocate her in a ring of fire, Aang went into the Avatar State and knocked Zuko unconscious. After Azula was weakened by Aang and Katara, she fired a bolt of lightning at Katara, thus knocking her down. Aang went into the Avatar State again and knocked Azula out before she could hurt Katara. Aang and Katara escaped on Appa.

Aang and Katara were seen fighting Azula and Zuko. An angered Aang rose from his crystal prison in the Avatar State before Azula struck him in the back with lightning, thus rendering him unconscious.
entities.short_description: A firebending prodigy, Azula was manipulative and obsessed with power. She was a skilled strategist who orchestrated the coup of the Earth Kingdom capital, Ba Sing Se, and halted the invasion on the Day of Black Sun.

entities.name: Azula's ship captain
entities.description:
The captain was fairly popular among the Imperial Firebenders serving under his command, as he cared about their welfare.

When Zuko and Iroh were deemed traitors by Fire Lord Ozai, he traveled with the princess to capture them. Early in their search, Azula informed the captain and other assembled troops that despite any potential hesitancy they might have taking up arms against a member of the royal family, she would not hesitate to punish those who disobeyed orders. When she was finished, the captain ran up to the Crown Princess and informed her that the ship could not enter the port due to the tides. Azula coldly asked if the tides commanded the ship, to which he voiced confusion. Azula threatened to have him thrown overboard in the event that her orders were not followed, making it clear that she was the one in charge, despite the fact that he was the formal commander of the ship. The captain agreed to enter the vessel at the port, despite the difficulties.

When Azula successfully tricked Zuko and Iroh into the charade that her father wanted them to return to the Fire Nation, the captain accidentally revealed that it was a sham, mistakenly referring to the banished members of the Fire Nation Royal Family as "prisoners". Upon hearing themselves referred to as prisoners, Zuko and Iroh immediately discovered the ruse and Azula shot the captain a deadly glare. Zuko easily pushed him out of his way and off the ship so he could reach and fight Azula.

After Zuko and Iroh had escaped, the captain was punished by Azula for his failures. He was banished to the Fire Nation colonies. His former subordinates were displeased about this harsh treatment, though one Imperial Firebender argued that they could all be happy that the captain had at least not been executed for ruining Azula's plans.

entities.name: Azulon
entities.description:
However, after ordering Ozai to kill Zuko due to the former's attempt to usurp Iroh's birthright, Azulon himself was murdered after his daughter-in-law, Princess Ursa, made a deal with Ozai to provide the latter with a poisonous substance, which was used to end Azulon's life. Although seen as uncaring and cruel, even toward his own people, he is remembered as one of the Fire Nation's strongest and most effective leaders.

Born shortly after the beginning of the Hundred Year War, Azulon was the firstborn of Fire Lord Sozin. he received tutelage in the bending art under his father's supervision from a young age. In his time, Azulon was considered to be one of the best firebenders in the world, and no one would dare challenge him. Over time, he grew into a ruthless and frightening man who demanded perfection.

Just like his father, Azulon attempted to find the missing Avatar by sending out search parties, though these missions failed.

Azulon led the Fire Nation to victory in many glorious military campaigns. His military achievements included the conquest of the Hu Xin Provinces and the Battle of Garsai. He assumed the title of Fire Lord at age twenty, following the death of his father, and continued to lead his country in the war. He continued most of Sozin's policies, ruling the Fire Nation autocratically and through fear. In general, he was regarded as a very capable leader by his subjects.

entities.name: Ba Sing Se airship captain
entities.description:
At Fort Bosco, the airship captain oversaw his crew load Korra and Asami onto the airship. Upon Korra's plea to free her so she could protect the queen against the Red Lotus, knowledge she had gathered after talking to Zaheer in the Spirit World, he dismissed her as insane herself, as she was the one speaking of "terrorists" and the "Spirit World". The moment he entered the ship's cargo bay, the vessel took off and he made his way over to the cockpit, where he oversaw his co-pilot navigating the ship over the Si Wong Desert.

As they were flying over the fourth quadrant of the desert, the captain was startled when their escaped prisoners suddenly burst into the cockpit. Upon noticing the damage Korra had accidentally inflicted upon the ship by airbending the co-captain against the controls and breaking them, he sent out a distress signal to Ba Sing Se, alerting them of the Avatar's escape and their imminent crash-landing's location. However, he was knocked unconscious against the control panel himself when Korra flung his co-captain against his back, breaking the radio in the process.

Emerging from a hatch on the ship's roof, the captain overheard Kong starting to panic due to their predicament of being stranded in the desert and told everyone that rescue was on its way as he had radioed Ba Sing Se before they went down. When Asami proposed to work together to repair the airship, the captain denied the request, stating that the ship nor the girls were going anywhere, as the women were still in their custody and they had a duty to transport them to the Earth Queen. Even when Korra warned him about the dangers of fighting the Avatar, he would not budge in respect of the orders he had been given. When Asami believed she saw a sand dune moving, the captain dismissed it as a typical mirage one would see in the desert. However, they soon realized there was something lurking beneath the sand and, under the pressure of his crew, the captain relented and gave the order to repair the ship.

entities.name: Ba Sing Se airship co-pilot
entities.description:
At Fort Bosco, the co-pilot boarded the airship along with Arik and Kong, who brought their prisoners aboard. He made his way over to the cockpit and as soon as their captain had ventured inside as well, he started the ship's engines and took off.

As he was navigating the ship over the Si Wong Desert, the co-pilot was started when Korra and Asami burst into the cockpit. He instantly charged the escaped prisoners, though was thrown back into the controls by an airbending blast, short-circuiting them in the process. He recovered and tried again, only to be blown back a second time, now into his captain, resulting in a broken radio.

After the airship crash-landed in a sand dune in quadrant four of the Si Wong Desert, the co-pilot crawled out of a hatch atop the ship, joining Kong and Arik as well as Korra and Asami. Although he initially sported a distant attitude toward the girls, he was quick to let go of his animosity upon witnessing a creature roaming around in the sand and work together with their captives to fix their aircraft.

After having dug out the ship and having made the necessary repairs, the co-pilot stood with the rest outside of the vessel while Kong tested out the engine. Although the test was a success, the co-pilot was forced to flee for his life lest he would be crushed by falling debris when a sand shark emerged from the sand and destroyed the ship, dragging most of it, supplies and all, underneath the desert's surface. As Asami suggested building a makeshift sand-sailer with the remaining scraps of metal, the co-pilot and his crewmates were ordered by the captain to gather up the material.

entities.name: Ba Sing Se University student
entities.description:
During his studies at Ba Sing Se University, he ran into Team Avatar. The group questioned him about the location of Appa, who had recently been stolen by the sandbenders, to which he replied that he had never seen any sandbenders or nomads in the city. However, he suggested the gang speak with Professor Zei, whom Team Avatar had ironically met some time before.

The conversation took an awkward turn when Sokka questioned him about the Hundred Year War with the Fire Nation. Clearly uncomfortable with the topic, and with some influence from Joo Dee, he alleged not to know about it because his major was not political science. The young man quickly gathered his belongings and left, claiming to be late for class, leaving Team Avatar with unanswered questions.

The student seemed to be very cooperative and casual, as well as sociable, as when Team Avatar asked about Appa and the Si Wong tribes, the young man was very friendly. However, like many of the residents of the city, he felt very uncomfortable talking about the War.

entities.name: Baatar
entities.description:
Suyin hired Baatar as an architect in the creation of the city of Zaofu. Sometime later, the two married and had five children: the eldest, Baatar Jr., became an engineer and began assisting Baatar in developing his many public projects, Huan became an artist, Wei and Wing invented the game power disc, and Opal became their family's first airbender following Harmonic Convergence.

While Suyin hosted a dinner for Avatar Korra and her friends, Baatar passed by the dining hall and informed his wife that he would have to eat in his office because he had a major breakthrough regarding the remodeling of a tram station. Suyin allowed him to continue his work, to which Baatar responded by calling her the best.

The next day, Baatar, along with Huan, Wei, and Wing, were witness to his wife fighting against his sister-in-law, Lin. Their fight soon ended when Opal intervened. Later that evening, Baatar and Suyin each gave permission for Opal to travel to the Northern Air Temple and begin her airbending training under Tenzin.

At Opal's farewell dinner, Baatar watched in admiration as Suyin praised their daughter and raised his glass in a toast to her. He later watched as she left for the Northern Air Temple in an airship.

entities.name: Baatar Jr.
entities.description:
While Suyin hosted a dinner for Avatar Korra and her friends, Baatar Jr. and his father passed by the dining hall, where the latter informed the matriarch that they would have to eat in his office as they had a major breakthrough regarding the remodeling of a tram station. After the two left, Suyin proudly remarked that Baatar Jr. was an engineer who was responsible for handling all of his father's projects.

He later attended Opal's farewell dinner and subsequently accompanied the rest of the dining group to the rooftop, where they watched Opal depart for the Northern Air Temple for airbending training.

After the insurrection of the Red Lotus, Baatar Jr. made plans with Kuvira behind Suyin's back to leave Zaofu and stabilize the situation in Ba Sing Se and the rest of the Earth Kingdom. At some point, he entered a romantic relationship with Kuvira, which progressed to the point that he proposed to her, which she accepted.

By 174 AG, he traveled the Earth Kingdom by train. When Bolin reported to him that two more states had agreed to join their alliance, he happily took the reports from him and relayed the message to Kuvira, stating that they had reached ninety percent of their goal. He was about to celebrate their achievement with Varrick, Zhu Li, and Bolin by drinking some tea, though when Kuvira stated that she refused to celebrate until the Earth Kingdom was reunited completely, he digressed and put his cup back down. However, the contents ended up being spilled on his clothing when their train suddenly halted due to an earthen obstruction on the tracks caused by bandits.

entities.name: Baboon spirit
entities.description:
The baboon spirit was meditating in the Spirit World when he was approached for help by Aang, who sought the location of the Moon and Ocean Spirits. The spirit brusquely told the Avatar to leave, but Aang persisted in asking him for help, causing the baboon spirit to become more and more agitated as he tried to continue his meditation. With Aang failing to heed his request, the spirit told him to follow a Spirit World firefly as it flew past, sighing in relief when the Avatar departed.

The baboon spirit was visited again by Aang when he returned from his encounter with Koh, the Face Stealer. After Hei Bai helped the Avatar to return to the mortal world, the baboon spirit expressed his pleasure at Aang's departure, much to the annoyance of Hei Bai, who transformed into his monstrous form and struck the baboon spirit with a huge energy blast, sending him flying.

The baboon spirit directed Aang to Avatar Kuruk on Aang's second adventure through the Spirit World, although Aang did not keep the memory of their encounter.

The baboon spirit prefers tranquility to aid him in his meditation, and can become very irritable if someone disrupts this serenity. He will attempt to ignore anyone that disturbs him, and will only help them if it becomes necessary to return to his meditation. He speaks with a distinct accent.

entities.name: Bai
entities.description:
Unlike most Fire Nation citizens, Bai was well informed about the war crimes which his country had committed during the Hundred Year War. He consequently took it upon himself to ensure that this information remained secret for others during the late rule of Fire Lord Azulon and early reign of Fire Lord Ozai. Bai fiercely guarded all artifacts and documents at the High Temple which could contradict the Fire Nation's official propaganda.

In the night before Ozai's coronation as Fire Lord, Bai captured intruders who had snuck into the Dragonbone Catacombs. This group, consisting of Teek, Aniki, Wenli, Xaipan, Sunlin, and Yinzin, had sought to steal a scroll from Sozin's time containing secret information. Even though Bai had them imprisoned, the six broke out and escaped with the scroll thanks to aid by Bai's fellow Fire Sage, Niuan. Upon learning of this, Bai chased after them.

Bai was completely loyal to the Fire Lords despite knowing the true motives of the Fire Nation's imperialistic war. Though not proud of the crimes committed by his country, such as the Air Nomad Genocide, Bai believed that the Fire Nation's people as well as culture were naturally stronger than those of the other nations. According to this world view, wars of conquest were a natural consequence. The Fire Sage considered this logic to be mere pragmatism, independent of any moral questions.

However, Bai was well aware that other Fire Nation citizens would not accept his logic so readily. As a result, he believed that propaganda and lies were neccessary to ensure a stable country, and that normal citizens had be be "protected" from the truth. Instead of pondering the war's morality, the commoners should focus on how to best serve their nation. To ensure his country's and government's survival, Bai was even willing to destroy the priceless artifacts under his watch or murder anyone who was not be trusted with the information they contained.

entities.name: Bai Yin Du
entities.description:
Bai Yin was raised in Liyuan by her father, who was born under Fire Nation occupation of the Earth Kingdom during the Hundred Year War. By the time of her youth, the area around her hometown had long suffered under a great drought. Having sustained burn scars across his arms during the old Fire Nation rule, her father's health steadily deteriorated as he grew older. Witnessing his struggles, Bai Yin dedicated herself to strengthening her community so it could endure the drought just as it had survived the war.

When Kya arrived in Liyuan as a voluntary aid worker, Bai Yin welcomed the Avatar's daughter and escorted her to her quarters. Later that week, she invited Kya to dinner, where she introduced her to her father and explained the hardships her community had endured over the decades. Determined to prevent Liyuan from succumbing to the drought, Bai Yin shared her resolve to secure its future.

The next day, Bai Yin and her soldiers defended Liyuan against a raid by sandbending bandits. Although they drove off the attackers, they failed to prevent them from escaping with one of the village's water casks. Frustrated by the outcome, Bai Yin blamed the failure on her soldiers' reliance on sandbending. In response, Tsetseg agreed to help her recruit more benders from across the Si Wong Desert. Bai Yin also enlisted Kya because of her healing abilities. When the waterbender questioned why they could not simply borrow another cask from the military outpost, Bai Yin explained that there was never enough water in the desert and that obtaining more would inevitably deprive another community of its share.

Guided by Anwat and Tsetseg aboard their sand-sailers, Bai Yin and Kya traveled to a hamlet settled by a wayfinding stone. The elder firmly denied that any benders lived there, but Bai Yin was convinced he was lying. Furious, she demanded that he reveal their whereabouts. A young sandbender named Dorzhi ultimately stepped forward and surrendered himself without protest. Bai Yin thanked him for his patronage and assured him that his clan would receive water after one month of his service.

entities.name: Baku
entities.description:
Baku was born into the isolationist Lambak clan that lived on a remote Fire Island, traditionally independent of the four nations. Under the tenure of Chief Ulo, he served as the clan's blacksmith. He took great pride in his work, but was often frustrated at the uninterested attitude of the other clan members. He was also one of the few Lambak people who was critical of Ulo, though he did not openly voice his views due to fearing possible repercussions. At some point, he married and had at least one son, Kamao, who developed a boisterous and sexist attitude by his teenage years.

When one young clan scout, Malaya, requested Baku to teach her how to craft weapons, the older man was happy to oblige. The two worked well together, though Baku repeatedly encouraged her to also spend time with his son, In the course of several lessons, Malaya increased her smithing skills until she and Baku created a fine dagger together. When they finished their project one day in 66 AG, the blacksmith used to occasion to praise the scout's abilities and wide-ranging interests before sending her on her way.

After the Lambak clan village was attacked and largely destroyed by rampaging Western Kingdom Trading Company guards, Baku took charge of rescue and aid efforts due to Ulo's absence from the settlement. In this regard, he was helped by Malaya and Gyatso who had previously chased after the guards. The blacksmith's home had also been destroyed during the attack, and to his horror, his dead wife was eventually discovered under the house's rubble.

As fighting continued on the island, Ulo and Malaya were eventually slain, adding more losses to the already suffering clan. With no one else stepping up, Baku effectively assumed the leadership of the Lambak survivors. Later on, disputes erupted on what to do with the Western Kingdom Trading Company guards who had been captured after their rampage. An Air Nomad expedition, supported by Gyatso, advocated that the company members should be turned over to Queen Guo Xun of Omashu, their sovereign. Baku initially opposed the idea, but agreed not to kill the captives. He ultimately relented and handed the guards over to be brought back to the Earth Kingdom.

entities.name: Baljin
entities.description:
Born among the Air Nomads, Baljin initially grew up and trained airbending at the Northern Air Temple. From an early point, he realized that he felt uncomfortable in a highly moralistic as well as monastic community, often sneaking out of the air temple to visit other locations across the world. Eventually Baljin concluded that he had no future at the Northern Air Temple, and resolved to permanently leave. An opportunity to do so arose when the young airbender met members of the Guiding Wind, a renegade order and revolutionary movement that espoused a strong commitment to freedom. He thus ran away and joined the group, spending quite some time with them and going on various missions.

Ultimately, Baljin opted to settle down on the independent Jasmine Island, feeling a strong connection to the location and hoping to pursue "his own independent development" without the Guiding Wind, though he remained loyal to the movement's cause. On Jasmine Island, he generally strove to make his life interesting, "mess[ed] about and [did] what he want[ed]", though also helped the locals using his various skills including his airbending. He eventually joined the local security forces, the protectors, seeing it as a way to both assist others as well as live a free life.

At the time of Baljin joining the protectors, the latter were in crisis due to the machinations of Magistrate Emerald, the civilian representative of the Earth Kingdom on Jasmine Island. Emerald was organizing a creeping coup, undermining the island's old power structures to eventually annex it into the Earth Kingdom, though he did so slowly and covertly. The protectors were among the organizations targeted by Emerald, and he managed to gradually dismantle them by replacing them with Earth Kingdom soldiers who could allegedly better defend the islanders. Ultimately, Baljin became one of the few loyalists who remained protectors even as their organization crumbled.

The situation changed when Emerald imprisoned two Guiding Wind revolutionaries, namely Fengying and Sakuru. This drew the attention of the Guiding Wind's leaders, Khandro and Zeisan, who traveled to Jasmine Island to help their followers. Baljin took a special interest in their arrival due to his existing connections to the Guiding Wind, as he had not yet met the movement's leaders and was thus eager to learn from them during their time on Jasmine Island.

entities.name: Ban Buhai
entities.description:
Ban Buhai was a spy for Earth King Jialun who posed as an unremarkable fishing merchant who often took his stock to sell in Ba Sing Se. He used the fishing business as an excuse to be away for long periods of time, spying on the Northern Water Tribe.

He was tasked with a mission to discover a way to destabilize the alliance between the Northern and Southern Water Tribes. The Earth King believed that if he could get the North to act unilaterally without the agreement with the South, it would drive a wedge between the tribes. To that end, Buhai gathered intel on Chief Skiri of the North to exploit at a later time.

Ban Buhai was an exceedingly successful spy, to the point that almost nobody knew his real identity.

entities.name: Banished servant
entities.description:
This servant girl was among a group of women that attended to Princess Azula prior to her coronation as Fire Lord. She offered the princess cherries from a bowl, but had neglected to ensure they were free of pits, as Azula discovered when she ate one. The princess became furious with the young girl and demanded to why there was a pit in her cherry on "the most important day of [her] life". The servant girl timidly explained that she had not left the pit in on purpose, and that it was "just a small mistake". Her response enraged Azula, who denied that it was a small mistake due to the chance of her choking on it and possibly dying. The panicked servant girl begged for forgiveness, and Azula decided that, as it was a special day, she would "show mercy" and chose to banish her instead. The young girl was subsequently ordered to leave the Fire Nation Royal Palace immediately.

entities.name: Baraz and Ahnah
entities.description:
Before Kuvira's army began their conquest, Baraz and Ahnah lived in the Earth Kingdom. However, when the army seized control of their homes, they became prisoners of war due to being of non-Earth Kingdom origin. They managed to escape the detainment camp, along with several other firebenders and waterbenders.

One day as they were walking in a forest, Baraz, Ahnah, and their group saw Bolin and Varrick become caught in their trap. Upon noticing their Earth Empire military uniforms, they assumed they were working for Kuvira, despite the duo's insistence that they were deserters. After freeing the duo from the net, they bound their hands, intending to use them to pass a nearby border checkpoint. The waterbenders were bending water into their water skins, while Bolin was asking how they had ended up in one of Kuvira's reeducation camps and Baraz tells him that Kuvira has been capturing and locking up everyone not of Earth Kingdom origin. Varrick asked where they were going and Baraz and Ahnah told them their goal. Bolin used his lavabending to keep them at bay, once again apologizing for what had happened to them and insisting that they were not aligned with Kuvira anymore, and Varrick adds that if he and Bolin are recognized, they'll be taken back to Kuvira. Baraz was willing to believe him, to Ahnah's disappointment; she relented, however, when he reasoned that if Bolin wanted them dead, he would have already buried them in lava. He continued by explaining that they needed to work together and trust each other in order to get past the border checkpoint which was the only way to freedom. Bolin cooled the lava and asked them where the checkpoint was. Even though Varrick pointed out that he and Bolin might be recognized, the group decided to take the risk regardless.

Initially, Bolin and Varrick's ploy managed to get the Earth Empire soldiers to let them through the gate, but the duo were soon recognized and a fight broke out between the refugees and the Earth Empire soldiers. Soon, the prisoners and them were surrounded by many mecha suits and Kuvira's soldiers. Immediately, Baraz burned the rope on his wrist and started fighting with the others. He and Ahnah were fighting a mecha suit, but it was too powerful for them. They were saved by Varrick, who disabled the suits, by creating an electromagnetic pulse device. Varrick wanted to escape and inadvertently abandon Baraz and Ahnah's group. Bolin refused, using his lavabending to drive back the soldiers. Baraz was surprised they had stayed and thanked him, saying they did not have to come back. Seeing that the duo could be trusted, the refugees offered them a boat ride up north, which they accepted.

entities.name: Basalt
entities.description:
Basalt was born during the later stage of the Hundred Year War. After joining the island's protectors and training as a warrior, Basalt eventually volunteered to serve as a combatant in the Great War against the Fire Nation. This decision was quite common for protectors of the time. Alongside several other protectors and friends, he ventured to the Earth Kingdom where they organized as a militia to fight as guerrillas and saboteurs to support the Earth Kingdom military. As part of his combat experience, Basalt developed a grudge aimed at a young Fire Nation officer named Zhao. In one battle, Basalt was heavily wounded at his hands, whereupon he was sent back to Jasmine Island by his commanding officer.

Back home, Basalt was able to heal and recuperate, though his hands remained marked by scars. He sought to soon return to the frontlines in the Earth Kingdom. and together worked out a plan to stop Yueya. This culminated in a battle where Basalt and his friends defeated the admiral, helping to save their home.

Basalt was a boisterous and determined man who had found solace in his service as a warrior. Having been a protector since his youth, fighting was so ingrained in his identity that he became quite insecure in times of peace. As a result of his experiences in war, Basalt also developed a vengeful streak and became easily angered.

Basalt was a decent earthbender, excelling in creating earthen shockwaves and tackling his opponents with brute force.

entities.name: Bathroom attendant
entities.description:
In 174 AG, he and several other agents were sent by Kuvira to kidnap Prince Wu, the rightful leader of the Earth Kingdom. While having lunch at a restaurant with Team Avatar, Wu went to the bathroom where he encountered the agent, who offered Wu some cologne, which the latter happily accepted. Before he sprayed the gas on his target, he covered his mouth, using a napkin. After Wu got knocked out, he towed the monarch to the truck where his accomplices were stationed. He pretended to haul laundry bags to the truck to reduce suspicion; however, this attracted the attention of Korra, who asked him whether he had seen Prince Wu, which the agent promptly denied. When something moved inside the truck, Korra saw Wu pop out from among the laundry bags. Realizing the scheme had been uncovered, the agent immediately attacked Korra before fleeing the scene in the truck, driving away from the restaurant. After a quick chase, Team Avatar managed to tip the truck, but were surprised to find that Wu had been transported by a different truck to the train station. After being caught and interrogated by Mako, the agent was handed over to the police and sent to the police station for questioning.

entities.name: Bato
entities.description:
Bato was born and raised in the village of Wolf Cove in the Southern Water Tribe, and was good friends with Hakoda. The two of them often played pranks on other members of the tribe and enjoyed spending time together.

Bato left his village around 97 AG, along with the other men of soldiering age. Sometime after, Bato was badly burned by a Fire Nation soldier and brought to the abbey, where the sisters took care of him and nursed him back to health.

During their travels, Aang, Katara, and Sokka found Bato's ship on a beach. Once Bato found them camping near the vessel, Katara and Sokka were elated to be around him, feeling almost at home again in his presence and his tent, which was decorated with furnishings from the South Pole continent. Bato was Hakoda's best friend as a child and through him, Sokka and Katara felt a connection to their father that they had not had in years. The three talked and reminisced long into the night, leaving out Aang. Bato acted as somewhat of a surrogate father toward Sokka and agreed to take him ice dodging, since Sokka never had the chance to with his own father. He also bore news of their father, stating that he awaited instructions on how to relocate him and the other Water Tribe men and offered to at least send word to the two of Hakoda's location as they accompanied Aang. However, in the comfort of their reunion, Katara and Sokka began to lose sight of where they were truly needed, as Aang began to feel betrayed and alone. Although at one point Sokka and Katara opted to accompany Bato on a journey to reunite with Hakoda, the siblings soon realized their duties to Aang and parted with the tribe member.

In the spring of 100 AG, Sokka and Katara received a message telling them that their father was at Chameleon Bay. Sokka agreed to reunite with his father while Katara stayed behind with the Earth King. When he reached Chameleon Bay, he walked into his father's tent, where a war meeting was in session. Bato, sitting next to Hakoda, tapped him to signal that Sokka was in the room. Later, Bato filled tangle mines and made mention of Hakoda's dry sense of humor as well as Sokka's similarity to his father.
entities.short_description: Bato was born and raised in the village of Wolf Cove in the Southern Water Tribe, and was good friends with Hakoda. The two of them often played pranks on other members of the tribe and enjoyed spending time together.

entities.name: Ben Ta
entities.description:
Ben Ta's small Earth Kingdom village was taken over by the forces of General Onomu of the Fire Nation. Shortly after, Ben Ta's mother passed away, and Ben Ta directly linked her mother's death to Onomu's soldiers seizing food and medical supplies for the war effort.

She later became the leader of a rebel group known as the Armadillo Bears. Ben Ta wanted to genuinely do the right thing, and her band of rebels did help people, but she was overzealous in her approach to the Fire Nation. She got word that General Onomu had been spotted nearby after she was due to be escorted to Ba Sing Se by a group of people working for the Earth Kingdom government, after the general planned to defect from the Fire Nation. Ben Ta led the Armadillo Bears on a mission to hunt Onomu down and kill her, planning to track the party escorting her from West Heiatu to Ba Sing Se.

As leader of the Armadillo Bears, Ben Ta was charismatic and passionate. Once, Ben Ta was ignorant, caring, and warm, but she completely changed after the Fire Nation invaded her home. Ben Ta was totally unbalanced when it came to the Fire Nation, and she saw the world in black and white. She sometimes felt longing for the woman she once was before the Fire Nation invaded, but she then remembered what the Fire Nation was doing to her home, and thoughts of vengeance buried the longing that she had. She was angry, protective, imbalanced, and driven by revenge, though she could change her mind on some matters when it came to the Fire Nation if presented with strong evidence that someone was trying to change. This aggression combined with her innate magnetism made her a dangerous leader that people couldn't help but follow.

Ben Ta was a master earthbender. She could use earthbending to launch herself into the air, and could inflict damage to others by crashing down with earthbending from large heights.

entities.name: The Big Bad Hippo
entities.description:
During his time as a wrestler, he was one of the most recognizable competitors in the Earth Rumble tournaments due to his extremely large size and distinctive manner of speaking. He often omitted determiners and articles when he talked, turning "Hippo mad!" into his catchphrase. Like The Boulder, The Hippo also referred to himself in the third person.

Team Avatar first witnessed The Big Bad Hippo in action during the first round of the sixth edition of the Earth Rumble tournaments, where he faced The Boulder. The Hippo demonstrated his unique fighting style by catching a rock The Boulder launched at him between his teeth, chewing it up, and spitting it out before initiating his signature move, "rocking the boat". This maneuver proved highly effective, causing The Boulder to stagger backward and nearly fall out of the ring. At the last moment, however, The Boulder recovered and hurled a large slab of earth at The Hippo. Despite his immense durability, which allowed him to withstand the direct hit seemingly unharmed, The Boulder ultimately defeated him by lifting both The Hippo and the earth beneath him and throwing them out of the ring.

After Aang won the tournament by easily knocking Toph out of the ring with his airbending, The Hippo and the other wrestlers assisted Xin Fu in attempting to reclaim his prize money. After the group cornered Aang and Toph, The Hippo threw a metal cage over both of them, successfully capturing them.

After Toph's parents paid the ransom to free their daughter, Sokka and Katara attempted to rescue Aang as well but were stopped by the band of wrestlers. The Hippo proceeded to lift Aang's metal cage onto his shoulder to leave the arena and deliver him to the Fire Nation for the bounty. Toph challenged The Hippo and the other fighters, promising to defeat them all again if they refused to release Aang. Taking them on simultaneously, she succeeded in defeating each of them. The Boulder, The Hippo, and the Headhunter were the last fighters standing. The Hippo defended himself by swinging a large earthen model of the Earth Kingdom's national emblem. Working together with the other two, he charged Toph, but she defeated them by shifting the ground beneath their feet.

entities.name: Biho
entities.description:
Biho was the field leader of the guards for Sparrowkeet Air, a company that helped innovate and invent war balloons for the Fire Nation during the Hundred Year War, and continued to operate in the Earth Kingdom and Fire Nation colonies after the end of the war. Biho joined up with the guards because it was a way for him to put his experience from the Hundred Year War to use making a bigger wage than he once had.

After Qian Yu took an Air Nomad artifact found at a Sparrowkeet Air factory, Sergeant Biho led the guards on Sparrowkeet Air's Flying HQ. The CEO Yuzhen Sr. and company president Yuzhen Jr. both had an emergency button which they could press to summon Biho and the rest of the guards.

Biho was not cruel, but he also was not merciful or kind. He was comfortable to follow the lead of Sparrowkeet Air as long as they kept paying him well. He was guided by power and driven to secure his own position.

Biho was a modest fighter. During a fight, he was good at quickly taking in his situation far faster than normal.

entities.name: Bin
entities.description:
Bin grew up in one of the outlying Fire Islands, and never really bought into the propaganda that was drilled into citizens day in and day out during the Hundred Year War. Most people assumed that Bin was dumb, but he was smart enough to realize that the Fire Nation nobility was running the longest con on earth, which was making people believe nobles were better than others.

When he was old enough, Bin started using his hulking appearance to intimidate rich people out of their money, and ended up making a living doing so long-term. His biggest stunt as of a few years after the war was helping the pirate Captain Mosi of the Dancing Nobleman Fleet steal a broken down airship from a Fire Nation junkyard.

After the war, Bin began to wonder if there was more to life than just a good laugh and a good con.

A joking individual, Bin was often assumed to be dumb as well as big and strong, but he had an eye for being able to scam rich nobles. He was also known for having a wild deameanor.

entities.name: Biyu
entities.description:
Biyu was the daughter of a skilled calligrapher who worked as a record-keeper for the governor in the area around Daying. He tried to pass on his interest in calligraphy to Biyu, but she had no interest in it. Against his wishes, Biyu used her earthbending to learn a physical job, and became a builder, helping to forge irrigation routes from the river to local farms.

Biyu started to fall for a young scholar from Omashu who was training to be the village magistrate of Daying. They had their first kiss at a beautiful fountain in Daying, with Biyu being the one to make the first move. After falling in love, the couple got married and had an earthbender daughter named Jin. After her daughter's birth, Biyu joined a battalion, wanting to protect Daying from bandits.

Biyu and her husband gave Jin a happy childhood. The family was not rich, but had enough money for Biyu to have a small jewelry collection for the governor's visits. Biyu promised Jin that she would pass down her pins and circlets to her when she was old enough. Biyu and her husband would also take Jin to see circus performers in the village every Autumn Festival. Jin would sit on her mother's lap during the performances, eating candied fruit on a stick and enjoying the show. Biyu and her husband were also keen to share the story of how they fell in love. They told Jin about their first kiss whenever they walked by the village fountain, and would always lean in to recreate the moment, much to Jin's embarrassment.

Biyu's father did not want Jin to learn earthbending, but she insisted on teaching her daughter at least the basics so that she learn how to control herself. Biyu also made sure that Jin knew enough about her bending to defend herself. They practiced out in the woods, with Biyu making sure to teach Jin about the philosophy of neutral jing that formed the basis of earthbending.

entities.name: Bo
entities.description:
Bo was the child of two Elders on the Council of Elders from the Southern Air Temple. Bo loved being an Air Nomad, and truly believed that Air Nomad principles were the only right way to live. They were also extremely outspoken about that fact and sometimes had problems controlling their temper with people who thought otherwise. The fact that this went against Air Nomad teachings was not lost on Bo, and they knew they had a ways to getting their master tattoos.

Bo voluntarily agreed to be part of an expedition sent to the Four Nations Summit & Technological Symposium to keep the peace organized by the Southern Air Temple on the request of Avatar Roku, including Ema, Chegu, Sherab, and Norbu. They wanted to prove that they had what it took to be a true airbending master.

Bo was impatient to become a master and was also deeply enthusiastic about their Air Nomad culture. They were well aware that they had a ways to go on working on the Air Nomad principle of humility.

Bo was a competent airbender, though was held back from getting their master tattoos due to their quick temper. They made use of thunderclap air blasts while fighting, and often worked with an ally to take down the same foe in combat.

entities.name: Boin
entities.description:
Born in Omashu, Boin was a devoted disciple of the Earth Sages, and set out on a mission to educate people across the world about them after they were purged by Earth King Jialun.

While on a pilgrimage to the Eastern Air Temple, Boin met a young nun called Nyanchi. She captured his imagination, while Nyanchi saw a kindred spirit in him and saw an opportunity to see the world and join Boin on his mission. Boin promised the Air Nomads that he would take care of Nyanchi, and acted as her guardian.

Eventually, Boin and Nyanchi met up with Ezra and Zeebee, and saved Sister Rioshon from bandits. The group agreed to accompany Rioshon to the Fire Nation Capital for the wedding of Princess Zeisan and Monk Khandro. Rioshon had uncovered a sinister plot to disrupt a pre-wedding symposium planned by Zeisan, but could not act herself as she was being watched by guards. Therefore, she tasked Boin and his allies to warn the princess.

Boin was a polite and cautious man. He was always a protector, willing to do anything for those he deemed worthy: primarily the Earth Sages, but also individuals such as Sister Nyanchi.

entities.name: Bolin
entities.description:
In the following months, Bolin quickly became close friends with the Southern Water Tribe industrialist Varrick and starred in The Adventures of Nuktuk: Hero of the South, a propaganda film series created by Varrick in an attempt to drum up support for the Southern Tribe within Republic City during the Water Tribe Civil War. After reuniting with Team Avatar, Bolin attempted to help his friends stop Chief Unalaq from fusing with Vaatu, the spirit of darkness, during Harmonic Convergence.

A few weeks after Harmonic Convergence, Bolin and his friends traveled around the Earth Kingdom to search for airbenders. At one point, the group had to flee from Ba Sing Se and split up from Tenzin. They continued their search until the Red Lotus attacked Zaofu, at which point they instead worked to combat the anarchist organization, and Bolin learned that he could lavabend.

After bringing down the Red Lotus, Bolin began a relationship with Opal and joined Kuvira in her goal of reuniting the divided Earth Kingdom with military force with the rank of corporal, However, he managed to escape with Varrick, leaving the army to believe they were dead for a while, and rejoined Team Avatar in Republic City to help them defeat Kuvira, while rebuilding his relationship with Opal.

Bolin was born to a multicultural family in Republic City two years after Mako; his father, San, was from the Earth Kingdom, and his mother, Naoki, was from the Fire Nation. At the young age of six, he lost his parents to a firebending mugger, leaving Mako as his only immediate family. To survive, Bolin was heavily dependent upon his brother who, as the oldest, took on a parental role. To generate some form of income, the brothers initially ran small-time scams on the streets of Republic City during their youth and, for a time, also consorted with the Triple Threat Triad.

entities.name: Boma
entities.description:
Before Yangchen left the Western Air Temple, Boma made an oath to the Western elders to keep her safe. Boma looked after her until and after she became a fully-realized Avatar.

When Yangchen was summoned toward Tienhaishi a week after she mastered all four elements, Boma accompanied her there, despite Yangchen's protests that she would be fine on her own. He had refuted those claims, stating that he had promised the Air Nomad nuns that he would look after her until she was ready to be on her own and that it was never a good idea to break a promise to a nun. During the Avatar's audience with the king, Boma was present as well, taking care of Yangchen's two winged lemurs, Pik and Pak, whom he comforted after they were scared by the local fortunetellers.

Believing the prophecy that something bad was to befall the city from the sea, Boma accompanied Yangchen on her stakeout on a cliff overlooking the water. When General Old Iron appeared and knocked Yangchen down, he helped her up and urged her to stop the rampaging spirit while he evacuated all the citizens to a nearby clearing.

As Yangchen began to settle into her official, diplomatic responsibilities, he occupied a strange and undefined role in her retinue. He did not look the part of a dignitary with his weathered face and plain way of speaking, and nobles sometimes rankled at his presence, while Boma had no problem rankling back. Some time after the evacuation of Tienhaishi, Boma and Yangchen went to Bin-Er together for the Avatar's first official visit to one of the shang cities. When Yangchen stayed at the Blue Manse at the edge of the shang district, Boma handled Yangchen's security team, and who was being hired and fired.

entities.name: Boqin
entities.description:
By 99 AG, Boqin was a Captain in the Earth Kingdom Army and commanded the Shen Guan garrison. He knew many of the local soldiers well, most importantly the Infirmary Guard. Shen Guan was one of the attackers' targets. Thus, the stronghold was assaulted by a Fire Army force under Captain Masaru.

Once Masaru's forces surrounded Boqin's main garrison at the fortress town, the captain sent a soldier outside with orders to sneak through enemy lines and request outside aid. Meanwhile, the Fire Nation commander urged his opponent to willingly surrender, pointing out the weakness of Shen Guan's garrison. Boqin was initially unimpressed, calling the demand a bluff and claiming that Masaru only called for their surrender as he was unable to storm Shen Guan's strong defenses. However, the Fire Nation captain revealed that his troops had begun attacking the Earth Kingdom camps around the fortress town, a fact soon confirmed by one of Boqin's subordinates. The Earth Kingdom captain still refused to yield, despite being deeply concerned for the fate of his troops outside the stronghold's walls.

Not long after, Avatar Aang flew into Shen Guan using his airbender staff. Boqin was shocked to see him, regarding him both as an outsider as well as a mere child. The officer did not allow Aang to explain who he was, ordering the boy to leave the fortress immediately. Despite his sharp words, Team Avatar subsequently decided to aid Shen Guan nonetheless, and attacked the Fire Nation forces at the camps. As they did so, Masaru prepared for a major attack; once this assault began, Shen Guan came close to falling to the Fire Nation. In his desperation, Boqin sent word to the infirmary at one of the camps, asking any soldier who could to come aid the defenders. The Infirmary Guard, by then knowing of Team Avatar's capabilities, subsequently enlisted the group's aid. With his old friend assuring Boqin that Aang, Katara, and Sokka were capable and trustworthy, Boqin allowed them to take part in the planned counterattack, conditioning that Aang had to follow his lead even if he truly was the Avatar. The Fire Army troops were ultimately bested by the allies, and Masaru was forced to order a retreat.

After this victory, Boqin told Team Avatar that he was grateful for their support and apologized for having underestimated them. However, Team Avatar responded positively, with Sokka telling the officer that he was a "pretty nice guy" after all. Boqin laughed and responded that they should keep that to themselves, as his stern reputation would suffer otherwise. He then sent them on their way, assuring them that he had requested reinforcements and the garrison could defend Shen Guan even without Team Avatar's help.

entities.name: Borte
entities.description:
Borte was enslaved by the League of Shattered Skulls. She managed to talk herself out of becoming a human sacrifice, and entered Chanyu's service in the Temple of Corruption.

As Borte lacked Chanyu's spiritual connection, she relied on her relentless determination to survive in the cult of Father Glowworm. Borte managed to position herself as a High Priestess through guile and manipulation of Chanyu's warped mind. As High Priestess, Borte received command of the Temple Guard, a fanatical group that answered only to her. She saw these zealots as the key for her to overthrowing Chanyu, and potentially claiming Murong's throne.

entities.name: Bosco
entities.description:
Prior to his capture, Bosco lived in the forests along the eastern coast of the Earth Kingdom. He was the only known member of his species, although the Earth King had commanded the top zoologists of Ba Sing Se University to lead a battalion of soldiers in scouring the Earth to find Bosco a mate. Little is known about his habits in the wild; however, Bosco enjoyed roaming the grounds of the Royal Palace with his master, and he developed a taste for cakes and pies, hence his weight.

Bosco was the guest of honor at a birthday party the Earth King threw for him, where he ate large portions of food and was fascinated when Aang performed waterbending tricks.

He frequently sat at Kuei's side and was one of the prime reasons Kuei decided to hear what Aang and his friends had to say about the conspiracy in Ba Sing Se, as Bosco took a liking to Aang.

Bosco was at Kuei's side when he welcomed the disguised trio of Azula, Mai, and Ty Lee. Apparently, Mai was forced to clean all of Bosco's waste, stating that "if [she had to] clean another pile of bear poop, [she would] throw up". Bosco was separated from Kuei after Azula ordered the Dai Li to arrest the King, but was soon reunited with his master when Sokka and Toph rescued him from Ty Lee and Mai, the latter not even stirring herself to fight.

entities.name: The Boulder
entities.description:
Though his pro-wrestling "stage accent" may have seemed unintelligent, he spoke with a degree of consideration and eloquence that suggested a greater intellect beneath his bombastic wrestler demeanor. Part of his unique pattern included always referring to himself in the third person and frequently employing earth-related puns.

At some point during his wrestling career, The Boulder got a crococat, whom he named "The Pebble", as a pet. The small animal quickly grew very attached to him and the two of them became inseparable for several years, though The Boulder hid his beloved pet from the public as it did not fit his image as a tough wrestler. Despite their good relationship, The Boulder occasionally had trouble with his pet, such when he attempted to take The Pebble to a veterinarian multiple times. On each occasion, the crococat became extremely obstinate and aggressive. Once, The Pebble even knocked out the wrestler. Thereafter, he even refrained from mentioning veterinarians around his pet.

The Boulder won at least one Earth Rumble tournament prior to spring 100 AG.

When The Boulder was a combatant in the Earth Rumble VI tournament in 100 AG, he faced The Big Bad Hippo in the first round. After taunting his opponent, The Boulder commenced with a frontal attack by chucking large pieces of rock at The Hippo, who remained unfazed by the assault. Almost knocked out of the ring by The Hippo's unique "rocking the boat"-technique, The Boulder managed to defeat The Hippo by lifting the earth underneath his feet and tossing him out of the arena. This feat of power sparked Katara and Aang's attention, who were spectators of the tournament in search of an earthbending teacher for Aang. Katara commented that The Boulder had some good moves, a statement to which Aang rightfully retorted that The Boulder was more prone to listen to his muscles than anything else.

entities.name: Broadsword man
entities.description:
In 100 AG, this broadsword man was roaming the streets of the river village when he saw two vagrants: the banished Prince Zuko and the retired General Iroh, disguised as simple refugees.

After watching Iroh's attempts to collect coins from pedestrians, the broadsword man offered him a gold piece, on the condition that he provided some entertainment. Compliant, Iroh began singing "Girls from Ba Sing Se". Despite Iroh's melody, the man remained petulant and dissatisfied. In an attempt to get Iroh to dance while singing, the man drew his dual broadswords and slashed them at Iroh's feet. When Iroh uttered the last note, the man halted his attacks and guffawed, satisfied. He awarded Iroh the promised coin and walked away, sheathing his swords.

At night, when he was walking through the streets alone, he felt threatened and drew his swords upon hearing a noise. Before he could identify its source, his dual dao blades were quickly knocked from his hands and he was harshly tossed against some nearby standing crates, rendering him unconscious. His swords were subsequently stolen by Zuko, who was under the guise of the Blue Spirit.

entities.name: Buddy
entities.description:
Buddy helped to defend and comfort Aera when Team Undefeated was badly bullying her over her disability. Tearan, Moriko, Akito, and Botan followed Aera home and started throwing insults at her, but Buddy swooped in and scared off the aggressors. Buddy almost got himself hurt in the incident, and Aera was deeply grateful that he had stepped in to protect her.

Meeting Buddy also helped Aera improve her firebending. Aera had been unable to master the traditional firebending forms because of her limb difference, and was only able to produce a small fire ribbon. Buddy grew very excited once he saw the ribbon, and started chasing after it. Aera laughed after seeing him react to her fire ribbon. She stopped being self-conscious, and focused on playing with him every evening. Over time, she found herself being able to make the ribbon longer and longer, and make it dance more and more.

One night, Buddy approached the fishing boat of Adaro. The cat bat was attracted by the irregular light emanating from the vessel, the result of Adaki's unsuccessful attempts to create a large fireball. Buddy eventually landed on the boy's shoulder, scaring him and causing him to stop firebending. The small creature responded by quickly flying away.

By accident, Aera mentioned her "other friend" to the rest of Team Adaki after they had started training for the Regional Bending Tournament. The other firebenders asked her more about the friend, and asked to meet him. Aera started to create a fire ribbon as a signal to lead Buddy to the beach, and he started to appear after a few minutes. However, Aera had not explained that her friend was not human. Sujun and Adaki started to grow scared once they saw Buddy approach, and Jiyung tried to warn Aera that the cat bat might hurt her. Aera quickly spun around and stopped bending, and Buddy flew away.

entities.name: Bujing
entities.description:
Known for his calculating manner, sadism, and ruthless attitude, General Bujing had an obsession with victory, even if it meant sacrificing inexperienced troops to gain a battlefield advantage.

In 97 AG, while Prince Zuko attended his first war meeting, Bujing explained a military plan to move a weak division of Fire Nation recruits to fight an experienced battalion of earthbenders. This would make the latter concentrate its efforts and resources on the former, leaving the way open for more capable Fire Nation soldiers to encircle and defeat them. In his words, the new recruits were the best bait available. Zuko spoke out against his plan, seeing it as a betrayal of the patriotism and honor of the new recruits. Bujing and the other attendees, including Fire Lord Ozai, were greatly offended. This outburst against the elderly general served as a powder keg for the strained relationship between Zuko and his father, who told him it was an act of disrespect and could only be settled by an Agni Kai. Zuko accepted, not being afraid of the elderly Bujing. However, Zuko unexpectedly ended up facing Ozai instead. Bujing attended the Agni Kai as a member of the audience and frowned upon seeing Ozai scar his son with firebending.

Bujing attended the war meeting the day before a solar eclipse, where he exchanged an uneasy glance with General Shinu when Prince Zuko entered the room. He later applauded Ozai's plan to destroy the Earth Kingdom with the power of Sozin's Comet.

Bujing was a sinister general who would do anything to win, even if it meant going all out and sacrificing a squad full of inexperienced soldiers on the battlefield. Despite his cruelty, his intelligence also shined in his plan of attack, as the plan would have given the Fire Nation troops a clear advantage. Bujing was a proud man, as when Zuko criticized his plan, he challenged him to an Agni Kai.
entities.short_description: Known for his calculating manner, sadism, and ruthless attitude, General Bujing had an obsession with victory, even if it meant sacrificing inexperienced troops to gain a battlefield advantage.

entities.name: Bully guard
entities.description:
By spring 100 AG, he served as one of the gondola guards. He escorted Suki and other prisoners from a hot air balloon sent by Princess Azula to the prison facility. At the gondola, he took enjoyment in seeing Suki's shock at the prison's extensive defenses. He then gleefully told her that she should forget any hope of escaping. No one escaped from the Boiling Rock; she "belong[ed] to us now".

In the next months, he rose to a regular guard at the prison. When Zuko and Sokka first arrived in the prison yard, the bully guard was goading Chit Sang in order to force him into firebending, which was prohibited for inmates. After Chit Sang, his girlfriend, and his friend's escape attempt failed, Chit Sang was interrogated so as to divulge who masterminded the plan; he accused the bully guard of being the instigator, as payback for the bully guard's earlier harassment of him. As a result, the guard was arrested and taken in for questioning. His interrogation was interrupted by Princess Azula, who cleared him of the charge, explaining that he was not associated with the escape attempt.

The bully guard tended to be very cruel toward the prisoners at the Boiling Rock, and he intimidated and harshly mocked the prisoners who were held there. He lived alone, as he was not a very social person and had no true friends or people to whom he could talk, and in addition he had little to no romantic relationships. As a result, he liked to take out his personal frustrations by harassing the prisoners, the only people he had some control and power over, such as Chit Sang. However, underneath his usual rough and unsettling personality, he was actually just a sad, lonely man.

entities.name: Bum-Ju
entities.description:
Several dragonfly bunny spirits, including Bum-Ju, played with Jinora at the Eastern Air Temple. Although the young airbender could see them, the spirits remained invisible to the others until Jinora urged them to appear under Kya's insistence. Bum-Ju and the other spirits led Jinora and her group to the ancient meditation circle away from the temple grounds, where Bumi officially met the spirit and named him. After their brief meeting, Bum-Ju fled along with the other dragonfly bunny spirits after Tenzin performed a spiritual cleansing ritual on the grounds, which attracted a colony of dark spirits from underground.

Bum-Ju reunited with Bumi following Avatar Korra's defeat of Dark Avatar Unalaq during the Harmonic Convergence of 171 AG. Soon after, the two witnessed the Avatar address the Southern Water Tribe to announce the end of the Water Tribe Civil War and happily listened as she declared her decision to keep the spirit portals open.

Soon after, Bum-Ju traveled with Bumi to Air Temple Island and fled from the retired commander when he attempted to dress him in a hand-knitted pink sweater. Bum-Ju attempted to keep Bumi from falling off a cliff in his attempt to reach the spirit, but was unsuccessful, witnessing as Bumi fell and began to airbend.

Bum-Ju joined Bumi and Team Avatar in their search for airbenders to recruit as part of the Air Nation, keeping the retired commander company while the group traveled across the Earth Kingdom aboard a Future Industries airship. Bum-Ju was with the team when they ambushed two Royal Earthbender Guards in order to access the military compound beneath the Earth Queen's Temple in Ba Sing Se where airbenders were held captive by the Dai Li.

entities.name: Bumi
entities.description:
Bumi's eccentricity arose from the fact that he always kept his mind "open to the possibilities". As a child, Bumi decided to use the Omashu delivery system as a chute ride, for which Aang dubbed him "a mad genius", a name that Bumi seemed to appreciate. Although Bumi appeared senile, he was in fact a brilliant and patient tactician, willing to wait until the opportune moment to strike in order to produce the most favorable outcome. Bumi carried himself with the same composure during a quiet, peaceful meal as he did when his city was under attack, and he rarely explained his actions, which tended to infuriate his subordinates.

King Bumi was born in 12 BG in the city of Omashu. At one point, Bumi was gifted a goat gorilla pup whom he took as a pet and named Flopsie. The earthbender raised the pup with great care and love, resulting in Flopsie becoming fairly docile in adulthood.

Sometime later in his life, Bumi was crowned King of Omashu. Under his rule, Omashu was turned from a strong but isolated bastion into a center of the Earth Kingdom resistance. He organized the supply of anti-Fire Nation guerrilla groups with arms across the entire continent, and invited inventors to his city so they could develop new weapons for the Earth Kingdom. Despite his efforts, however, the Hundred Year War increasingly turned against the Earth Kingdom. The Fire Nation advanced ever closer to Omashu, gradually closing the city's supply routes. Regardless, he remained eager to support anyone willing to oppose the invaders. At some point, he joined the Order of the White Lotus.

Bumi saw Aang again in 99 AG, when the Avatar, Sokka, and Katara were brought before him to receive judgment for destroying a cartload of cabbages belonging to a cabbage merchant. Aang did not recognize his friend, who was now one hundred years older than when they last met, and Bumi did not reveal their shared past and told his guards, when asked what Team Avatar's punishment should be, "throw them ... a feast!"

Zuko later found him and tried to force information out of him, only to be attacked by a machine, which ended in both their capture.

entities.name: Bun
entities.description:
Bun was born to his parents at Pebble Pond Village around 87/88 AG. His immediate family belonged to the middle class, but was not wealthy. Once he became old enough to do so, he helped to deliver skunk squids, though proved to be quite clumsy. He often dropped the squids during his deliveries, much to the other villagers' annoyance due to their extreme odor.

As he grew older, he heard heroic tales about soldiers past and present, including the Kyoshi Warriors. Based on these idealized tales and the fact that his older friends enlisted in the Earth Kingdom military, Bun developed the desire to become a soldier. Despite still being a young teenager, he eventually volunteered for the local army unit of General Andal, much to his parents' dismay. At the time, Bun was the youngest inhabitant of Pebble Pond Village to ever enlist in the military.

After just one week of training, Bun was assigned to fight in the next combat operation. While his parents were horrified, the young boy was eager to fight the Fire Army. He hoped to capture a Fire Nation dagger to gift it to his father and mother.

On the day before his first frontline deployment, Bun chanced upon a group of strangers who were confronted by several Pebble Pond Village inhabitants. The young boy attempted to make his way through the crowd with skunk sharks, but tipped and accidentally threw several of them onto other locals. The villagers fled in terror, but the strangers' leader Suki helped Bun up. Having overheard some of the previous conversation, he excitedly asked whether they were really Kyoshi Warriors. Mira and Aika affirmed this, adding that they were seeking to join the Earth Kingdom Army. Bun offered to help them, taking them to General Andal's ad hoc headquarters at his uncle's house. On the way, he commented that Andal would surely "flip" upon seeing them.

entities.name: Bun's parents
entities.description:
In 99 AG, Bun volunteered for the Earth Kingdom Army unit of General Andal. His parents opposed his decision due to him being underage and lacking martial abilities, but were unable to do anything as they lacked the money necessary to buy him out of his military service contract.

One week later, Bun brought a group of Kyoshi Warriors under Suki to his parents' house, explaining that they needed a place to stay for the night. Bun's parents shared a meal with the visitors, and his mother responded positively to the warriors' praise of the food. Meanwhile, his father urged Bun to eat more as he needed strength for the future. When Bun happily responded that he could not possibly eat due to his excitement about his deployment, Suki asked in confusion whether the young boy was a soldier. His parents remained silent in response, worry creasing their face, as their son boasted that he would surely capture a Fire Nation dagger as a gift to them. When the boy was distracted by Mira, his parents dejectedly told Suki about their worries.

On the next day, Bun's parents worriedly waved goodbye to their son as he marched off to the frontline.

Thanks to the Kyoshi Warriors' intervention, Bun barely survived his first battle, though he was heavily wounded and lost one of his legs. Bun was thus discharged from the military after just one operation. Afterward, his parents personally thanked the Kyoshi Warriors for saving their son. Talking with Suki, Bun's parents explained that they planned to move to Ba Sing Se, believing the capital to be safer than their home village. The father also noted that Pebble Pond Village had become tainted with "too many bad memories" for the family.

entities.name: Buo Ren
entities.description:
After joining the Earth Kingdom military, Buo Ren distinguished herself and rose in the ranks until being promoted to captain. Eventually, she was assigned to the small garrison on Jasmine Island, an island-state which was an Earth Kingdom protectorate. As a staunch loyalist of her nation as well as a follower of law and order, she strove to lead the local troops in accordance to the old treaty between the Earth Kingdom and the Jasmine Islanders. She thus tried to stay out of the natives' politics and focus on just leading her troops in a disciplined manner. She was popular among most of the garrison's soldiers.

However, Buo Ren soon noticed how her civilian counterpart, Magistrate Emerald, was gradually increasing the Earth Kingdom's influence on the island. Having lived among the natives for some time, Buo Ren felt conflicted over this as she respected the locals. However, she was also not willing to act against Emerald as long as he remained within the constraints of his position and acted in the Earth Kingdom's interests. Unbeknownst to her, Emerald was utterly abusing his position to undermine Jasmine Island's independence and effectively organizing a creeping coup. To avoid the captain's attention, the magistrate always sent Buo Ren on some mission when he conducted especially egregious abuses or covert operations.

Eventually, two Guiding Wind members, Fengying and Sakuru, broke into the Earth Kingdom outpost to find evidence for Emerald's illegal activities, but were caught by his personal guards. In response, Buo Ren increased the outpost's security. Meanwhile, the magistrate framed the two activists as devious criminals, and declared his intention to send them to the Earth Kingdom mainland to stand trial. Despite Emerald's claims, Buo Ren treated Fengying and Sakuru as dignified prisoners, already distrusting the magistrate's motives. Guiding Wind leaders Khandro and Zeisan subsequently traveled to Jasmine Island to seek their allies' freedom. Buo Ren and some of her soldiers were present as the two revolutionaries appealed to the island's leadership in the Council Hall, unaware that two of the three council members were effectively controlled by Emerald.

As the meeting at the Council Hall was ongoing, a group of Jasmine Island protectors, namely Ukiuk, Qi Wei, Pushi, Sukaya, and Baljin, infiltrated the Earth Kingdom outpost. Upon being notified, Emerald demanded that Buo Ren impose martial law on the island to catch the perpetrators, and she agreed. Ultimately, Emerald's attempted takeover was exposed and the situation of the island returned to the previous status quo.

Shortly after the Avatar's arrival in Republic City, Butakha met with the Fire Ferrets during one of their early practices in Toza's gym. There, he handed Mako the team's winnings from their previous match, but soon reclaimed all of it after he took off payment for Korra's pro-bending gear, the team's gym and equipment lease, rent on Bolin and Mako's attic space, and a personal loan for groceries taken out by Bolin. He proceeded to explain to the Fire Ferrets that they needed to ante up thirty thousand yuans for the championship pot or they would have to forfeit their position in the tournament.

When Avatar Korra first arrived at the Sato estate, the butler escorted her to the indoor pool and announced her presence to Asami, Mako, and Bolin. To show the guest a demonstration of his pleasureful servitude, Bolin ordered him to dry off himself and Pabu with a towel. entities.name: Buttercup Raiko
entities.description:
Buttercup and her husband attended the finale of The Adventures of Nuktuk: Hero of the South as honored guests, having been invited by Varrick in hopes of convincing them to help support the South in the Water Tribe Civil War. Buttercup was flattered by Varrick's many compliments upon their arrival, but remained silent as her husband reaffirmed his position to remain diplomatic in internal Water Tribe conflict.

In the middle of the mover, Buttercup and her husband were nearly kidnapped by four waterbenders, but were promptly saved by Bolin, who subdued the attackers with his earthbending. The president and his wife were secured by several of Chief Lin Beifong's officers to ensure their safety, while Varrick was apprehended for masterminding the attempted abduction.

In 174 AG, Buttercup accompanied her husband to Air Temple Island, where they both entertained Prince Wu in conversation. When an Air Acolyte notified all those present in the dining room that a ship from the South had docked at the island, Buttercup accompanied everyone to greet Korra, though was surprised to learn that the Avatar was not there, leaving everyone to wonder where she might be.

Weeks later, after the conclusion of Kuvira's attack on Republic City, Buttercup attended the wedding of Varrick and Zhu Li, sitting between her husband and Ginger. She smiled as she watched the ceremony unfold, happy for the two despite Varrick's attempted kidnapping of her and her husband three years prior.

entities.name: Cabbage merchant
entities.description:
Cai was born in Gaoling in the southern Earth Kingdom. He inherited a cabbage farm from his family, locally selling vegetables just as his mother and grandmother had done before him. At one point, he married and had a daughter and a son named Lau Gan-Lan. Unlike his ancestors, Cai had bigger dreams and wanted to sell his beloved cabbages to many more people. As a result, he ultimately decided to pack up his products and become a traveling salesman, seeking a good place to set up shop. He left his farm and children under the care of his wife, promising to send for his family once he had found the ideal location to settle down.

Over time, the cabbage merchant traveled to various locations in the Earth Kingdom, selling cabbages from a cart that was repeatedly destroyed, prompting him to exclaim, "My cabbages!" As he traveled widely, Cai was able to collect various recipes related to cabbages. He was known to have visited the northwest, southwest, and the southern islands of the kingdom, where he gathered inspiration to develop and perfect some of his cabbage dishes.

When Cai was trying to enter Omashu, his cart was destroyed by a troop of overzealous earthbending guards. Though horrified at the actions of the guards, the merchant retroactively admitted that his vegetables had indeed lost their freshness during the travel to Omashu. He subsequently obtained a new cart filled with fresh cabbages and began his attempt at selling his merchandise.

Soon after, his cart and cabbages were destroyed again when Team Avatar crashed into them while riding the Omashu delivery system. Following this, the outraged merchant alerted the guards to arrest the offenders. He demanded they be beheaded, "One for each head of cabbage!", during their subsequent trial, but King Bumi threw them a feast instead, to Cai's shock and annoyance. His cart was destroyed for a third time in Omashu by King Bumi and Aang while they rode the mail system again.

entities.name: Cai
entities.description:
At some point, Cai signed a contract to work in the Upper Ring of Ba Sing Se. However, she was actually taken to Lake Laogai, as a candidate to be brainwashed and turned into a Cultural Ambassador. During her imprisonment, she witnessed a group of Joo Dees shortly after their brainwashing, who would not respond or even flinch when called out to. She was considered for brainwashing on multiple occasions, placed into a lineup with other girls to be chosen by officials, but she was never picked.

After the Fire Nation took control of Ba Sing Se, Cai remained in her cell, with other Joo Dee candidates. Eventually, Jin, Xuan, Smellerbee, and Longshot snuck into Lake Laogai in search of Susu, and they found the cell with the Joo Dee candidates. While the girls did not trust them, Xuan explained that they were there to rescue them, and Cai told them a bit about her experiences in the prison. She joined the rest of the girls when their rescuers led them out.

Once freed, Cai had nowhere to return to, so she began to live and work at Wen Bakery as a baking assistant along two other would-be-Joo Dees.

A few weeks later, there was a commotion at the bakery, as Fire Nation soldiers complained about how savory the salted duck egg pastries were. Cai watched from the sidelines, and explained the situation to Jin when she asked. The incident inspired Jin and she subsequently came up with spreading word of the Silver Fangs' planned revolution through the pastries. After being informed of the plan, Cai and the other former Joo Dee candidates eagerly participated in the work, wanting to help the fight against the Fire Nation.
