entities.name: Defense attorney
entities.description:
In 128 AG, an underground malefactor named Yakone was tried for his criminal acts upon Republic City and its citizens. The defense attorney was present during the trial as Yakone's legal representative, where he urged the Council to acquit his client from all charges considering that the crime he supposedly committed was not possible to perpetrate.

Despite the attorney's efforts, Chairman Sokka delivered the verdict of the Council that, although it was common belief that bloodbending could only be performed under a full moon, Yakone was one of a few "unique benders" and had used his outlawed ability to commit crimes in Republic City without the presence of a full moon. He was found guilty of all charges and sentenced to life in prison. Outraged at the loss of the trial, the defense attorney crumpled a piece of paper and threw it on the ground.

However, before Yakone could be detained, the criminal demonstrated his bloodbending prowess by subduing every person in the courtroom, including the defense attorney. The attorney was knocked unconscious by Yakone, along with all of the other individuals present at the trial, shortly before the criminal fled the courtroom.

entities.name: Desna and Eska
entities.description:
As chiefs of the Northern Water Tribe, they oversaw various social and legal reforms, and took part in diplomatic efforts to stabilize the Earth Kingdom after the murder of Hou-Ting.

Desna and Eska were born in 155 AG to Unalaq and Malina. Growing up in the North, Desna and Eska developed little appreciation toward the Southern Water Tribe and its inhabitants, including their cousin, Korra.

In 171 AG, Desna and Eska accompanied their father to the South Pole continent for the Glacier Spirits Festival. They stood silently by as their father and their uncle, Tonraq, curtly greeted each other.

As the children of the chief, Desna and Eska sat at the table of honor during the royal banquet that was thrown in honor of their father. There, they attentively listened to the conversation Unalaq was having with Korra, though remained silent the entire time. After dinner, they attended the festival carnival, where they stood solemnly, gazing with disinterest at the passersby, before Eska was approached by Bolin, who was trying to charm her. Eska intently stared at him, inhaling sharply, causing the earthbender to become unnerved, and Desna monotonously stated that he thought Bolin was trying to establish a bond with his sister. Amused by the idea of spending time with someone of a different cultural background, Eska promptly stated that he now belonged to her. When Bolin asked if she wanted him as a boyfriend or a slave, she remained ambiguous and instead ordered him to win her prizes.

entities.name: Ding
entities.description:
While Ding was wandering through the woods one night during a full moon, Hama took control of his body using bloodbending and forced him to walk toward a prison she had set up underneath a mountain. Ding attempted to take control of his body again but was unable to do so and looked at the moon for what he thought was going to be his last sight of light. However, by the time Ding had reached the cave entrance, the sun had risen, breaking Hama's hold over him. Having regained control of his body, he ran back to the village. Thereafter, he prepared for each full moon by boarding up his home and taking refuge.

In the summer of 100 AG, while Aang, Sokka, and Toph were gathering information about the alleged spirit that had been abducting the village people, a traveling townsman directed them to "Old Man Ding", stating that he was the only one to have ever seen it and lived. Ding was approached by the group as he was boarding up his windows, though he struggled to lift the wooden boards as he did so. At the group's request, he recounted the story of his near kidnapping and subsequent escape to them. Ding's story led Team Avatar to the mountain where they rescued Hama's other victims and had her arrested for her actions, freeing Ding's town.

entities.name: Disha
entities.description:
Disha was the last Air Nomad companion of Avatar Kyoshi as she neared the end of her life. They traveled to places together such as Agna Qel'a. Disha and Kyoshi were companions for over 20 years; during that time, the Air Nomad observed how Kyoshi became more and more willing to take the lives of her enemies for the sake of justice and peace.

Two years before Kyoshi's death, she and Disha faced off with a daofei leader who sought revenge on Kyoshi for her killing of his father many years ago, to the point that he and his gang had committed atrocities for the sole purpose of getting her attention and giving him an opportunity to fight her. Kyoshi killed the daofei leader, after which Disha pointed out that that he had become a foe because of her past actions; she questioned how many other threats and conflicts they had needed to deal with were the same, before expressing concern for what Kyoshi would turn into should she have lived for another century. The Avatar was displeased by Disha's criticism, prompting the Air Nomad to leave her side and share her concerns with the Council of Elders; the Air Nomads subsequently became unwilling to aid Kyoshi any further.

By the 16th year of the era of Avatar Roku, Disha had a flying bison named Amra. After Roku was identified as Kyoshi's successor, Disha was selected to serve as his airbending instructor. She and Amra briefly visited the Fire Nation Royal Palace to take Roku to the Southern Air Temple, in order to begin his Avatar training. While in the Fire Nation, Disha attended a ceremony in which Roku said farewells to his fellow Fire Nationals; when he did so with Fire Lord Taiso, she showed a brief look of annoyance when Roku bowed first, rather than waiting for the Fire Lord to do the same.

While training Roku, Disha also took a special interest in supporting Gyatso, a young monk from the temple who struggled with his airbending following the death of his sister Yama.

entities.name: Diu
entities.description:
Jasmine Island, a small, independent state, was heavily affected by the Hundred Year War, particularly by a Fire Nation invasion known as "The Devastation". The islanders were still rebuilding by the end of the war, but once the physical and economic reconstruction was largely complete, new political divisions emerged. After "The Devastation", no elections had been held and the existing council had ruled for years with the general acquiescence of the entire community. When the council members such as Yuming finally stepped down and and announced new elections, various factions across the island saw this as a chance to kickstart substantial, genuine changes in reforms. Conversely, these factions – several influenced by past events and developments across the world – could not agree with each other.

The Climbing Vines were one faction which emerged during this period. It came into existence among Jasmine Island's rural population, mainly farmers and field laborers, who had benefited comparatively little from their homeland's economic recovery after the war, instead seeing their fortunes being eclipsed by the urban population at the island's docks. Regarding this as the result of unfair treaties by foreigners as well as individualistic dealings by some islanders, many rural people became angry and demanded changes. They eventually organized under Diu as the Climbing Vines, seeking a voice in the Jasmine Island council to implement communitarian and anti-imperialist policies.

Whereas the other factions – including the Autumn Leaves, Antiquarians, and Risen Wave – bitterly feuded, the Climbing Vines signaled their willingness to compromise and organize a coalition government after the elections. Regardless, no other faction signaled any interest in the Climbing Vines' offer.

Some of the Climbing Vines' political aims, such as the expansion of the council, were eventually achieved.

entities.name: Do
entities.description:
Do trained with Kavik several times during the latter's training with the White Lotus in Bin-Er. Once, he put a fire dagger to Kavik's throat as they sparred, close enough to leave a line of blisters.

The firebender came to see Ayunerak at the secret basement beneath Gidu Shrine outside the hours of his regularly scheduled visits, bringing news about her being able to return to the Northern Water Tribe. His footsteps thus raised Kavik's immediate suspicion, causing the young waterbender to launch water that he had pulled from the laundry towels at Do's feet, freezing his soles to the wooden planks. This, in turn, caused Do to pitch forward so violently he fell out of his boots, with him cursing Kavik's name on the way down. However, Ayunerak reacted with blinding speed, and unfroze the very water Kavik had used, sweeping it around in a lap and catching the laundry in a web of water, shoving it into a heap at the bottom of the stairs. Do landed in this, unharmed, but the firebender shouted at Kavik over the serious injuries he might have endured. Ayunerak shut down the argument between the two men, though she took the opportunity to inquire why Do had come. The firebender whispered in the Executor's ear to relay the lengthy message to her, before giving him a head shake to indicate he should leave. The firebender balked when he realized his superior's plans would not involve him, and gave Kavik a scowl as he tugged his boots back on. The young waterbender could not resist waving goodbye to Do as he left.

entities.name: Doji
entities.description:
Doji was always suspicious of the other nations, viewing them as lesser than Republic City and the United Republic. After it was revealed that Amon was actually born as Noatak and raised in the Northern Water Tribe, Doji came to primarily view the Anti-bending Revolution as proof that the other nations posed a threat to Republic City. The Unalaq Crisis once again proved to him that the Northern Water Tribe was a risk, and then only a few years later, the Earth Empire directly attacked the city. This led him to further develop personal fears and biases.

As an up-and-coming commander within the United Forces, he directed authority over Yue Bay. Prioritizing security at the cost of freedom and openness, Doji started constantly blockading, interdicting, and searching incoming vessels at the port, holding "suspicious" persons for questioning, and generally slowing down legitimate immigration procedures. While Doji remained at a lower rank than General Iroh, the remit of his authority in the area meant that he did not have to run his decisions past his commanding officer in advance. This meant that Iroh could walk back Doji's decisions, but it was not always easy or immediate. His beliefs and policies thus threatened to define the United Forces' presence in the area in accordance with his prejudices.

When a massive Northern Water Tribe passenger vessel named the Spirit Skies arrived at Yue Bay, Doji ordered his ships to intercept it. The ship was carrying an influx of immigrants to Republic City from not just the Northern Water Tribe, but also the Earth Kingdom, the Southern Water Tribe, and even some from the Fire Nation. With the Spirit Skies being one of the biggest passenger vessels to ever arrive at the bay, Doji viewed it as a threat, believing it was a chance for countless infiltrators to pass into the city all at once. He was determined to hold the ship until each and every passenger could be interrogated individually, their belongings searched, and their identities verified. General Iroh wanted to countermand Doji's orders, but the commander provided "evidence" of the nefarious purposes of the passengers, although Iroh suspected that this had been fabricated. Nevertheless, this evidence meant that Iroh could not countermand Doji's orders without appearing to be "aiding and abetting dangerous threats." Iroh looked for aid of people who could prove Doji was manufacturing evidence, and needed this done quickly, as some of the immigrants had health conditions, and were in need of treatment as soon as possible.

Doji was a considerably xenophobic person, and had a desire to cling to a past that never was. He valued security over anything else, and his own biases and fears shaped his actions and policies as a military officer.

entities.name: Dojo master
entities.description:
At some point during the last stage of the Great War, the dojo master trained a highly capable student named Taowu. However, Taowu saw his strength and growing martial arts abilities as a sign of superiority, and began to behave in a way that was unacceptable to the dojo master. The two split, and the dojo master ultimately migrated to the Southern Archipelago. At the time, the local islanders suffered under repeated Fire Nation raids. When the civilians recognized that the stranger was a martial arts master, they requested aid. The master agreed to train the locals, demanding regular food supplies and no further questions on their past or identity in return. The master then set up a hidden dojo in the Patola Mountain Range, and began to take in students. Before long, however, the pupils split into rival factions, disagreeing on the best fighting techniques and the most powerful jings. The only student who attempted to overcome the infighting, Xin Ming, held little respect among her comrades and was thus ignored.

In winter 99 AG, the dojo master finally got fed up with the students' squabbles, kicked everyone out of the dojo, locked up the food store, and then broke the key. The master declared that only the strongest pupil could enter the dojo, and until then, no one would get food. The students immediately began to fight, with the key pieces being split among three main factions. One day later, however, Xin Ming encountered Team Avatar by chance; she asked them to help her to gather the key pieces.

After succeeding, Xin Ming and her allies entered the dojo where the master confronted the group. At first, it seemed as if the master was trying to block their way, as Xin Ming had only won the contest by involving outsiders. When Team Avatar defeated the master in a duel, the latter kindly stated that Xin Ming and her friends had won fairly and proven to be the strongest. When one other student protested, the master declared that the strongest was not the one who conquered all, but the one who unites them, and that Team Avatar and Xin Ming managed to defeat the others even though they were outnumbered. Soon after, as Team Avatar was preparing to leave, the master approached Katara and Sokka, asking the siblings to lend their strength to Aang and revealing that they knew the boy's identity as the Avatar.

Following Team Avatar's departure, the dojo master and Xin Ming discussed the dojo's development. Though new trainees were arriving and swelling their ranks, the students still focused more of fighting each other rather than the Fire Nation. The master asked Xin Ming on her opinion of how to solve this issue, whereupon she proposed inviting outsiders as challengers. These would combat the students for rewards; in this way, the dojo's members would train and also unite against a common foe. The dojo master considered this a good idea, and allowed Xin Ming to set the plan in motion.

entities.name: Doorman
entities.description:
In 170 AG, on the night of the Revelation rally, the doorman was assigned to ensure that every attendant of the rally had an invitation, which came in the form of a flyer. When Mako and Korra arrived, disguised as a couple, he halted them, stating that they were about to enter a private event and asked them for their invitations. When Korra stumbled, he looked suspiciously at the couple until Mako casually showed the flyer and asked if it were the invitation. The doorman took it and warmly welcomed them as his brother and sister.

During the rally, immediately before Korra had planned to use waterbending to create a steam cloud as cover for Mako to rescue Bolin, the doorman confronted her and inquired her reason for being there. She attempted to fool him, claiming that she had been looking for the bathroom; however, the doorman did not believe her excuse. He subsequently took out his wrench and attacked her. Korra avoided his attacks and was able to use Mako's scarf to throw him into the pipes, rendering him unconscious, consequently causing the pipes to burst, thus filling the room with steam.

entities.name: Dorje
entities.description:
Dorje managed the Southern Air Temple at least as early as 316 BG, at which point he was allowing Kelsang, one of Avatar Kuruk's companions and also a resident of the temple, to be groomed to eventually take over his duties. However, Dorje later changed his mind after a series of events caused Kelsang to fall out of his good graces. These events included the time when Kelsang took the Avatar relics without his permission in 305 BG in order to identify the next Avatar,

While many Air Nomads had a reputation for their peaceful nature, fun-loving attitude, and appetite for baked pastries, Dorje reportedly eschewed many of these customs. According to Kelsang, with whom he had a falling out, he possessed an aversion to fun, distaste for fruit pies, and wrathful mood when disobeyed.

entities.name: Dorzhi
entities.description:
Belonging to one of the nomadic Si Wong clans that roamed the Si Wong Desert's Northern Plains, Dorzhi was cared for by an elder relative during his youth. At the time, the region suffered under a decades-long drought and the local clans mostly survived by pledging loyalty to the Earth Kingdom. He was an earthbender and learned how to control a sand-sailer when was still young.

One day in the 130s AG, two sand-sailers made a stop at the Si Wong meeting place where Dorzhi and his elder were staying at the time. The elder greeted the newcomers, embracing Tsetseg, a fellow tribeswoman who worked as an Earth Kingdom Army guide. When Tsetseg revealed that they had come to recruit sandbenders for an anti-raider operation, the elder initially claimed that no benders were present at the meeting place. Militia leader Bai Yin Du immediately realized that this was a lie due to the presence of other sand-sailers at the locality, threatening the elder. Seeing this, Dorzhi rushed out of a nearby building, revealing himself as a sanbender and volunteering to join the mission. Bai Yin happily accepted him and declared that he would receive a water ration for his clan after one month of service. Despite the elder's protests, Dorzhi subsequently accompanied the militia into the desert.

The group continued their journey until evening, when they set up camp at a small stone overcrop. They were surprised by a rattle jackal which promptly attacked, biting Dorzhi's right arm and injecting its venom. The rest of the group managed to fend off the creature and they fled onto their sand-sailers, returning to the open desert. Kya attempted to heal Dorzhi but discovered that her waterbending was blocked. Another militia member, Anwat, suggested muri bean leaves as an alternate treatment. While Dorzhi suffered growing pain and fever due to the venom, Anwat managed to gather some leaves from the surrounding desert. The group was able to create an ad hoc antidote and successfully cared for the young sandbender, though the boy remained deeply weakened. On the next day, Bai Yin ordered Anwat to bring Dorzhi to Liyuan for further treatment, while she, Kya, and Tsetseg continued their journey.

Dorzhi was later discharged from the Liyuan militia and happily reunited with his elder, assuring her that his arm "was not too bad" as he had received quick medical aid from the others.

entities.name: Dragon eel spirit
entities.description:
When Kuvira's power began to threaten the spirits who had come to reside in Republic City, the dragon eel spirit retreated to the Tree of Time in the Spirit World. They were later visited by Avatar Korra, who asked for the spirits' help in defending the city, but the dragon eel informed her that spirits did not get involved in human wars. Korra countered that the spirits had sided with Unalaq in his campaign of darkness, but the dragon eel corrected her that the former Chief of the Northern Water Tribe had misappropriated the power of Vaatu during Harmonic Convergence and forced the spirits to fight for him. Despite Korra's claims that she did not wish to force the spirits to do anything, the dragon eel concluded that, ultimately, she wanted the same thing as Kuvira: to use the spirits as weapons in a human war. Reiterating that spirits would not get involved, the dragon eel vanished, with the other spirits following their example.

After Kuvira's defeat and the creation of the new spirit portal in the heart of Republic City, the dragon eel spirit returned to the city's Spirit Wilds, and later circled the portal when Korra and Asami approached it to start their vacation in the Spirit World.

The dragon eel spirit was again circling the spirit portal when Korra and Asami returned to Republic City from their vacation, monitoring an argument between Wonyong Keum and Jinora about the airbenders' presence there as they did so. The spirit continued to keep its distance when Korra and Asami joined the discussion, but when Wonyong told Asami that Keum Enterprises owned the land surrounding the spirit portal and could therefore do with it as he pleased, the spirit angrily flew up to Wonyong and accused him of being "just another human" who refused to respect the sacred. Making it clear to the businessman that the deeds to the land did not give him the right to ravage and plunder the Spirit World, the dragon eel spirit turned to Korra and urged her to close the portal, as it was never meant to be there and left the Spirit World vulnerable to exploitation. Korra asked the spirit why they were suddenly interested in human conflicts, noting their previous vehement refusal to get involved when Kuvira posed a threat to Republic City. The dragon eel replied that since there now was a portal in the middle of the metropolis, they had no choice but to protect their kind. When Korra refused to follow up on their request, reasoning that the new spiritual energy would have a harmonious effect on the citizens of Republic City, the spirit relented and retreated to the portal, though not before warning her that they would hold her responsible for keeping the portal safe.

entities.name: Druk
entities.description:
In his 20s, Fire Lord Zuko found a juvenile dragon that he named Druk. Over the years, Druk grew up and became Zuko's loyal companion, and the two of them flew around the world together.

Zuko traveled on Druk to Ming-Hua's prison after hearing about the waterbender's escape.

Soon after, Zuko mounted Druk to survey the North Pole for any signs of Zaheer and his company, whom they spotted approaching under the cover of a snowstorm. During the altercation that followed, Druk attempted to stop Ming-Hua and P'Li by attacking them with a fire blast. Despite the intensity of the attack, P'Li easily deflected the blast and fired a combustion beam straight toward Druk, who cried out in pain from the impact.

Druk recovered, however, and was fit enough to fly his master and Tonraq toward the Misty Palms Oasis, where he waited outside the town walls after Zuko had gone inside, scaring two camels as he stared at them.

entities.name: Due
entities.description:
While separated from Aang, Katara, and Sokka, Appa and Momo encountered Due and Tho, who began hunting them down. Aang eventually found Appa and Momo and stopped Tho and Due, who were more than happy to find fellow waterbenders from outside of the swamp. Due, Tho, and Huu subsequently invited the team to their camp to share a meal.

Months later, Due, together with his fellow tribesmen Tho and Huu, helped with the initial land stage of the invasion of the Fire Nation during the Day of Black Sun in 100 AG, but remained behind when the invasion force started scaling the volcano. When the eclipse ended, the Fire Nation deployed its airships to the beach to destroy the submarines, the invasion force's only means of escape. The three waterbenders tried to protect the submarine fleet, but their efforts proved to be in vain. Like the rest of the adult fighters, Due was detained in a Fire Nation prison, but was released at the end of the Hundred Year War and later attended Fire Lord Zuko's coronation ceremony.

Due did not appear to be particularly intelligent, usually letting Tho think for him, but he deeply value family ties and relationships, since he considered himself and Katara to be "kin" as they were both waterbenders. He even called his catgator, Slim, a member of the family. In general, he was dim-witted but friendly and worked hard alongside his friends and family to keep them happy and well-fed. He also proved to be a master waterbender.

Due was a powerful and strong waterbender, proving his skill in both the swamp and during the invasion of the Fire Nation. Due also was a master of the rigid and stiff Foggy Swamp waterbending style, and was able to counter an attack from Aang and Katara combined.

entities.name: Duga
entities.description:
Duga grew up poor, but joined the Fire Navy to hone his firebending abilities. He was mercilessly bullied by fellow crewmates who did not understand his amazing gift due to his sensitive nature, and ended up deserting to escape the torment. Rather than return home a failure, Duga swore to make something of himself and joined up with a crew of pirates the first chance he got.

The young man proved himself invaluable to the crew of the Burning Wave by setting merchant boats alight with his bending while the pirates plundered to their hearts' content. Duga slowly worked his way through the ranks until he was first mate, when he then bit his tongue as the captain squandered the wealth they stole. Eventually, the foolish former captain died on an expedition, leaving Duga in charge.

Waiting for the moment his entire life, Duga set about changing the Burning Wave for the better. He soon won the loyalty of his crew, who doubted his leadership skills at first, but grew to cherish their captain as their pockets grew heavy with coin. Under Duga's leadership, the Burning Wave made more money than any other Crimson Sails pirate faction during the Hundred Year War by also dabbling in mercantile pursuits, but they only shared the bare minimum with the Armada. Their greed made them an object of scorn on Crimson Sails, but enterprising pirates who actually wanted to make a profit knew that Duga and the Burning Wave were their best shot.

Duga used to have a good working relationship with Tengfei, leader of the Renegade Phoenix, and some even said that the two were in love. However, the relationship soured when Duga left Tengfei stranded on a mission, because she was caught by guards. Some would have made the choice to go back for her, but Duga placed profit above any loyalty he had toward a fellow pirate. Crews of the Burning Wave and the Renegade Phoenix came to blame one another for more than a few blundered missions, and they continued to clash after the war was over.

entities.name: The Duke
entities.description:
Jet and the other Freedom Fighters came across The Duke when they caught him trying to steal food from their camp. According to Jet, The Duke never had a home and he eventually joined the group.

Being a constant companion to Pipsqueak, the duo became guerrilla fighters, assisting Jet in the fight against the Fire Nation occupation of Gaipan. When Aang, Katara, and Sokka were cornered by a company of Fire Nation soldiers, The Duke and the other Freedom Fighters came to the rescue. During the ensuing battle, The Duke dropped out of a tree, right on the helmet of one of the soldiers and rode him "like a wild hog monkey". When Jet introduced his Freedom Fighters to Team Avatar after the battle, Aang mistook The Duke for being Pipsqueak. After snooping through the camp's supplies, The Duke and Pipsqueak found barrels full of blasting jelly and boxes filled with jelly candy. The Freedom Fighters loaded up the loot in a cart and headed back to their hideout, where they had a feast to celebrate their victory over the Fire Nation soldiers.

A few days later, The Duke was among the Freedom Fighters who headed out at night with a cart filled with barrels of blasting jelly. When Jet was explaining his plan to blow up the dam with the jelly and subsequently flood Gaipan and everyone living there, The Duke voiced concern for the people, something Jet countered by stating that it was "the price of ridding this area of the Fire Nation". The Duke proceeded to help Sneers and some other Freedom Fighters to place the barrels full of explosives at the base of the dam.

After Jet destroyed Gaipan with a flood intending to kill every inhabitant, During their time at Chameleon Bay, they were described as "surprisingly helpful" when they were not getting into trouble.

entities.name: Earth Empire fugitives
entities.description:
Before the beginning of the Earth Empire, these firebenders and waterbenders lived in the Earth Kingdom states. After Kuvira brought about the beginning of the empire, their states were purged by her military and these benders were subsequently imprisoned due to being of non-Earth Kingdom origin. However, they managed to break themselves out of the prison and hide in a big forest. The forest, however, was bordered by the Earth Empire's security forces. The group managed to find the sole checkpoint in the border. They then devised a plan to trap some Earth Empire soldiers to make their escape.

Days later, Bolin and Iknik Blackstone Varrick, who became fugitives themselves as result of deserting the Empire, fell for their trap. After they were released from their trap, the group's leaders Baraz and Ahnah explained to the duo about the actual situation of the people in the re-education camps. They later revealed their motive to use the duo to make their escape. However, before they could act, the group was cornered by Bolin who used lavabending to keep the group at bay. After each side understood the other's situation, they decided to work together to make their escape. On reaching the checkpoint, Bolin and Varrick pretended to be Earth Empire soldiers taking the fugitives through the checkpoint. They almost managed to pass through the checkpoint, until Bolin and Varrick were identified. The group was quickly surrounded by the soldiers and mecha tanks and a battle ensued. During the battle, Varrick managed to create an electromagnetic pulse to disable the mecha tanks and Bolin used lavabending to drive the soldiers off and the group, along with the duo, managed to escape. Bolin and Varrick were given the offer to accompany the group on their journey north and the two accepted since they could reach Republic City via that route in order to inform the government of the incoming threat from Kuvira.

During their journey, the benders passed their time narrating their stories, with Baraz being the last to do so, although the stories turned out to be incredibly boring. Varrick managed to liven up the mood by spinning a story for his next mover The Adventures of Nuktuk: Hero of the South, placing Bolin as the protagonist and having him take on Avatar Korra's past enemies: Amon, Vaatu, Unalaq, and Zaheer. At the end of the story, the group, having enjoyed it, gave a round of applause to Varrick, although it quickly died out, and they became annoyed with Bolin after he criticized the story.

entities.name: Earthbender captain
entities.description:
The earthbender captain served in the Earth Kingdom military during General Iroh's siege of Ba Sing Se, where he developed an especially strong hatred toward the Fire Nation officer.

Not long before the winter solstice of 99 AG, he and his unit of earthbending soldiers stumbled upon a bathing Iroh and captured the retired general by trapping him in the spring with their earthbending. When a soldier commented that Iroh was a Fire Nation soldier based on his uniform, the earthbender captain quickly identified Iroh for who he truly was: the Fire Lord's brother, the Dragon of the West. He smugly finished off by stating that the "once great" General Iroh was now their prisoner.

The captain and his unit set out immediately, riding through the night on their ostrich horses to take Iroh to Ba Sing Se to face justice. Still angered over Iroh's attempt to conquer the city, the captain stated that the city was greater than Iroh, as it would not yield to him.

The next day, the captain asked Iroh whether something was wrong when the latter had gasped in shock when he saw Aang's spirit pass by on Avatar Roku's dragon, Fang. Iroh initially stated that everything was fine, though swiftly reconsidered and complained that his handcuffs were too loose, asking for them to be tightened. Though he was surprised by such a request, the captain ordered his corporal to do as asked. However, Iroh had tricked him, as the firebender had heated his chains and pressed the corporal's hand against them, burning him, before firebending from his feet at the rest of the troops in order to facilitate his escape. While the earthbender captain attempted to calm down two started ostrich horses by pulling tightly on their reins, he watched as Iroh rolled down a mountainside.
entities.short_description: The earthbender captain served in the Earth Kingdom military during General Iroh's siege of Ba Sing Se, where he developed an especially strong hatred toward the Fire Nation officer.

entities.name: Earthbending academy teenagers
entities.description:
While leaving Master Yu's Earthbending Academy, Team Avatar overheard the two boys praising Earth Rumble as the best earthbending competition in the country. When the team asked about what it was and where it was held, the boys refused to tell them, proceeding to laugh cruelly at the group and walk off. Katara ran after the boys and came back with information about the tournament. When asked how, she replied, "A girl has her ways." As it turned out, she had left them scared, heads locked together and frozen up to their chins in ice.

The team later returned to the academy after the tournament to find out who the mysterious Blind Bandit was, and the teenagers recognized Aang as the boy who had beaten her. They at first did not provide any information, but after Katara threatened them again, they shared information stating that the flying boar Aang had seen earlier in a vision was the symbol of the Beifong family. The team later used this information to track down Toph Beifong after Sokka ended the conversation by saying "Water Tribe".

Both students appeared to be quite obnoxious and egotistical. They displayed a nasty attitude toward Aang when asked about the Earth Rumble VI tournament, teasing and poking fun at him. They did, however, also appear somewhat cowardly, growing particularly intimidated in Katara's presence.

entities.name: Elderly swordsman
entities.description:
A resident of the village of Gaipan, the elderly swordsman was among the citizens who gathered when the Rough Rhinos arrived at the settlement in the 90s AG. The village leadership quickly surrendered to the Fire Nationals, seeking to ensure their survival. Frustrated at the easy victory, the Rough Rhinos' leader, Colonel Mongke, grabbed the village leader and demanded that he duel him. At this point, the elderly swordsman stepped forward and declared his willingness to fight despite the colonel's protest that he was "pathetic". Even though the swordsman displayed some skill, he quickly tipped and fell due to his advanced age. Though utterly disappointed at this anticlimactic outcome, Mongke spared the old man.

The elderly swordsman was among those villagers of Gaipan who left or were expelled after the Fire Nation occupation began. As he moved through the nearby woods with his belongings, the old man encountered a young boy named Jet by chance. The latter recognized him from the attempted challenge in Gaipan, accusing him of "running away" after failing to fight Mongke. The swordsman tried to convey that his own fighting spirit remained unbroken, but his body was failing him. When Jet remained unimpressed, the old man attacked the young boy. While the boy evaded the swordsman's strikes, the elder asked whether Jet was truly willing to relentlessly battle the Fire Nation.

When Jet eventually screamed that destroying the Fire Nation was "all that I have left", the swordsman was satisfied. He passed his hook swords to the boy and respectfully bowed, declaring that Jet displayed the necessary spirit to fight. Afterward, the old man grumbled about his back pain and continued his journey.

entities.name: Elua
entities.description:
Elua had an especially close relationship with Princess Ursa, who considered Elua to be like family. Because of their bond, she served as Ursa's secret courier to deliver messages to Hira'a. Unbeknownst to Ursa, Elua was also acting under the orders of Ozai. The prince had ordered her to file the secret letters away, instead of sending them to Ursa's hometown. However, after reading one of the princess' letters, she discovered a secret that she decided was enough reason to personally deliver the letter to Ozai.

Elua had a conflicting personality. While appearing to be highly loyal to Ursa, she betrayed the princess' trust by following Ozai's orders to intercept the secret letters. She was, however, completely terrified of Ozai while delivering Ursa's last known letter to him.

entities.name: Ema
entities.description:
Ema was adopted by the Air Nomads when his Earth Kingdom village was swallowed by a giant tsunami. As one of the only survivors with no family left, he was taken in by the Air Nomads of the Southern Air Temple and raised as one of their own.

The kindness of the Air Nomads taught Ema that even if one struggled in life, there was always hope, and he used that hope to develop a number of gliders that helped him compete with even the best airbenders. Ema had not left the temple since he was taken there as a toddler, and volunteered when the Southern Air Temple sent a group of Air Nomads to keep the peace at the Four Nations Summit & Technological Symposium at the request of Avatar Roku, including Bo, Chegu, Sherab, and Norbu. He wanted to see the world, and also perhaps to reconnect with his Earth Kingdom roots.

Ema was a truly hopeful figure, even though some of those he faced off doubted him. He was very earnest and compassionate to others.

Although he lacked airbending abilities, Ema was able to engineer inventions that allowed him to mimic airbending to a certain extent. He also had several alchemical satchels that he could drop from his glider during a fight.

entities.name: Ember Island Players
entities.description:
The Ember Island Players were all professionals, however their pay was relatively low. Almost all of them wished to advance to a greater stage. Their plays featured overly-dramatic acting and dazzling special effects. They performed The Boy in the Iceberg, written by Earth Kingdom playwright Pu-on Tim. They also frequently performed - or "butchered", according to Zuko - the play, Love amongst the Dragons. When Zuko was young, his mother used to take their family to see their plays.

A list of the characters portrayed by the actors in the play, in order of appearance: {| width="100%"

The actress who played Katara was much more curvy and older in comparison to the real Katara. Unlike the real Katara, Actress Katara was always lamenting and was preoccupied with hope. She had a more dramatic voice than Katara, expressed her feelings greatly toward everyone, especially Aang. Unlike the real Katara, who at the time was conflicted about her feelings for the Avatar, she was madly in love with Zuko and saw Aang like a brother. She overreacted to almost everything, frequently breaking into bouts of sobbing. Although Team Avatar, namely Katara, displayed dislike for her acting skills, the Fire Nation locals expressed much enthusiasm toward her and the play in general.

The actor who played Sokka served as the comedic character in the play, was much thinner and older than the real Sokka, and had buck teeth, a big top-knot rather than a warrior's wolf tail and hair around it, something which Sokka did not have until Book Three. While the real Sokka seemed to like his performance, he did not like how the script delegated him to comic relief. Most of his jokes were centered on hunger and meat, a comic exaggeration of Sokka's love of food. With the help of Suki, Sokka snuck backstage and gave the actor some jokes that he felt were more himself. The actor was initially exasperated by "a fan with ideas" but after reading, he found he liked them and spontaneously used them in the play, to the delight of Sokka and the audience but to the annoyance of the other actors.

entities.name: Emerald
entities.description:
Born in the Earth Kingdom, Emerald was very ambitious. Concluding that he could rise in the ranks of the Earth Kingdom bureaucracy by annexing new territories, This location was a formally independent state, but had been under protection of the Earth Kingdom since a pirate invasion in the 3rd century BG. The past magistrates had been tasked to uphold and oversee the implementation of the Jasmine Island-Earth Kingdom treaty, with the job being widely regarded as rather unimportant and even boring. In contrast, Emerald recognized that he could exploit the treaty and the magistrate's post to garner covert power. As few others applied, he easily got the job.

Upon arriving on Jasmine Island, Emerald initiated his long-term project, even as he publicly claimed to honor all terms of the old treaty between the natives and the Earth Kingdom. and used it for bribes and to hire new followers. Furthermore, he brought in a growing number of Earth Kingdom traders and settlers, arguing that this would strengthen the island's economy. Though some economic growth did happen, the wave of migrants largely created a local community that generally supported his actions. The islanders initially did not recognize the dangers of these developments, and many welcomed Emerald's investments.

Conversely, the magistrate quickly realized that he could not rely on his military counterpart, Captain Buo Ren of the Earth Kingdom Army garrison on the island. The latter was a moralistic and law-abiding officer who enjoyed the loyalty of the garrison; knowing that she would oppose his schemes, Emerald deceived her over his projects and often sent her on missions to distract her from the developing conspiracy. Indeed, no one among the Earth Kingdom's leadership knew of or approved his plans either, but Emerald believed that they would quickly accepted his actions once he presented them with a new province for the Earth Kingdom.

Over years, he gradually subverted many of Jasmine Island's institutions. He began to dismantle the island's security forces – the protectors – by further reinforcing the Earth Kingdom Army garrison and then claiming that the protectors were becoming unnecessary. Among these military reinforcements were also elite soldiers who were directly loyal to the magistrate, allowing him to deploy these troops without getting Buo Ren involved.

entities.name: Emi
entities.description:
When Emi was a young student at a Fire Nation school, Yangchen visited their class to conduct a special firebending training exercise. Emi acted shy and embarrassed by the Avatar's presence and avoided looking at her when they heard about the activity. Yangchen explained to the class that, when she had been learning firebending herself, the training course they were about to use had been under construction. She told the students that, at their age, it was easy to allow their emotions to control their bending, and emphasized the importance of maintaining a calm mind and exercising patience in stressful situations. As Yangchen led the students toward a training tunnel, she noticed Emi lingering behind the rest of the group and appearing uncertain. Yangchen reassured them that they would make it through the exercise if they had confidence in themselves and their classmates. Upon reaching the tunnel, Yangchen instructed the students to enter and emerge together while older students attempted to distract them with firebending, reminding them to remain calm when confronted with unfamiliar situations and to rely on one another throughout the exercise.

Emi entered the tunnel alongside their classmates, carrying a flame to illuminate the way. As the group proceeded through the course, they noticed flames ahead and assumed that the older students participating in the exercise were attacking them. Confused and frightened by the apparent confrontation, Emi questioned Yangchen, pointing out that she had not warned them that the older students would attack. Yangchen responded by asking whether the older students had actually attacked them, prompting Emi to reconsider what had happened. While the rest of the class initially celebrated their apparent victory, Emi remained doubtful and began assessing the situation more carefully.

As the students realized that they had become lost, Emi deduced that the older students had never actually attacked them and were instead merely intended to serve as a distraction. They concluded that the class had reacted too quickly and, in doing so, had missed the obvious solution to the exercise: the red lanterns marking the correct path through the tunnel. Emi also recognized that the flames they were carrying had prevented them from seeing the lanterns clearly. Following their realization, Emi and their classmates lowered their flames, allowing the markers to become visible, and followed them through the remainder of the course. They subsequently emerged from the tunnel together and successfully completed the exercise, with Yangchen reiterating her lesson about maintaining a calm mind, exercising patience, and learning from and relying on others.

entities.name: Enaka
entities.description:
Although she was assigned to guard the Four Nations Summit & Technological Symposium, Enaka was well aware that Minister Khuchtei was in charge, and would not deviate from her orders without very good reason. She was not particularly interested in the summit, and mostly wanted it to come to a close with as little trouble as possible.

Enaka accompanied Khuchtei when she burst into Zoryu Hall to inform the other delegates that crates of rare and valuable meteorite ore had been stolen. The theft of the meteorite metal was very close to her worst nightmare, as she expected to be blamed for failing to protect the metal.

Enaka was driven by her desire to maintain order. She was mostly obedient of those she recognized as her superiors, though she could grow worried when she expected to be blamed for any perceived failings.

Enaka was a skilled firebender. Her signature technique was using a "flamecharge" to hurtle at her foe with enormous speed and force.

entities.name: Engineer
entities.description:
Six months after the Anti-bending Revolution, the engineer awaited his boss, Asami Sato, as she landed Future Industries' latest product, the commercial biplane. Despite Asami's excitement and belief that the planes were now ready to ship, the engineer had concerns about the future of the company. He expressed his fears of imminent bankruptcy since no company was willing to work with them due to Hiroshi Sato's incarceration for allying himself with the Equalists. However, he was told by Asami not to fear, as she planned to travel to the Southern Water Tribe to meet with Varrick, who could restore Future Industries to its former state of success.

After Harmonic Convergence, the engineer was employed by Asami to steer a Future Industries airship during Team Avatar's journey to rebuild the Air Nation.

entities.name: Enuk
entities.description:
Enuk came from a proud and successful Southern Water Tribe family. After they gained airbending abilities following the Harmonic Convergence during the life of Avatar Korra, they joined up with the Air Nation to explore their new abilities and fully explore who they really were. When they left, the duties of carrying on the family tradition fell to their younger sibling, Changunak.

Enuk participated in the Air Nation's defense of the spirits three years after Harmonic Convergence. After Changunak came to Republic City, Enuk hoped to protect her from the dangers and stresses of the city, and the burden that they left behind.

Enuk was a capable airbender. They incorporated their Water Tribe origins into their distinct style of airbending, and they often created long, flowing winds like streams of water.

entities.name: Erchtei
entities.description:
Erchtei was born into a highly respected family on the outer Fire Islands. Dissatisfied with a lawful life in the Fire Nation, however, he opted to become a pirate and join the Fifth Nation. This decision not only disgraced his entire family, but also greatly hurt their finances as he stole his relatives' money to kickstart a corsair career. As a powerful firebender, Erchtei rose in the ranks of the pirate nation and became a commander. He took part in the battle against Yun's forces, including Kyoshi, in 296 BG. This clash shattered the Fifth Nation and ended in Tagaka's capture, though Erchtei was able to escape with a remnant faction of corsairs.

After a period of time, Erchtei and other Fifth Nation loyalists were contacted by Tagaka who had broken out of prison and tried to restore their grand fleet. Though her previous defeat had destroyed Erchtei's faith in the pirate queen, he joined her forces as he lacked the charisma to convince his followers to stay independent. Thus, he became the new second-in-command of Tagaka's fleet, though harbored the hope of eventually getting the chance to seize power himself.

Seeking ways to loot resources and money to rebuild the Fifth Nation, Tagaka agreed to Erchtei's plan to attack Jasmine Island. Unlike his superior, Erchtei had bigger ambitions for the location: He wanted to not just plunder, but to rule the island. Erchtei envisioned himself as a governor on behalf of the Fifth Nation. Accordingly, he hoped to reach some kind of accord with the locals to ease the takeover. As the pirates approached Jasmine Island, they chanced upon a Fire Nation warship and captured it. In the process, they kidnapped inventor Tei Eesoni; neither Tagaka nor Erchtei recognized Tei's true value, instead forcibly conscripting her as an "engineer" to aid with the captured warship's engines.

Upon arriving at Jasmine Island, the pirate fleet was attacked by a small Fire Nation ship commanded by famous firebender Hei-Ran. As this clash was still ongoing, Erchtei opted to already launch an initial small attack on Jasmine Island to exploit the element of surprise. Despite Mirlon's intel, Erchtei's knowledge of the locals was quite limited. Thus, his initial attack was more of scouting mission; the pirate commander also used the opportunity to talk with a group of protectors, including Ara, Joh, Fu Karaq, Revik, and Yarru, trying to convince them to surrender. Instead, the natives fought off the first landing.

entities.name: Erdene
entities.description:
Erdene and her sister Qacha came from Bhanti Island in the Fire Islands. To Erdene, the island was awfully, terribly, obnoxiously boring. After Harmonic Convergence, Erdene gained airbending abilities, and she was ecstatic. She immediately began badgering her family to let her leave the island and go train with the new Air Nation, as it was her big chance to see the world.

While Qacha was hesitant, eventually the sisters' mother insisted that Erdene go to meet up with the other airbenders and learn how to use her abilities — and that Qacha go with her to keep her out of trouble. Erdene was grateful to be able to leave, but annoyed that her overbearing older sister had to come, too. But when they left Bhanti Island, Erdene was thrilled with every last thing she saw and experienced.

When they reached Republic City and met up with the Air Nation, Erdene immediately proved herself capable as an airbender. She was prodigiously talented, and was easily capable of mastering techniques and abilities as fast as she could be taught. However, she also found the more restrictive elements of her training to be stifling, and she had a tendency to sneak out as often as possible, requiring Qacha to follow her.

Erdene and Qacha met Bolin on a team where they protected a train depot from saboteurs, where they worked together with Thi, Meeka, and Dae to resolve the situation. After this incident, Bolin asked to meet the five again for a quick noodle lunch at Dancing Dan's Noodles near the Varrimovers International Studio. He explained that the production of new mover Sengo: Lady of the Winds was having problems, and that he suspected that benders were endangering the set. Being busy as President Zhu Li Moon's personal assistant, Bolin asked the team if they could do him a favor by handling security for the mover production.

entities.name: Ezra
entities.description:
Growing up in the Fire Nation Capital, Ezra trained as a firebender along with other noble children. When he was young, he had a dispute with Minister Zianda, who took the effort to get Ezra kicked out of school and banished from ever learning in any Fire Nation academy.

Bereft of other options, Ezra took to the streets and eventually ended up in the Earth Kingdom, where he trained with earthbenders to hone his own bending, ultimately creating a hybridized and forceful way of bending.

Eventually, he met up with Nyanchi, Boin, and Zeebee, helping to save Sister Rioshon from bandits. He agreed to accompany her to the Fire Nation Capital for the royal wedding of Princess Zeisan and Monk Khandro, where he hoped he might lay Minister Zianda low in revenge for getting him kicked out of firebending school. However, Rioshon eventually asked Ezra and the others to warn Princess Zeisan about a sinister plot to disrupt a pre-wedding symposium held by the princess, with Rioshon being unable to do so herself as she was being watched.

Ezra was a very determined individual, but could also be excessive.

entities.name: Fai Lan
entities.description:
Fai Lan was born to "Ma", the infamous leader of the Burning Ember Gang, a criminal outfit which dominated Fire Nation Capital's Harbor City during the Great War. When his mother stepped down from her position, control over the gang passed to Fai Lan. Unlike his mother, he was no firebender and thus had to rely on terror to keep control of the crime group.

By bribing the Domestic Forces and crushing all potential rivals, Fai Lan was able to maintain and expand the Burning Ember Gang's influence. By 95 AG, he was even planning to expand into the upper-class Hari Bulkan, home to the Fire Nation Royal Family and the Fire Nation government.

Fai Lan usually posed as a mysterious and quiet figure, hiding his extreme brutality and temper unless provoked. Forced to compete with benders for power, he had to rely on his force of personality to keep his followers in line; However, Fai Lan was determined to deal swiftly and viciously with anyone who outright questioned his authority.

Despite his brutality, Fai Lan was also an intelligent leader who managed his criminal realm well and planned ahead for the future. His gang respected him, and he put great importance in providing protection to all those loyal to him. Nevertheless, his aid was always tied to some kind of demand.

entities.name: Fan
entities.description:
Fan was originally a bounty hunter. In the last years of the Hundred Year War, she earned a fearsome reputation as someone who was willing to take any job and work for the most dubious employers; it was popularly said that "Fan's so heartless she'll turn in her own mother for a bounty". Eventually, Fan assembled a crew of fellow bounty hunters, namely Wei, Kinmei, and Shu-Hui; together, the group became infamous for their effectiveness in catching bounties in the Earth Kingdom. At one point, the group encountered another famous bounty hunter, June, and developed a good relationship with her.

After 100 AG, however, bounty hunting became increasingly difficult as the Earth Kingdom government tried to curtail non-state vigilantism. Thus, Fan and her crew opted to use their hard-earned money to settle down in the Fire Nation colony of Daxia Harbor, buying a farm. While the others specialized in various subjects, Fan managed their entire business as well as their production of tea blends. She gradually became very proud of their farm, and felt that that they had made the right choice in settling down. However, they and other farmers in the area soon started to suffer under the increasingly despotic Wuyi Tea Cartel, a crime group which taxed Daxia Harbor's small merchants.

One day in the late 100s AG, Fan and her comrades were once again selling their products in Daxia Harbor when they were surprised to see June strolling by. Fan quickly greeted her, and upon noticing their acquaintance's confusion, explained their new way of life. She then gifted June a llamapaca wool scarf, dried mango, pickled yams, and a bit of tea for June's prisoner, Iroh. After the two thanked Fan for the gifts, they noticed nearby merchants being harassed by some thugs. The ex-bounty hunter explained that these were members of the tyrannical Wuyi Tea Cartel, but quickly shifted the topic and invited June to visit their farm in the future.

Later that day, June –now alone– visited Fan's farm. Happy to see her, the latter eagerly showcased the grounds to her acquaintance. After a small tour, the two rested on the farm's porch and drank some tea. Noticing June's unease, Fan asked where Iroh was, but June refused to answer and pointed out that the he had done terrible things in the past. The farmer responded that this description also fit her; after a while, June asked whether Fan and her crew were willing to do one last job –break Iroh out of the Wuyi Tea Cartel's prison– for some money. Fan smiled and responded that she would give her a "'friend of the crew' discount".

entities.name: Fang
entities.description:
Roku found Fang when the latter was just a baby, not yet hatched from his egg. Fang's parents were gone, so Roku raised the young dragon as his own. Eventually, the pair became inseparable.

By 37 BG, Fang was large enough to easily fly with Roku on his back, and together they discovered the first Fire Nation colonies in the Earth Kingdom.

By 12 BG, Fang lived in a cave located just behind Roku and Ta Min's modest cottage on Roku's island. When the volcanic island experienced a massive eruption that year, Fang attempted to aid his friend. Even though Roku insisted that he leave, Fang stayed with him the entire time. After initially helping Roku to contain the eruption, Fire Lord Sozin betrayed the Avatar and left him to die. Seconds before a pyroclastic flow rolling down the mountainside overcame Roku's location, Fang subsequently flew down and curled up around Roku in a form of protection, and the two died together. Following his demise, Fang entered the Spirit World along with Avatar Roku.

Fang's spirit first appeared to Aang when he was attempting to stop Hei Bai from destroying Senlin Village. After Aang discovered he was in his spirit form for the very first time, he was confronted by Fang's spirit, who took the young Avatar to the Crescent Island Fire Temple on Crescent Island to see Avatar Roku's statue, where he learned that Roku wanted to speak to him during the winter solstice about Sozin's Comet. Afterward, the dragon took Aang back to his body.

entities.name: Farmer and wife
entities.description:
In 100 AG, the couple encountered a sleeping Appa in their storage room after the flying bison had escaped the Fire Nation circus. The farmer became frightened, attempting to ward the startled beast away with a pitchfork. His wife brought a small torch with her, which terrified Appa due to his pyrophobia. Appa subsequently destroyed the store room in his panic and flew away, leaving the couple dazed.

While hardworking, the couple was somewhat humorless and superstitious. As such, their fun-loving neighbors liked to tease them with the occasional crop circle or a dead bird in the well.

entities.name: Fat
entities.description:
Fat came to Piandao many years before Sokka's visit and proved his worth by cooking him a delicious dinner. Piandao trained Fat in exchange for some good, home-cooked grub, and the two have been together at Piandao's castle ever since.

Upon Sokka's arrival at Piandao's doorstep, Fat warned him that Piandao was notorious for turning nearly every aspiring student down. After Sokka subsequently failed to procure a token that would prove his worth, Fat was skeptical that the young Water Tribe warrior would be allowed to train at the estate, though granted him access to the castle nonetheless in order to face Piandao. He was present when Piandao agreed to train Sokka and subsequently became the young man's training partner, easily overpowering and humiliating him in their earlier battles. When Sokka's training led him to rearrange the courtyard of the castle, Fat became upset at the considerable mess Sokka made. As Sokka's training neared its end, Fat was bested by Sokka in a one-on-one sword fighting match. Although he was less than pleased with being beaten by the young man, Fat held no grudge and aided Sokka in the procurement of pieces of meteorite to forge the latter's sword with.

When Sokka and his friends were leaving, Fat stopped them just outside the castle gate, saying that Piandao had sent him a gift to remember him by. He handed Sokka a small sack, inside of which was a white lotus Pai Sho tile, and bowed respectfully before returning inside.

Fat was a disgruntled, no-nonsense type of person. He took things very seriously, and was very loyal and obedient to Piandao.

entities.name: Father Glowworm
entities.description:
Father Glowworm is an ancient spirit, far older than other beings such as Koh, who was already immeasurably old. Possessing the power to create rifts between the spirit and physical worlds, it proceeded to cross over to the latter to prey on humans so it could feast on their blood. It would subsume the physical bodies of its prey, leaving only its victims' teeth behind, which would linger in the prehensile slime it produced. To avoid drawing attention, Father Glowworm only emerged in remote locations for limited periods of time. As a consequence of its actions, dark spirits influenced primarily by the pro-human actions of Avatar Yangchen used its rifts to cross over, something which did not bother it.

At some point, these incursions caught the attention of Avatar Kuruk, who began to combat the dark spirits at the cost of his own deep spiritual corruption. Eventually, Kuruk managed to find a spirit who pointed him in the direction of Father Glowworm. Upon being confronted, the Avatar made the mistake of trading names with it, sealing a curse upon anyone who knew of the spirit's existence. In their ensuing battle, though Father Glowworm proved stronger, Kuruk was too stubborn to give up and eventually the former was forced to retreat severely weakened and unable to threaten the physical world for a generation or two.

At some point prior to 296 BG, Father Glowworm had met Jianzhu, whom it later referred to as the "architect". They met again that year when the earthbending master asked Father Glowworm whether Kyoshi or Yun was the Avatar. Being able to sense the Avatar's spirit due to its past confrontation with Kuruk, the spirit knew that one of the children had to be the Avatar. Still, Father Glowworm was amused that the physical world was in a poor enough state for Jianzhu to even have to ask and told him that it would need blood in return for its help.

When Jianzhu agreed, Father Glowworm pointed to Kyoshi with a tendril, identifying her as the true Avatar, and coiled another tendril around Yun. Father Glowworm became furious when Jianzhu subsequently attacked it with a wall of earth, which enabled him and Kyoshi to escape from the cave, Father Glowworm and the young earthbender consequently ended up in the Spirit World, where Yun attempted to appease the spirit and convince it to become his teacher in hopes of finding a way back to the mortal world. Despite seeing through Yun's ruse, Father Glowworm initially humored him by accepting the human's compliments. As soon as the earthbender was getting a bit more hopeful, however, the spirit cruelly told him that he was nothing, and not even worth conversing with. Although there would be no escape for Yun, Father Glowworm promised that part of him would achieve immortality by being subsumed into the spirit. Father Glowworm subsequently attacked Yun to feed on his blood.

entities.name: Feishan
entities.description:
Despite these positive traits, however, Feishan was also a brutal, often arbitrary, and extremely paranoid monarch who was infamous for massacring perceived enemies and his willingness to plunge the four nations into chaos if his authority was threatened. His response to foreign intervention during a rebellion directly led to a fundamental shift in international relations during the Platinum Affair, resulting in great tensions and the emergence of the shang system.

Feishan was born in the late era of Szeto. When Feishan was still a quite young monarch, he faced a rebellion from General Nong, who sought to depose him and become the next Earth King. Neither side wanted to throw away their chances for success in a single moment, and so their forces danced around each other, prolonging the war. At this time, Avatar Yangchen was still a young child in the care of the nuns at the Western Air Temple.

Possibly influenced by the Order of the White Lotus, the leadership of the Fire Nation and Water Tribes lost patience, and conspired in secret to back Nong over Feishan, while keeping up a pretense of friendliness toward both sides. They loaned funds to the Earth King in the form of paper banknotes, hoping the loyalist soldiers would lose confidence in the king's ability to pay them with only written promises. Meanwhile, they sent Nong ingots of platinum, an extremely valuable currency. However, Feishan found the strategic moment he had been waiting for, and fell upon Nong at Llamapaca's Crossing, wiping his enemy off the face of the map.

Though Feishan would have liked to wage war against the Fire Nation and Water Tribes for their involvement in Nong's rebellion, he recognized that his military was weak due to the civil war. He thus opted for another form of vengeance: In retribution for what his fellow heads of state had done, he closed his nation's ports, cut off diplomatic communication, and expelled ambassadors from his land. He kept the captured platinum, melting it down and using it to plate the giant badgermole statue behind his throne, declaring that diplomatic relations would return to normal once the entire surface fully tarnished and appeared as stone, which would be approximately a century or even longer. The Fire Nation and Water Tribes responded by announcing their own states of isolation. However, Feishan and his court still desired luxury goods from abroad, and there was money to be made from Earth Kingdom exports. As a result, the Earth King, Fire Lord Gonryu, and Chief Oyaluk of the Water Tribes agreed to restrict trade to four cities to handle controlled amounts of international trade. The overall incident had become known as the Platinum Affair.

entities.name: Female prison guard
entities.description:
Shortly after Sokka and Zuko infiltrated the Boiling Rock posing as guards, the latter made his way to the prison's lounge. There, the female guard and two other guards were eating at a table, one of them telling Zuko to take off his helmet and relax. He replied that if there was an incident he could be struck in the head and the guards laughed. The female guard said he will loosen up after a week and Zuko inquired whether he could ask them a question. She dismissively told him he cannot date the female guards and one of her colleagues jokingly assured the disguised prince that he would not want to. She threw a cup at the man in anger, hitting him in the head, while the other guard at the table laughed. Zuko proceeded to ask them if war prisoners were brought to the Boiling Rock.

Later, Sokka and Zuko got to the cell where Suki was being held. Sokka went inside to talk to her, while Zuko stood watch at the door to let them know if actual prison guards arrived there. The female prison guard came and told Zuko she needed to enter the cell. He attempted to stall her until Sokka got out, telling her that the prisoner could sneak up on her while the lights were off. However, she told him to step aside and, when she was about to shove him, Zuko grabbed her arm and slammed her into the door. She also pushed him back against the door as they began a scuffle. Sokka exited the cell and the guard asked him to help her, but Sokka hesitated, unsure of how to react, until he knocked Zuko to the ground, whispering that he will figure out a plan. She and Sokka then proceeded to take the prince to another cell.

After Zuko was taken to a cooler because he firebent and Sokka went to free him, they hid inside the small chamber as the female guard and another guard passed by, discussing the arrival of new inmates. She asked the man if anyone interesting would be brought to the Boiling Rock and, among other people, he said that war prisoners would also be detained there. Zuko and Sokka listened to their conversation, thinking that the latter's father could also be one of those prisoners.

When Sokka went to talk to Zuko again, now imprisoned in a standard cell, and let him know about the escape plan Hakoda and him had come up with, the female guard and a colleague walked there and she said they had orders from the warden to take Zuko somewhere else. Sokka lied that he wanted ten seconds to beat up the prince, to which she agreed as she folded her arms and smiled. He went inside and told Zuko the plan before she and the other guard took Zuko to a cell where Mai was waiting for him.

entities.name: Feng
entities.description:
Feng was working at the Jasmine Dragon after the Hundred Year War, and Iroh came to rely on her as his primary helper at the tea shop. One day, she was getting tired past closing when she was tending to Li-Mei, the last customer of the day. Iroh noticed her exhaustion and told her to go home and rest, or see the city's nightlife if she preferred, offering to take over from her. Feng thanked Iroh before leaving for home.

Later, Feng told Iroh that Li-Mei had returned to the shop. She went to bring the customer a set of tea, but was tripped up by the spirits hiding in the tea shop, and apologized to Li-Mei for the mistake. The customer told her not to worry, and simply asked if she was alright. Iroh approached her, telling her to accept mistakes, and asked her to take a break. A while later, she told Iroh that Li-Mei wanted more tea. After Iroh asked Li-Mei to accompany him to dinner, he went to close up, but Feng smiled, telling Iroh that she could handle the shop for the rest of the night. Iroh thanked her, telling Feng that she was a kind and lovely young lady.

Over the following time, Feng started to notice that the Jasmine Dragon's supply of tea was becoming irregular, as their merchants of choice had difficulties in replenishing their stock. She spoke to other tea shop owners around Ba Sing Se, learning that these suffered from the same issue. One day, Feng was present when an anti-Iroh protestor started to make a ruckus outside the Jasmine Dragon. At Iroh's suggestion, the waitress delivered a cup of tea to the protestor, yet the man threw the drink to the ground in his fury. Afterward, a group of angry customers rallied and drove the protestor away. In the evening, Feng again checked the Jasmine Dragon's tea supplies, and informed Iroh that they were low on all blends due to the continuing delivery irregularities. The older man promised to take care of the problem, and he subsequently restored the regular tea supply during a small adventure.

Six months later, Feng assisted Iroh in presenting the Jasmine Dragon's newest tea blends whose ingredients had been supplied by June, the shop's newest employee.

entities.name: Fengying
entities.description:
Fengying was originally a member of the Fire Nation military, serving for an extended time and becoming a "veteran". Conversely, she grew increasingly disillusioned with the Fire Nation's leadership and became opposed to traditional aristocratic power structures. Eventually, she left the military and found solace by joining the Guiding Wind, a group originally founded by Air Nomads under Khandro, who sought to end the dominance of nobles and the wealthy across the world. Fengying became a valuable member of the movement, as few suspected an ex-soldier to work with pacifist airbenders. Accordingly, she could carry out missions for the Guiding Wind without raising too much attention.

At one point, Fengying met and befriended a Jasmine Islander named Tsenten who had already forged good relations with Khandro. Eventually she also encountered a young firebender named Sukaya, taking her under her wing and teaching her. Fengying subsequently recommended Sukaya to a Fire Nation military academy to further hone her skills, earning the young girl's lasting gratitude.

In the 50s BG, Tsenten - by then a member of the Jasmine Island Council - asked for the Guiding Wind's aid. The councilman suspected that the local Earth Kingdom civilian representative, Magistrate Emerald, was engaged in illegal operations. His friends Fengying and Sakuru eagerly responded to the request. Both regarded Emerald as the kind of pro-monarchy figure who they had sworn to oppose.

Upon arriving on Jasmine Island, the two Guiding Wind members managed to infiltrate the local Earth Kingdom outpost, where they discovered evidence not just about corruption but a creeping coup covertly led by Emerald. Before Fengying and Sakuru could escape, the two were caught by the magistrate's guards. Having no intention to allow the revolutionaries to go free with the knowledge of his activities, Emerald subsequently declared them criminals and argued that they should be brought before a court in the Earth Kingdom; thus, he would win time and minimize the chances of a fair trial. Meanwhile, Emerald threw Fengying and Sakuru into a prison located under the Earth Kingdom outpost, allocating them to the "toughest" cells specifically outfitted to prevent their escape. Fengying's cell was filled with straw which would ignite and burn her alive or suffocate her if she attempted to firebend. Despite their harsh imprisonment, they were treated with respect by Buo Ren, the head of the local Earth Kingdom Army garrison.

The captain was rendered immobile after Toph used metalbending to slam him onto the roof.

entities.name: Fire Nation bar patron
entities.description:
One summer day, this man decided to stop at a Fire Nation bar with his friend, where he attempted to ride the mechanical komodo rhino. He was left disoriented, however, rendering him in need of assistance from his friend in order to dismount. He subsequently watched as Katara, disguised as a boy, attempted to ride it and warned her to hold on with both hands, but she did not listen and was thrown off the rhino as well.

Katara was thrown into his friend, who yelled at her in anger. Katara called his friend a "toothpick", angering the Fire Nation bar patron. Katara nearly began a fight with him and his friend, but was dragged off by Toph, much to his and his friend's enjoyment.

entities.name: Fire Nation councilwoman
entities.description:
During the meeting at City Hall where Tarrlok suggested creating a task force to deal with Amon, the councilwoman stated that she was inclined to agree, but was skeptical as to whether they would find someone willing to command the task force. Tarrlok subsequently volunteered for the job, so she and all other council members, excluding Tenzin, voted for the creation of the force.

After Amon made a threat on the Pro-bending Arena, the Council decided to cancel the tournament finals. After some persuasion by Chief Lin Beifong, however, the councilwoman, along with all of the other Council members besides Tenzin, voted in favor of keeping the arena open.

Following Lin Beifong's resignation as Chief of Police, Saikhan was appointed the new Chief, and the Fire Nation councilwoman, along with all of the other members of the Council, was present at his induction ceremony. Later on, when Tarrlok proposed that a law be created which would set a curfew for nonbenders and make it illegal for anyone to join the Equalists, the Fire Nation councilwoman voted in favor of the idea.

The Fire Nation councilwoman was present at City Hall on the day after Tarrlok and Avatar Korra's battle. Upon the arrival of Tenzin, Lin, and Team Avatar, the council page revealed that Tarrlok was a bloodbender, and that he had kidnapped Korra. The Northern Water Tribe representative, exposed as a criminal and outnumbered, began to bloodbend the entire group, including the councilwoman, until they were rendered incapacitated.

entities.name: Fire Nation drill sergeant
entities.description:
The drill sergeant quickly targeted Sokka after his fake beard fell off, saying that he was "going to watch him like an eagle-hawk". He ordered him to demonstrate riding a komodo rhino and became disgusted upon witnessing Sokka fail miserably.

When this officer handed out the uniforms to the recruits, Sokka was given a uniform that was too large. When Sokka commented on that, the sergeant remarked that "maybe [Sokka was] just too small". When Sokka stumbled, he ripped off the sergeant's sash displaying his badges, causing him to grow angry. He forced Sokka to run with a moo-sow while following him on a komodo rhino, do push-ups in the rain with the moo-sow on his back, and clean the restroom and the stalls of the hybrid pigs.

The next day, he went to the barracks and noticed that Sokka had disappeared. Following an unsuccessful camp-wide search, he declared Sokka a criminal, and he and his company went after him.

He came upon the cave where Sokka, Katara, Aang, Appa, and Toph were hiding out. Sokka emerged from the cave and noticed the sergeant and several soldiers, along with two rhinos. The sergeant dragged Sokka out of the cave to face justice; however, before this could be done, Sokka claimed that he had discovered earthbending and waterbending spies attempting to infiltrate the Fire Nation, and whom he had tracked to the cave. The sergeant was initially skeptical, but was soon convinced upon witnessing Toph, Aang, and Katara bending. He allowed Sokka to go into the cave and confront the benders, calling him a brave soldier.
