entities.name: Jeong Jeong
entities.description:
Jeong Jeong was born in the Fire Nation in 39 AG. One of his students was Zhao, a young man who had been thrown out of his parents' home and feigned interest in Jeong Jeong's teachings about discipline. Believing Zhao's words were honest, Jeong Jeong taught Zhao powerful offensive firebending techniques, but when the older man tried to convey the bending art's dangers as well as the necessity of restraint, the student revealed his true nature. Seeing how Zhao was solely regarding firebending as a way to destroy his opponents and a pathway to gain power, the admiral refused to continue his teachings. Afterward, the young man left to join the Fire Army.

Though Zhao proved to be Jeong Jeong's most destructive student, several of his pupils caused great suffering during the Hundred Year War. After many years of watching his students wage war and cause destruction, Jeong Jeong began to question his own teachings. At some point, he joined the international Order of the White Lotus.

In 89 AG, Jeong Jeong deserted the Fire Nation Navy and vowed never to teach firebending again. he was officially declared to be the first deserter of the Fire Nation military. Under constant pursuit by the military, he was forced to move from place to place, never settling in one area for more than a season. Years after his defection, Jeong Jeong came in contact with Lin Yee's tribe in the northwestern Earth Kingdom, and was declared a living god. They offered him residence at a small camp, where he stayed during the winter. Around 96 AG, another Fire Nation deserter, Chey, joined Jeong Jeong's group and tried to learn from the ex-admiral.

When Avatar Aang's return became known, Jeong Jeong forbade his followers from contacting him. Despite this, Chey brought the Avatar to Jeong Jeong's camp so that he could learn firebending in 99 AG. Jeong Jeong was furious, since it was clear to him that Aang was not interested in learning discipline, and had not learned waterbending or earthbending. He said that because Aang had not learned how to master these elements, he lacked the disciplinary principles which would aid him in controlling the power of firebending, and thus refused to even see him. Defiantly, Aang sought out Jeong Jeong in a small hut, where he was meditating surrounded by candles sitting before a dead tree.

entities.name: Jesa
entities.description:
Over time, Jesa became one of the most renowned daofei outlaws in the Earth Kingdom, and along with Hark led her criminal organization to great successes. The two reduced their activities following the birth of their daughter Kyoshi, though they eventually left her in the care of villagers at Yokoya. Jesa eventually died of fever, and Kyoshi would come to use her metal fans to enhance her own bending.

Jesa was born in the Eastern Air Temple, and showed great promise as a bender. She earned her arrows and became an airbending master while still young, and was highly regarded among the Air Nomads. All that changed, however, when she met a young earthbender and thief named Hark during a journey through the Earth Kingdom. He convinced Jesa to join him for one of his criminal schemes, and as it turned out, she greatly enjoyed this kind of adventure. After a short time, she went rogue, became a full-time criminal, and fell in love with Hark.

Disavowing the traditional Air Nomad lifestyle, she tattooed snakes over her airbender arrows, quickly became infamous in the underworld, and rose to the de facto head of the Flying Opera Company, Using her sky bison, Longyan, Jesa and Hark's underground network became very influential and powerful, even able to force Earth Kingdom officials to do their bidding. For her crimes, the Air Nomads considered her one of the greatest disgraces to their culture in recent memory. Over time, Jesa's airbending powers weakened; she believed that this was related to her abandoning a spiritual lifestyle and turning to a materialistic existence full of violence and greed. To compensate, she crafted a pair of metal fans to enhance her lessening airbending abilities.

In 312 BG, she gave birth to a daughter, Kyoshi. Jesa and Hark consequently decided to mostly quit their large-scale criminal activities; they did not explain the reason for this decision to their associates. The small family consequently traveled through the entire Earth Kingdom, never staying in one place for a long time. When Kyoshi was about five or six, however, Jesa and Hark left her in the village of Yokoya in the care of a local villager. Jesa gave her daughter her fans as well as a journal she had written before departing.

entities.name: Jet
entities.description:
When Jet was only eight years old, he witnessed his parents' deaths at the hands of the Fire Nation soldiers known as the Rough Rhinos. Jet grew up to become a hook sword-wielding vigilante, possessing a burning hatred for the Fire Nation and going to extreme lengths to exact his revenge, even to the point of endangering civilian lives in a raid on a small Fire Nation-occupied Earth Kingdom town.

Jet disbanded the Freedom Fighters after an encounter with Team Avatar and, together with Longshot and Smellerbee, decided to start a new life in Ba Sing Se. When he tried to expose Prince Zuko and Iroh as firebenders, the Dai Li arrested and brainwashed him into submission.

A second encounter with the Avatar and his friends revealed to Jet the truth about the Dai Li, and he helped them find Appa by leading them to Lake Laogai, the Dai Li headquarters. There, Jet was fatally wounded by Long Feng when he overcame the hypnosis placed upon him.

The young vigilante Jet held a deep-seated grudge against the Fire Nation because of an attack by the Rough Rhinos, who killed his parents and burned his village, Bihou, to the ground. From that day on, he despised the Fire Nation and dedicated his life to stopping them any way he could, even at the cost of innocent lives.

entities.name: Jetsun
entities.description:
While Jetsun and Yangchen were not related by blood (at least any closer than fourth or fifth cousins), Jetsun was like an older sister to her, cutting up fruit in a stupid way and giving her the symmetrical pieces, and showing her no mercy on the airball court. Jetsun had strong spiritual abilities, and had been able to cross over into the Spirit World.

Once, Jetsun witnessed her having an episode where she recalled Mesose from her past lives. Not being able to stand the screams, she sped through the temple to help out, and navigated her way around without using her glider. Jetsun helped Librarian Tsering to search the Great Library for the name, even though they were not fully sure who or what Mesose was. She found the book she was looking for and took it to Yangchen in the infirmary, and began to read aloud the scholarly works of Mesose, a companion to Avatar Gun.

Jetsun eventually guided Yangchen into the Spirit World for the first time, and went to a meditation circle in the meadows above the temple cliffs for their attempt. Abbess Dagmola and Librarian Tsering came along, but deferred to Jetsun as a guide. As soon as they began meditating, Yangchen quickly crossed over into the Spirit World with Jetsun, the latter of whom praised Yangchen for being able to pull it off on her first try. While Jetsun at first explained that mere existence was the "great lesson" of the Spirit World, she enthusiastically agreed to explore her surroundings with Yangchen.

Jetsun and Yangchen walked together into a lonesome forest, and came upon a group of shishi. Yangchen had frozen in place, which puzzled Jetsun, as her sister had always loved animals. However, the shishi were actually sensing the fear of another past Avatar, and began to turn dark. Jetsun told Yangchen that she could wake up, as the shishi began to gather in a hunting formation. Jetsun grabbed Yangchen, tossed her over her shoulder, and ran, as her sister regressed to a younger version of herself. She ran to a brook which soon turned to a raging river. She told Yangchen that she would not wake up before the Avatar, and ripped her orange shawl and wrapped it around Yangchen, throwing her into the air and shouting at her to wake up. While Yangchen was able to make it back to the physical world, Jetsun could not.

entities.name: Jia
entities.description:
A native of Jasmine Island, Jia was still a child when the Fire Nation military invaded her homeland and caused large-scale destruction. Her apartment building was set on fire during the fighting, but it was saved by her cousin Thaki's waterbending. Afterward, Jia became Thaki's ward until she was old enough to care for herself.

By Jia's young adulthood, the Hundred Year War had ended, but Jasmine Island became subject to a political crisis. As a new election was scheduled, various factions began to bitterly feud over their homeland's future direction. Jia joined one group, the isolationist and highly traditionalist Antiquarians. She quickly became an avid reader of the group's extensive library, focusing on wartime literature. These books alongside the Antiquarians' beliefs caused Jia to become increasingly militant in her worldview, seeing outsiders as a constant threat. She came to the conclusion that Jasmine Island had to prepare itself for armed conflict with other powers, further radicalizing her. Jia called on her party leader Yan to support the bolstering of Jasmine Island's defenses, Over time, she became a prominent figure within the Antiquarians.

Eventually, tensions on Jasmine Island further escalated when someone stole a bag of golden jasmine seeds from the yearly harvest, a symbolically potent and disruptive action. A team of protectors, including Jia's cousin Thaki alongside Ganzaya, Kim Jin, Kosui, and Zo, visited the Antiquarians' headquarters which was located in a museum. Upon their arrival, Jia offered them a tour, using the opportunity to talk about the threat posed by the Fire Nation and the Earth Kingdom. She also voiced suspicions about foreign agents being responsible for the theft.

Consumed by her party's ideas and the writings of wartime authors, Jia became a martial person who regarded even peaceful politics as a game of "strategy and positioning", describing diplomatic missions as "incursions" or "reconnaissance".

entities.name: Jialun
entities.description:
In the previous era of the Avatar, Kyoshi had shaped bureaucratic policies to aid the poorest of the kingdom, strengthened ties between the disparate states, and drafted a constitution with the 46th Earth King. Although Kyoshi had passed away, the peace and prosperity from her Era was maintained by the Earth Sages, who had regained the trust of the people and had a reputation as wise advisors and academics. They were confident in speaking out against the Earth King, and criticized Jialun when he began to twist the kingdom's constitution for his own benefit.

Jialun also became opposed to Queen Guo Xun of Omashu, a successful subordinate monarch who was steadily expanding her power across the western Earth Kingdom. Uncaring that Guo Xun's successes also strengthened the entire Earth Kingdom, the Earth King saw her as a potential rival and plotted her destruction. In 63 BG, Jialun attempted to undermine Guo Xun by helping to orchestrate a plot between Ba Sing Se's peace minister, Pushi, and Omashu's peace minister, Huaji. The objective was to poison the citizens of Omashu through its water supply with components of the Lambak mineral, the latter stolen from the Fire Nation. Jialun desired instability so he could consolidate his power over the Earth Kingdom, potentially using Huaji as a figurehead Omashu monarch. and Ta Min exposed Jialun's plans to Guo Xun. A bitter rivalry thus began to erupt between Ba Sing Se and Omashu.

Frustrated over the continued criticism by the Earth Sages, Jialun eventually orchestrated the Night of Silenced Sages. He had the Dai Li arrest every single Earth Sage across his kingdom. The temples were closed, and those who searched for the sages ended up disappearing. Eventually, the temples reopened as Royal Learning Halls, with any remaining sages becoming Grand Lectors, tightly controlled by the crown and forced to never speak of the sages again. Avatar Roku was still a young man at this time, who had only begun his journey to master the four elements, and was in no position to respond to such an event at the time. Jialun succeeded in quashing organized outspoken internal opposition, though his actions attracted the ire of many sympathetic to the sages, including Queen Guo Xun. The monarchs of Ba Sing Se and Omashu further intensified their rivalry: both monarchs had spies in each other's courts, and both throne rooms became vipers' nests.

Following the purge of the sages, Jialun further manipulated the Earth Kingdom's political system to his benefit, and portrayed himself as incompetent, which was entirely to his design.

entities.name: Jiang
entities.description:
After many years on the force, Jiang discovered his airbending abilities after Harmonic Convergence, and briefly spent some time studying at Air Temple Island. However, his short fuse and struggled with patience led to his rapid departure, and he continued to work as a detective for the Republic City Police.

Jiang lost everything in the wake of Kuvira's spirit cannon, as he was separated from his family during the evacuation of Republic City. His home was destroyed by the cannon blasts and there were no reports of his husband or children, leading him to presume that they had been taken from him.

After spirit energy canisters went missing from Juniper Kim's laboratory, Jiang took the case into his own hands, with his personal motto being that it was better to ask for forgiveness than permission.

Jiang was always a man of action, but he became more jaded and more willing to break the rules to get results than ever after losing everything. He could easily fly off the handle if provoked or if he saw an opening. While Jiang was still cunning and clever in his middle age, he could let his hot head and recent emotional trauma get the better of him very easily.
entities.short_description: As a member of the Earth Kingdom's daofei, Jiang descended from a long line of river pirates who made their living raiding using the sailing ship Flying Wolfbat. She grew up on the river rather than any settlement and…

entities.name: Jianjun
entities.description:
Jianjun was a Fire National, but spent a substantial part of her youth in the Earth Kingdom. As a result, she had an innate understanding of many Earth Kingdom traditions. After reaching adulthood, she enlisted in the Fire Army and was accepted into the personal guard of General Uyanga, As a result of her duties, she spent much time with her superior's family and became the protector of Uyanga's young son. Seeing him grow up and growing close to him, Jianjun began to regard the boy as a surrogate son.

Her life greatly changed when Haoran's insurgents attacked Uyanga's estate, partially collapsing it. Jianjun was at the side of Uyanga's son at the time of the attack, and the two were trapped under rubble together. Whereas the soldier was left emotionally scarred, the boy was heavily injured. When Uyanga subsequently declared her intention to hunt and destroy Haoran's rebels at all costs, Jianjun volunteered to aid this mission to avenge her ward's suffering.

As a result of her skills at manipulation, Jianjun was sent out as a spy to find the insurgents. She soon managed to discover that the militants had linked up with a group of refugees at Maizu Village. There, Jianjun spread the rumor that a Fire Nation attack was imminent, causing a panic as the civilians ran for safety. Amid this chaos, the spy joined the refugees' ranks and began traveling with them as well as Haoran's rebels. Leaving coded messages behind, she allowed Uyanga's troops to trail them. The general chased the mixed Earth Kingdom group over the next month. Though she gradually realized that endangering the refugees during this hunt was morally questionable, Jianjun continued to do her duty until the refugees and rebels sought safety at the abandoned Western Air Temple.

Once at the air temple, Jianjun began to sabotage various exits, seeking to hinder the movement of the Earth Kingdom rebels and refugees as well as give Uyanga's troops more time to arrive. Most importantly, she managed to destroy an elevator and tunnel which presented the easiest entryways into the structure through explosives. Yet her activities were noticed by a refugee, Woong, and an insurgent, Xinyan; to distract them, she blamed the explosions on the activities of a local spirit named Tien.

entities.name: Jianzhu
entities.description:
Jianzhu was an Earth Sage, earthbending master, and one of the world's leading politicians during the late 4th and early 3rd century BG. At the peak of his power, he was the de facto ruler of most of the Earth Kingdom, though his power was constantly challenged by political rivals.

Having been Avatar Kuruk's close friend and later earthbending teacher, Jianzhu felt responsible for his friend's premature death due to his lack of guidance. In addition, the search for Kuruk's successor proved futile for several years, while the world increasingly descended into chaos. Fueled by guilt and a desire to restore what he regarded as balance, Jianzhu stepped in and assumed many traditional duties of the Avatar. With the aid of his old friend Kelsang, he forged a large network of allies and destroyed many rebel and bandit groups that had grown in power. Over time, his methods to maintain balance became more and more extreme to the point where he was willing to sacrifice anyone to achieve his goals. Eventually, Jianzhu identified a boy named Yun as Avatar and began to rigorously train him.

This endeavor proved futile, however, as Yun was eventually proven to be a regular earthbender, whereas a servant girl named Kyoshi was the true Avatar. In a desperate attempt to gain control of Kyoshi and train her to become the perfect Avatar, Jianzhu sacrificed his pupil Yun and murdered his friend Kelsang. When she escaped, Jianzhu mobilized all his resources to hunt her down. In the process, he murdered both a large number of leading Earth Sages as well as Kyoshi's friend Lek. Jianzhu finally met his end when he confronted and dueled Kyoshi, but was interrupted and killed by a returned Yun.

In his testament, Jianzhu bequeathed all his wealth to Kyoshi and vouched for her good name - his final attempt to shape her according to his ideals. Overall, Jianzhu greatly influenced Kyoshi, and she adopted some of his beliefs, though outright rejected others.

entities.name: Jiawei
entities.description:
Formerly a member of the Equalists, Jiawei's activities in the organization led to him losing his left forearm and being sent to prison. Pakuk, the Vice-President of Cabbage Corp, pulled some strings to get him released, leading Jiawei to become indebted to the former. At some point, Jiawei designed and built a prosthetic to replace the forearm he had lost.

After being released from prison, Jiawei was sent by Pakuk to infiltrate Prosthetist of Tin Town. Desiring to build a mecha fabrication base in the Republic City underground, Pakuk entrusted Jiawei with staging natural disasters that would motivate the town's residents to leave, allowing Cabbage Corp to purchase the space. Posing as a doctor, Jiawei built high-quality prosthetics for the town's residents, as many of them had disabilities similar to his own. At night, he would perform acts of sabotage against the town's infrastructure.

Jiawei was soft-spoken, and kept a low profile due to his status as a spy. However, he was still a compassionate individual, and did his best to ensure that no one was injured as a result of his acts of sabotage.

Jiawei was a skilled mechanic, engineer, and doctor. He built a prosthetic in order to replace his left forearm, and later built similar prosthetics for the resident of Tin Town while he was undercover there. He wore a specialty toolbelt to aid him in his acts of sabotage.
entities.short_description: Formerly a member of the Equalists, Jiawei's activities in the organization led to him losing his left forearm and being sent to prison. Pakuk, the Vice-President of Cabbage Corp, pulled some strings to get him…

entities.name: Jie
entities.description:
At some point, Jie rose to become the leader of the Denied and learnt that an ancient Avatar named Sonam had possessed the power to gift bending abilities by using an empowered staff.

Around 110 AG, Jie and her comrades tracked down a statuette of Sonam which contained a map, leading to the location of Sonam's staff. Yet the item was also discovered by Avatar Aang who was ignorant of its potential importance and brought it to a sanctuary inside one of the Southern Air Temple's towers. Jie and her followers Kallik, Hong, and Yuddah ambushed Avatar Aang at the temple, seeking to steal the statuette. Though Hong managed to take the item, it was quickly reclaimed by the Avatar. The Denied kept battling Aang until Jie became impatient and shot an explosive arrow at her opponent, seeking to kill him. However, the attack destabilized the entire tower. Amid the chaos, Aang was knocked out while saving Kallik's life. Furthermore, Sonam's statuette broke and Kallik was able to take the map within.

As Jie, Kallik, Hong and Yuddah rushed back to their airship waiting outside, the collapsing tower's upper half threatened to fall onto the vessel. Yet Aang awakened and entered the Avatar State, earthbending the tower back into place, letting Jie and her group get away.

With the map in their hands, Jie and her followers traveled across the Endless Ocean to snatch Sonam's staff. During the voyage, Kallik spotted the Avatar and the Fire Lord's airship through a telescope. Jie promptly ordered her forces to launch a surprise attack to kill their opponents. When Kallik questioned the order by pointing out how the Avatar had saved her life, Jie angrily reprimanded the younger woman by pointing out that the Avatar had failed them all and they had to gain bending powers at all costs.
entities.short_description: At some point, Jie rose to become the leader of the Denied and learnt that an ancient Avatar named Sonam had possessed the power to gift bending abilities by using an empowered staff.

entities.name: Jin
entities.description:
Her life was further disrupted when the Fire Nation conquered Ba Sing Se, whereupon Jin and her associates went underground and participated in operations against the occupation forces. Having helped to rescue Susu in a daring mission at the Earth Kingdom Royal Palace, Jin ultimately acted as one of the Silver Fangs coordinators of a mass uprising during the liberation of Ba Sing Se in summer 100 AG.

Jin was born into the Guan family Her mother Biyu was an earthbending worker as well as soldier, while her father was a scholar who served as Daying's magistrate. Though they struggled most of their lives, Jin's parents were strong and able to provide for their family;

Around 97 AG, the Fire Nation military attacked Daying. Jin's mother was one of the earliest victims, being killed alongside the rest of the village's soldiers in an ambush. As the Fire Army stormed Daying, her father sent her away under Gong-gong's protection; her father subsequently went missing, and was believed dead. Even as their home burned behind them, Gong-gong brought Jin to safety and they joined a group of refugees, moving toward Ba Sing Se. At a later point of their travels, Jin was almost killed by a falling tree, but barely saved by Gong-gong, though the old man was badly injured by the accident.

After finally crossing the West Lake, Meanwhile, Gong-gong forbade Jin from honing her earthbending skills, wanting her to avoid her mother's fate by not engaging in dangerous tasks. He continued to teach her calligraphy so that she could socially advance through education. Indeed, Jin's skills were noticed at a Lower Ring school and she managed to get a scholarship for a literature academy.

entities.name: Jin Bo
entities.description:
Jin Bo was born into the influential Jin family on Jasmine Island, a small, independent state. At one point, he began to investigate his homeland's culture as a hobby. His work expanded and eventually became a major effort, making him quite respected among his compatriots for his tireless activities and great love for Jasmine Island. Eventually, the state's leadership officially recognized him by naming him a magistrate of arts and culture, turning his hobby into a profession.

Being a popular figure, various people suggested to Jin Bo that he should stand in the elections for the island's ruling council, but he always declined. As he was solely devoted to his work on cultural history, he argued that this would have made him a "one topic councilmember", completely unsuited to politics.

In the early 90s AG, Jasmine Island became subject to a brutal Fire Nation invasion, later dubbed "The Devastation" by the locals. The Fire Nationals wrought great destruction, indiscriminately burning, looting, and killing. Amid this chaos, Jin Bo desperately attempted to save as many documents, art, artefacts, and other important cultural as well as historical items, believing that the loss of the local culture would greatly harm the very "soul of the island". He specifically asked them to venture to a number of locations, rescuing artisan scrolls on pottery techniques used for locally unique teapots, decades-old notes about golden jasmine tea production, and a number of remembrance statues.

entities.name: Jin Wei
entities.description:
It is unclear at which point the feud between the Gan Jin and Zhang truly started. The two tribes were already hostile toward each other by the early 3rd century BG,

The Gan Jins have believed for one hundred years that during the process of this ritual when Jin Wei was approaching the western post of their tribe with the sacred orb, a man from the Zhang tribe, called Wei Jin, knocked him out and stole the orb. According to legend, this event started the tribal feud between the Zhang and the Gan Jin.

The Zhang thought for a hundred years that Wei Jin was traveling the country when he stumbled upon a man of the Gan Jin tribe. The Zhang stated that he tried to tend to the man's wounds, but Jin Wei insisted he finish the ritual and carry the orb to the West post instead of caring for him. As believed, Wei Jin did what he said, but as he approached the western post, he was arrested by other Gan Jin warriors for stealing the orb and sentenced to twenty years in prison without being thanked for his selfless deeds as the Zhang stated.

Avatar Aang, upon hearing the names of the two tribes' ancestors, revealed that he knew them and that they were twins. He recounted the true events of the supposed incident, explaining that when they were eight, they played a game called "Redemption". Jin Wei was running with the ball when he fell, so Wei Jin picked it up and started running to the other end of the field. However, he stepped out of bounds and was put in the penalty box for two minutes. Finally, the tribes made up and continued their journey to Ba Sing Se, the Earth Kingdom capital, together, followed by the canyon guide. Aang later revealed to Sokka and Katara that the story was completely fictional.

entities.name: Jing
entities.description:
Jing grew up darting in and out of the halls of Ba Sing Se University among people who were much older, but only half as brilliant as her. When she was not studying, Jing's brilliant mind designed all manner of wondrous draughts, tinctures, and potions.

Jing sold her inventions for fun, but when her mixtures ended up in the hands of some (well-paying) criminals, the city guards came along after Jing promised to keep her inventions out of the criminal underworld. Jing ended up meeting a group of new friends: Tao, Masaru, Sarnai, and Quartz, and loved them all. She considered all of them to be a little bit broken, but she was determined to fix anything.

Jing had a heart of gold and was a very curious person, although she could also be stubborn.

Jing was a genius potion maker and considered to be more brilliant than many who were twice of age. She made use of her potions during fights by keeping them on a bandolier.

entities.name: Jingbo
entities.description:
After the end of the peace talks in Yu Dao following the end of the battle for Yu Dao, Jingbo attended the banquet in celebration of the city's newly elected coalition government, finding a seat with Yee-Li, Xing Ying, Sokka, Katara, and Toph Beifong. When Aang showed up later as well, Jingbo was excited be invited by Avatar to accompany him the following day on a field trip.

Like the other Air Acolytes, Jingbo was eager to learn more about Yangchen's Festival. When Toph refused to bow for the statue, which was the first part of the ceremony, and insulted the holiday, Aang taught Jingbo and the other Acolytes that true Air Nomads let insults pass them by in order to preserve inner peace. He did partake in the bowing ceremony and his excitement for the holiday's celebration only grew after that. Jingbo politely thanked Xing Ying for her offered helped, though rejected it, announcing it was his honor as a junior Air Acolyte to carry the festival supplies to the sacred meadow where they would enjoy a ceremonial meal.

Their walk led them toward a town that was built atop the sacred meadow, causing Jingbo to be equally distraught as Aang over the destruction of the peaceful place. When the group ventured through town, he followed Aang, Katara, and the other Air Acolytes toward a fenced-off area from which a repugnant smell arose. He was catapulted over the fence by Aang's earthbending and caught with his airbending, although he still landed on his back, the heavy backpack preventing the young boy from immediately getting back up. His predicament only worsened when four guards arrived and tried to expel them from the private grounds for trespassing. Aang used his airbending once more to blow the Air Acolytes out of harm's way when the guards attacked them with earthbending, causing Jingbo to be squished by his backpack. He was helped to his feet by his fellow Acolytes and subsequently received another lesson about Air Nomad tradition from Aang: avoid conflict unless absolutely necessary, and even then, contact should be kept to a minimum. Together with the other Acolytes, he applauded the Avatar for his demonstration of the lesson by using his airbending to let the attacking guards knock each other out. When Satoru arrived on the scene, Jingbo declined shaking his hand in greeting, though politely bowed his head in line with Air Nomad custom. He later attended a tour of the Earthen Fire Refinery with the others, though grew worried when Aang once again stared off in the distance to Yangchen's apparition, who was only visible to the Avatar, wondering if there was something he could do to help Aang.

entities.description:
Not long before Aang froze himself in an iceberg, he created and taught his peers a new airbending trick, the air scooter, which was a sphere of air upon which one could ride, and the other children soon created an accompanying game. When Aang asked to play, he was denied as the others felt that his being the Avatar would give his team an unfair advantage. As Aang left, Jinju was the last to be picked, though neither team showed interest.

entities.name: Jinora
entities.description:
Jinora was born to Tenzin and Pema in 160 AG on Air Temple Island. She grew up as one of only two airbenders in the world, until she was later joined by a sister, Ikki, when she was three, and a brother, Meelo, when she was five.

During the fall of 170 AG, Jinora and her family traveled on Oogi to the Southern Water Tribe compound to meet Korra, who was due to start her airbending training with Tenzin. Once they arrived, Jinora happily greeted her grandmother, Katara, and told her that she had been reading all about her old adventures and had been "dying" to ask her what happened to Zuko's mother. Katara began to explain, calling it "an incredible tale", but was interrupted by Ikki, which greatly annoyed Jinora. The next day, the ten-year-old and her family had to leave the South Pole to return to Air Temple Island, as Tenzin had only come to inform Korra about his duties in Republic City, which made it impossible for him and his family to stay at the compound.

After Avatar Korra ran away from her compound and traveled to Republic City, she finally convinced Tenzin to allow her stay on his island so he could teach her airbending. At this decision, Jinora and her siblings excitedly hugged Korra, celebrating her stay.

When Korra began her training, Jinora demonstrated the proper way to navigate through the spinning gates before speeding them up with a blast of air. She tried to offer advice to the Avatar, but ultimately Korra failed to make it to the other side. After destroying the training relic in a fit of frustration, the Avatar snapped at Tenzin, calling him a bad teacher and storming away. Jinora and Ikki responded by hugging and comforting their father as their little brother kicked around the charred and splintered remains of the gates, mimicking Korra.

entities.name: Jinpa
entities.description:
Becoming Kyoshi's secretary, Jinpa aided the Avatar on her quest to stabilize the four nations. Although badly wounded during Kyoshi's battle with Yun in Yokoya, Jinpa was successfully healed, and introduced to the other members of the Flying Opera Company.

In his later life he would go on to write a book titled "The Lives of the Avatar".

Monk Jinpa was present at the Southern Air Temple when Avatar Kyoshi sought refuge there, following the death of Avatar Kuruk's earthbending master, Jianzhu, who wished to control the next incarnation of the Avatar.

Jinpa was somewhat responsible for Kyoshi's accommodation at the Southern Air Temple. One day, he informed her that investigators sent by the Earth King believed that daofei were responsible for the mass poisoning in Yokoya that killed several Earth Sages as well as some of the Avatar mansion's staff. When asked about any news from Qinchao, Jinpa, unused to relaying so much dreadful news, reported that the authorities had recovered Jianzhu's body and a couple of witnesses corroborated her story, confirming that a young man killed him in cold blood. However, most of the townfolk weren't convinced her of innocence; the Avatar remarked that she was not going to bother the Chins anytime soon. Lastly, Jinpa informed her that Jianzhu changed his will, bequeathing the mansion and all his wealth to Kyoshi, as well as urging the other sages to support her. This gave the impression to the world that Kyoshi murdered him to gain his wealth, as Jinpa noted it was suspicious the Avatar and the Earth Sage were meeting in Qinchao so soon after the poisoning.

entities.name: Jinzuk and Rina
entities.description:
Rina was the daughter of Avatar Roku and his wife Ta Min. As Rina grew up, she met and later married Jinzuk, who became a magistrate of Hira'a. They subsequently settled down in the village and had one daughter together, Ursa. As a master herbalist, Rina taught her daughter much about medicinal herbs and poisons.

When Ursa was twenty-one years old, Fire Lord Azulon approached the couple with Prince Ozai in tow. The Fire Sages had prophesied that a powerful bloodline would result from the marriage between his son and a descendant of Avatar Roku, namely Ursa, and Azulon wished to bring this prediction to fulfillment. While Jinzuk was entertaining the guests in the family's greenhouse, Rina was inside the main house, crying over the Crown Prince headpiece that she had inherited from her father. When Ursa came home, Rina told her to go to her father and his guests in the greenhouse, but emphasized to her daughter that she loved her.

Ursa accepted Ozai's marriage proposal, stating that it brought much honor to her family. Rina and Jinzuk attended their daughter's wedding and bid her a final farewell, as during their lifetime, the consorts of the Fire Nation royals were not permitted to have any connection with their family or home towns. Ursa attempted to have letters secretly sent home, but was betrayed by her servant, Elua, to Ozai, and no letters ever reached Jinzuk and Rina. Both of them died years before Ursa's eventual banishment, having never heard from their daughter again.

entities.name: Jiro
entities.description:
Jiro was once a member of the Creeping Crystal Triad. After assisting the triad in achieving a "big score", Jargala Omo rewarded him with a large portion of the payout. This was enough money for Jiro to leave the triad and try to build a legitimate life for himself.

Jiro invested his money in an old, abandoned theater in Harmony Park that had not yet been redeveloped, and completely renovated it into the Stoneriver Auction House, spearheading the construction. Although it was relatively new and recent, the auction house was built by traditional artisan methods to give it a historical air, allowing it to present itself as something classy and old, with deep roots in the antiquities trade throughout the world. When the auction house opened, Jiro meticulously ensured all his items came with a bill of sale, and worked with historians to authenticate all purchases he made. Jiro also started dating Little Yang, a talented singer. He did not tell her about his past with the triad, and started doing his best to be the legitimate businessman she understands him to be.

Jiro was doing his best to steer clear of any criminal activity, and achieved relative success at the auction house. However, Jargala started pressuring him into auctioning stolen and illicit goods. She was quick to remind him that he made the money to open the auction house thanks to the triad, and wanted him to pay his dues once more. The auctioneer was torn on what to do, as while he owed a lot to his former boss, he was well aware that the Creeping Crystal Triad was dangerous.

Jargala managed to convince Jiro to hold an illegal auction night for the whole of Republic City, selling valuables and relics looted by the Creeping Crystal Triad during the Earth Empire attack on the city. As the relics would be officially sold through the auction house, they would be made "legitimate" through sale, with money being laundered to the triad.

entities.name: Jiyung
entities.description:
Jiyung was born on Karr Lok Island of the Fire Nation. She attended the island's school, Sunray Academy, where she made three friends: Adaki, Aera, and Sujun.

One day during one of their meditation classes at Sunray Academy, Jiyung realized that Adaki had fallen asleep next to her and woke him up. After class, she, Aera, and Sujun expressed concern for their tired friend. The group's talk was interrupted by another student who declared that a fight between students was taking place at one of the school's training rooms.

Once Jiyung and her friends arrived at the training room, they witnessed a group of sixteen-year-old students easily defeating a group of six graders. Jiyung commented that the older students clearly had an age advantage in regard to their firebending power, yet also demonstrated highly trained skill. After the match, the students were surprised when Chuan, the top firebending teacher of their school, appeared on the stage to declare that they were still seeking fifth graders for a youth team to enter the regional bending tournament. She offered to train any fifth graders who enlisted, despite her students usually being fourteen at the youngest. Much to Jiyung's horror, Adaki suddenly declared that he and his friends would sign up.

Afterward they went to math class, and Jiyung used the opportunity to calculate their winning chances in the regional bending tournament. During the next lunch break, she desperately told Adaki that they had little chance of succeeding, not to mention her own tendency to crack under pressure. Adaki remained unfazed, pointing out that they would fight as a team. Despite also being skeptical, Sujun and Aera also mused how they could use the potential prize money. Realizing that her friends were leaning toward joining the tournament, Jiyung gave in and admitted that they could see how the training would go. As Adaki tried to sign them up, discussed a team name. Though the friends agreed on "Team Adaki" for the time being, Jiyung and the others clarified that the name did not signify Adaki being the official leader.
entities.short_description: Jiyung was born on Karr Lok Island of the Fire Nation. She attended the island's school, Sunray Academy, where she made three friends: Adaki, Aera, and Sujun.

entities.name: Jobal
entities.description:
In 174 AG, when President Raiko ordered a mandatory evacuation of the citizens of Republic City, Jobal decided that the government did not have the right to make him leave, and thus stayed in his apartment. When the other citizens of Republic City evacuated and abandoned their pets, he took them in, fed them, and valued them as his family.

After the invasion was stopped, Avatar Korra and Meelo went searching for the pets. Eventually, Meelo found one of the pets, Nibbles, and followed it into Jobal's apartment, where he found the rest of the animals along with Jobal. When the airbender said that he was going to return the pets to their owners, Jobal firmly refused, stating that they were like family to him. However, when Meelo showed him photographs of the pets with their original owners, Jobal decided to let Meelo return the pets, sadly saying goodbye to them. Meelo then suggested the Jobal should return with him and live in a refugee camp, where there was food, tents, and people to keep him company, an offer to which he agreed.

One day at the camp, Meelo served Jobal dinner, as well as giving him a myriad of ring-tailed winged lemurs as replacements for his previous pets.

entities.name: Joh
entities.description:
Joh was the eight child of two fathers belonging to the rich and influential Jin family on Jasmine Island. "Unplanned but beloved", Joh was born about a decade after than their older siblings. All their close relatives were wealthy and successful; their parents and siblings excelled as merchants and had set up numerous trade routes. It was generally expected that Joh would also follow this trend, though they were generally allowed to pursue their passions, with their fathers providing both emotional as well as financial support. Joh eventually opted to temporarily leave Jasmine Island to attend Ba Sing Se University. When they returned home, Joh contemplated their further career options, and joined the protectors until they had made a decision about their chosen enterprise.

Joh thus attended a formal tea ceremony in an temple at Jasmine Island's coast, where they and four others —Ara, Fu Karaq, Revik, Yarru— had gathered with the protectors' leader Chidaw and an elderly talekeeper named Siarruk. In this ceremony, they officially joined the protectors. Later that day, the five new protectors opted to celebrate their new status together, and took a small fishing boat on a joyride. Eventually, they spotted a large warship approaching Jasmine Island, followed by a smaller vessel. To the group's shock, the large ship was manned by Fifth Nation corsairs under Tagaka, while the smaller ship was attacking them under the leadership of famous Fire National Hei-Ran. After making contact with the latter, Joh and their comrades hurried back to Jasmine Island to warn the locals of the upcoming pirate raid.

The group and the other protectors subsequently fended off a first landing led by a pirate scout force under Erchtei. Indeed, Joh and their comrades fought hard in the subsequent battle, even battling Tagaka herself and helping to defeat Erchtei, though both managed to escape. The group also discovered that another protector, Mirlon, had defected to the Fifth Nation and assisted the raid. They confronted the turncoat.

Joh and their comrades subsequently helped to decide what the Jasmine Islanders should do with the pirates captured during the failed raid. They also tried to mediate in an unexpected dispute between Hei-Ran and the rescued Tei Eesoni.

entities.name: Jojan
entities.description:
Sometime after the end of the Hundred Year War, Jojan notified San about Giya entering the store and was informed that she was simply another fake collector. Jojan snickered alongside his boss when he dismissed the girl's attempts to purchase the shell of a hermit marmoset and later attempted to escort Suki out of the store. He urged the Kyoshi Warrior to stop squirming so that he would not be forced to be aggressive with her. After he refused to release Suki, Jojan was flipped over and knocked unconscious. He was woken up by San shortly after and ordered to fetch buckets of water to put out the fire which his boss inadvertently started.

entities.name: Joo Dee
entities.description:
Joo Dee once served as a caretaker and tour guide for Aang and his companions after their arrival in the city. She effectively shared this role with several other ex-Cultural Ambassadors.

This Joo Dee was one of many women brainwashed to become Cultural Ambassadors. Her true name was unknown; Dai Li agents tended to reuse the name Joo Dee for all of the Cultural Ambassadors as "they had a hard time telling them apart".

Joo Dee first appeared to be a stereotypically vapid and ignorant tour guide. Despite the fact that Team Avatar had information regarding the war against the Fire Nation, she constantly "handled" the entire group into following her tour, promising them an audience with the Earth King within six to eight weeks. She showed no change in personality when Team Avatar responded negatively to her bad news and was constantly smiling, giving her a somewhat eerie demeanor. When Aang and the group went searching for Appa and information about the war, Joo Dee hung back from the others, ever-smiling. When Sokka asked a question that got close to the truth, Joo Dee would smile broadly and shake her head at whoever was under interrogation, eliciting a withdrawn and scared reaction from the person. When Team Avatar crashed the Earth King's party, Joo Dee urged them to leave lest they all be in trouble. She attempted to usher them out, but by doing so, she inadvertently caused Aang to spill the contents of the jug he was carrying over one of the noble women and subsequently expose himself as the Avatar. When all the party guests became aware of Aang's presence, Joo Dee's perpetual smile melted into something closer to despair and fear.

After meeting with Long Feng, Aang and company were to be escorted home by Joo Dee, but they were shocked to see a different woman with the same name and eerie smile who claimed to be Joo Dee in place of the guide they had initially met.

entities.name: Joonho
entities.description:
Joonho was the captain of Sulan's Smile, a pleasure craft belonging to the Fire Nation Royal Family. In 295 BG, he was tasked with escorting Avatar Kyoshi out of the Fire Nation after the resolution of the Camellia-Peony War.

After the resolution of the Camellia-Peony War, a palace minister arranged transport for Kyoshi. The following morning, the Avatar found Joonho and his crew waiting for Kyoshi at the docks. The crew obeyed the Avatar as she ordered the ship to sail to a dark patch of the Mo Ce Sea and anchor there. Joonho waited for her next order, and expressed confusion when the Avatar told them to stay put until she returned, noting that there was nothing to see. Before telling the captain that there used to be something there, Kyoshi plunged into the sea.

As the Avatar struggled in the water following her meeting with Avatar Kuruk, Joonho and his best swimmers rescued Kyoshi, bringing her up to the side of the boat. As the captain and crew surrounded the Avatar, Kyoshi expressed her irritation that they had disobeyed her order to stay put. After Joonho pointed out that it was obviously a stupid order, Kyoshi drooped her head on the deck and closed her eyes, mumbling to Joonho how he could think he could defy his Avatar.

One month later, the pleasure boat's crew brought Kyoshi to Yokoya before her final confrontation with Yun.

entities.name: Juicy
entities.description:
As Opal desired to free her family, who were at the time incarcerated by Kuvira, she and Lin Beifong saddled up Juicy to prepare for a journey to Zaofu. After Bolin joined their quest as well, Juicy flew the three to the metal city, where he was introduced to Toph Beifong, who made a remark about his body odor being even worse than Appa's. As the elder asked Opal why she chose such a "leaky, nasty thing", the young airbender clarified that Juicy had chosen her and good-heartedly jabbed that she had checked whether she could do something about that, while affectionately petting the bison.

Juicy flew the foursome to a factory not far from Zaofu, where he stayed out of sight, awaiting Opal's summoning after they had rescued Suyin and the rest of her family. Upon hearing her bison whistle call, he rushed in, and took Opal and Bolin to a nearby village to save Zhu Li. Later, Juicy flew the ten people, among them, Suyin and her family, to safety, before heading back toward Republic City after dropping off Toph.

Several months later, Juicy raced Opal, Korra, Asami, Toph, and Suyin to Gaoling, as they hoped to catch up with Kuvira, who has stolen a Metal Clan biplane. The bison landed in the Earth Empire reeducation camp to unload its passengers, who promptly engaged Commander Guan and his soldiers.

entities.name: Jujinta
entities.description:
Jujinta was a "Yuyan" who grew up on an island where he and others underwent harsh training in order to learn how to use projectile weapons such as bows, arrows and knives with pinpoint accuracy. In a later conversation in which his past was brought up, he implied that he and his fellow trainees were forced to do morally reprehensible things to survive, and that those of them who failed to compete with the others were discarded.

At some point, Jujinta was involved in an incident in which he murdered his brother, and left his family to seek forgiveness from the spirits. He ended up in Jonduri, where he made a living by working as an errand runner in Zongdu Chaisee's large organization, but held no love for his employers or compatriots. Jujinta had also taken an oath not to use a bow and arrow. Avatar Yangchen later understood the meaning of Jujinta's customs and rituals through her past lives. Jujinta also mentioned he could never return to his home island again.

In year 17 of the era of Yangchen, Jujinta was competing against another young man, Shigoro, in a knife-throwing contest, the winner of which would be selected for the association's next job. After confirming the prize with association manager Tael, Jujinta stabbed Shigoro in the shoulder of his throwing arm and announced that he was forfeiting the competition, before commenting that Shigoro would not be employable for a while. With little other choice, Tael selected Jujinta for the job and introduced him to Kavik, a runner who was secretly in the employ of Avatar Yangchen, and who sought to infiltrate the association while investigating the Unanimity project.

The rest of the association members refused to talk to Jujinta after they left to take Shigoro away for medical attention, and by extension, they refused to talk to Kavik. Jujinta performed his own personal rituals, before sitting next to Kavik on the bench. Jujinta acted quite coolly around Kavik, aware that the waterbender was trying to pry into him.

entities.name: June
entities.description:
Confident and self-assured, she tracked her prey with the help of her mount, Nyla, a shirshu. Though blind, he saw by means of his powerful scent receptors, reportedly sensitive enough to "smell a rat a continent away". When her work began to dry up after the Hundred Year War's end, June eventually retired from bounty hunting to become the Jasmine Dragon tea discoverer, using her and Nyla's skills to seek out the most rare and dangerous tea ingredients.

June originated from the Earth Kingdom. Her parents were an unusual couple, as her mother was an infamous thief who had been first captured and then rescued by her father, an Earth Kingdom soldier turned bounty hunter. In her childhood, June loved to listen to her parents' stories, in particular of how they fell in love after her father understood her mother's cause. One day, soldiers discovered them, whereupon June's mother told her husband to flee with their daughter, as his punishment for being a deserter would be more severe than hers. Before being captured, her mother implored June to be free.

Now alone with her father, she spent much time traveling with him. It was from him that she adopted the tracking and fighting skills she employed. June's father received a shirshu from a rare animal collector in payment for a bounty, and gave it to her. The shirshu, named Nyla, became June's inseparable companion. She and her father both swore to never owe allegiance to no one and never represent any government authority. Over the course of her career, she met various other bounty hunters, taking a liking to some such as Fan's crew.

Early in 100 AG, June tracked a fleeing target who had stowed on board Zuko's ship and captured him while inflicting mild damage to the ship. Iroh developed an immediate interest in her while Zuko was angered, though quietly impressed, with her proficiency and skill.

entities.name: June's parents
entities.description:
June's mother was originally an infamous thief known for robbing Earth Kingdom nobles, giving their riches to the poor and herself. In contrast, her father was the member of an Earth Kingdom military elite unit. The paths of the two crossed when an Earth Kingdom official tasked the father's unit to hunt down the thief.

The soldiers lured June's mother into a trap using a great treasure, capturing her and handing her over to authorities. She was thrown into a prison. However, one soldier had not just come to regard the Earth Kingdom's system as corrupt, he had also fallen in love with the famous criminal. Much to the thief's surprise, the soldier opened her prison cell's door one day, unlocked her shackles, and allowed her to go free. The criminal reciprocated the soldier's feelings and the two escaped together.

Eventually, the ex-soldier and the thief had a daughter, June. They were loving parents, and the young girl enjoyed listening to her parents' stories, especially the tale of their first meeting. Yet the family life was disrupted when the father's ex-unit discovered their hideout and cornered them during a surprise raid. The mother implored her lover to take June to safety, staying behind to delay the troops. When the ex-soldier initially argued against this decision, the thief declared that she was a mere criminal, whereas he was a defector and thus could expect far more cruel punishments. As the thief urged her partner to ensure that their daughter would always be free, the father took June and escaped through a window of the hideout.

Afterward, June and her father became nomadic bounty hunters, traveling the world. The older man passed on his tracking and fighting skills to his daughter, and also implored her to never work for any government authorities and remain independent. At one point, June's father received a shirshu from a rare animal collector in payment for a bounty, and gifted it to his daughter. The shirshu, named Nyla, became June's inseparable companion.

entities.name: Junho
entities.description:
One of many Fire Nation citizens who felt "lost" following their country's defeat in the Hundred Year War, Junho joined the Rough Rhinos in an attempt to find a place to belong. As part of the group, he served as security detail in employ of Loban and Lao Beifong at the Earthen Fire Refinery.

One day in 102 AG, Team Avatar and three Air Acolytes appeared at the refinery. Lao Beifong ordered the Rough Rhinos to "escort" them off the refinery's premises, but Avatar Aang and Toph Beifong refused to leave. Junho and his comrades were knocked back by airbending and earthbending before they could attack. When the Rough Rhinos quickly got up again, Junho and Yeh-Lu found themselves fighting Katara. Although he was unable to hit the nimble waterbender with his war hammer, Junho was quick to taunt her and Sokka when the two retreated, referring to them as "ice savages". Colonel Mongke promptly urged Junho and Yeh-Lu to get on their komodo rhinos to chase after the Water Tribe members.

The chase concluded at a nearby river, where Junho was initially unfazed by Katara's claim that the Rough Rhinos were in "big trouble". The mercenaries were consequently frozen in ice by the waterbender, and Junho watched silently as Sokka subsequently taunted Yeh-Lu.

A few months later, Junho and the other Rough Rhinos stopped working at the Earthen Fire Refinery.

entities.name: Juniper Kim
entities.description:
Juniper served in the Earth Empire's science division, contributing to the development of General Kuvira's war machines. In the aftermath of Kuvira's siege of Republic City, Juniper wanted to atone by using her talents to heal rather than destroy. She arrived in Republic City and quickly found other scientists looking to use their skills to help those in need. She pitched a project to them: discover peaceful uses of wartime technology to aid Republic City. Her past was not a secret, but she worked behind the scenes, and many were surprised to learn she worked for the Earth Empire. As she was seeking funding, she met Asami Sato, the CEO of Future Industries. Asami saw that Juniper's willingness to make up for past misdeeds was genuine, and the two became friends.

With some pooled funds and pulled strings, Juniper and her team secured an unused building in one of the city's industrial areas and started their work. As interest grew among other innovators and politicians, Juniper got used to explaining how weapons and other technology could be harnessed for tools. However, those who did not share her vision started paying attention to the project as well. The Peace Lily Society opposed the use of technology and weapons invented through the oppression of the Earth Kingdom's people, and started protesting outside Juniper's laboratory for weeks.

Eventually, the canisters were stolen from the laboratory, along with weapons from Kuvira's mech. Juniper arrived one night to find the canisters were gone and the scientists working at the laboratory at the time were knocked out. Asami used her resources to help Juniper to keep all protesters and reporters at bay, as the scientist had no experience dealing with the press and the theft could turn out to be a PR disaster.

Juniper wanted to help the world struggling through the use of technology. She was ashamed of working on Kuvira's war machines, and ever since fleeing the Earth Empire she tried to use her skills for good. She was always anxious about what people thought of her upon learning that she worked on the weapon that caused so much pain and suffering. Juniper was primarily driven to atone for her past and could be overcome with guilt.

entities.name: Juno
entities.description:
While lounging in his hut with his friends, Juno encountered Katara and Sokka, who had been separated from the rest of Team Avatar after a storm. Upon landing, Sokka fell on Juno's hut and destroyed it. Juno was outraged by this and wanted Sokka to reimburse the damage he had caused. He and his fellow thieves threatened the duo with Sokka's weapons. Sokka was unable to defend himself as he had broken his arm when he made contact with the hut, so Katara used the little water she carried in her water skin to create a diversion, buying herself and Sokka enough time to make a getaway. The band of thieves gave chase and found the siblings calmly awaiting them at the bank of a river. Katara raised a giant wave of water, forcing Juno and his friends to return their stolen belongings. They did so reluctantly, but when one of Juno's friends threatened and insulted them, Katara and Sokka decided that the thieves could use a "cool-down". The waterbender brought down the wave and washed Juno and his friends away.

entities.name: Junsik
entities.description:
In approximately 316 BG, Junsik married Hei-Ran after she returned from her time as a companion of Avatar Kuruk and began teaching at the Royal Fire Academy for Girls. Their marriage was so fulfilling that, in Kelsang's eyes, Hei-Ran was at her happiest during that time.

A few years later, around the time of Kuruk's death, Junsik and Hei-Ran welcomed their daughter, Rangi. However, Junsik passed away shortly afterward, leaving Hei-Ran grieving and widowed.

Junsik was rarely mentioned in historical accounts. His daughter, Rangi, expressed guilt over not thinking about him as often as she did about Kelsang, but she wished she had more time to spend with both of them.

entities.name: Junyi
entities.description:
Junyi was a swordsmith who fell in love with one of his clients, a man who was married to a woman who was the mayor of the town. The feeling was mutual and the two men were set to run away together, but their affair was discovered by the mayor. She had her husband killed and pinned the crime on Junyi, manipulating the system so he had no way to prove his innocence.

Since then, he was on the run, posing as a lowly beggar in various towns to uncover corrupt people in power and bring them to justice under the identity of Langzi. Others said that Langzi was a master warrior who could wield any weapon. No one knew who they were or what they looked like, as Junyi always kept his face covered in a mask, but people knew that Langzi's focus was always taking down corrupt politicians who exploited the common folk. Langzi eventually rose to the top of the Dai Li's most wanted list.

entities.name: Juro
entities.description:
Juro was the elder sibling, and generally handled interpersonal and political issues on Goro's behalf due to the younger brother lacking talent for either. The two brothers were extremely close and looked out to keep each other safe. According to Juro, there was a "long story" behind the circumstances of how he and Goro became officers in the military.

After being assigned to serve on the prison rig, Juro became known to both other guards as well as the prisoners for his extremely polite and humane nature. This made him generally popular, though some soldiers regarded him as a try-hard who was too nice to serve in the military. Juro disliked his commander, the cruel warden, though generally obeyed him as he had no interest in incurring his wrath.

In late 99 AG, Juro and the other guards were put on alert by the warden due to suspicious activity across the rig. Juro discovered the source of the problems, Avatar Aang, as he was patrolling the prison's factory section. The soldier casually greeted the intruder and asked for his name, while introducing himself. Afterward, he politely asked what Aang was doing in the factory area; the airbender responded that he was just hanging around. With some regret, Juro made it clear how unbelievable this claim was, considering the circumstances. This meant he would have to take Aang into custody. The officer was saddened when Aang declared his unwillingness to surrender. The two engaged in a short duel, and Juro was bested. He complimented his opponent's strength before fleeing to get backup; however, he forgot his key on the way.

Later, Juro and Goro rediscovered Aang at the factory's central vent. As the airbender had just monologued about his aims, Juro expressed his admiration about his enemy's plan and asked whether he had thought about it alone. His conversation with Aang was cut short by Goro, however, who was eager for battle. Though the two brothers were a formidable fighting team, they could not defeat Aang. In the clash, Goro was hit hard and fell unconscious, whereupon Juro became extremely concerned. Though Aang assured him that his younger brother was mostly unharmed, Juro readily explained the way to the airbender's target area so that his opponent got out of the way and he could bring Goro to safety.

entities.name: Kahchi
entities.description:
Kahchi originally earned some renown as a guan dao master in service to the Fire Nation before joining the Rough Rhinos. He was the squad's oldest member.

At some point between 95 and 99 AG, Kahchi and his comrades were hired by Fire Lord Ozai to hunt down Onomu, a former Fire army general who had defected to the Earth Kingdom.

During the spring of 100 AG, Team Avatar was camping out in the southwestern Earth Kingdom when Kahchi and the Rough Rhinos ambushed them for the second time. However, the friends managed to ward the military group off and escape.

Not too long after the incident, the Rough Rhinos raided the Earth Kingdom's Chin Village in honor of Fire Lord Ozai. In an attempt to scare the village, Kahchi used his weapon to destroy the statue of the village's founder, Chin the Great. Team Avatar was there by coincidence, since Aang had just undergone a trial for killing Chin in his past life as Avatar Kyoshi and was found guilty by the town's mayor when Kyoshi confessed to the crime. When Aang, still dressed in Kyoshi's clothes, approached Kahchi, the latter readied his guan dao. Aang leaned forward and extended his arms out behind him, holding one of Kyoshi's fans, which he opened as he ran. He spun aside out of the rhino's way at the last moment and used the fan to airbend Kahchi out of his saddle over the cliff.

entities.name: Kahola
entities.description:
Kahola was born to a Southern Water Tribe mother, Gayu, who had abandoned the tribe because she was shunned for a romantic fling with a Fire Nation soldier. As she was not one to let fate decide her destiny, Gayu set sail and became a prosperous pirate with the only Southern waterbender pirate raiding the seas.

Gayu began to push her son, Kahola, to take his rightful place as leader. However, the bright young waterbender was not sure if he wanted to embrace a life of piracy. He wanted to know if there was something more out for him other than raiding and stealing from others to make a living.

He decided to strike out on his own, but Gayu's protégée, Honu, pledged to follow and protect Kahola. Kahola was intending to find a pirate called Duga, who he heard was a merchant as well as a pirate, and wanted to see if he could give Kahola some advice.

Kahola was unsure whether a life of raiding and stealing was right for him. He was otherwise a bright young man, who could be both perky and arrogant.

entities.name: Kai
entities.description:
Kai grew up as an orphan. When he was finally adopted by a nice family in 170 AG, he took advantage of their kindness by stealing their life savings and spent six months on the run from Earth Kingdom authorities.

Following Harmonic Convergence, Kai soon discovered he possessed airbending. Soon after, he encountered Team Avatar, who was searching for airbenders to rebuild the Air Nation. He told them a false story on how his parents were killed by outlaws who were pursuing them, earning their sympathy and quickly being accepted in their company. Just as he boarded their airship, ready to depart, a sheriff and his deputies arrived, whom he falsely claimed to be outlaws. After Avatar Korra bested them, the sheriff revealed Kai's true identity as a thief. The boy attempted to run off with his loot, but was caught by Mako. The sheriff quickly took custody of the young lad, intending to send him to prison. However, in exchange for returning the life savings to Kai's family, Korra convinced the sheriff to allow Kai to turn over a new leaf with Team Avatar. Though the compromise was accepted, Mako warned Kai that he would be watching him, stating he knew the kind of person Kai was, due to having a similar past. Promising to change, the young boy turned to board the ship, where he gladly accepted Jinora's offer to teach him more about airbending, just before she blushed.

While en route to Ba Sing Se, Kai attended an airbending lesson under Jinora's tutelage, during which he swiftly took down Bumi with one air swipe. He stole the retired commander's wallet during the skirmish, engaging in a game of chase after Bumi found out.

Upon arriving in Ba Sing Se, Kai's kleptomania got the better of him and he slipped away to use his airbending to pickpocket the wealthy. When the team noticed his absence, Kai was found by Mako and Bolin while he robbed a rich Ba Sing Se citizen. He ran away from them, though as he boarded the monorail, he was grabbed by the collar by Mako. However, he used his airbending to free himself and managed to exit the cart just in time before it left for the Lower Ring, leaving the brothers on it without their wallets.

entities.name: Kaja
entities.description:
As a Fire Sage, Kaja was chosen to help Avatar Roku learn to control the Avatar State. Roku managed to trigger the state after five months by utilizing the power of the winter solstice sun rather than triggering it on his own. In doing this, he became trapped under its influence and could not control his actions, destroying most of the temple. Kaja eventually managed to free him from the Avatar State and ordered him to rebuild the temple, making it clear to the Avatar that his training would only be continued after the reconstruction. Not long after, Roku managed to master the Avatar State and Kaja's job was complete.

He remained a staunch supporter of Roku after helping him master the Avatar State. Internally, he worked with his fellow Fire Sages to preserve Fire Nation spirituality, and often worked with the Fire Lord on these matters. While Sozin was worried that the popularity of Air Nomad philosophies and teachings among the Fire Nation nobility was eroding Fire Nation traditions, Kaja was not worried. He thought that fads had a way of coming and going among the rich, and his focus was on maintaining tradition for future activities. While he was concerned with what he saw from his nation's subtle moves to expand their reach, he did not want to distract Roku too much from his important international work.

Following the Air Nomad Genocide, Kaja was the first to make a controversial declaration that the Avatar had not died in the attack. Some time later, Kaja fathered a son, who in turn fathered Shyu. Kaja's son fiercely defended his father's views and was eventually executed for defying the Fire Lord.

Kaja was committed to the cause of balance and service of the Avatar. He was a very friendly and spiritual man devoted to Roku, and was accepting of people from all nations.

entities.name: Kallik
entities.description:
Kallik lost her entire family during the Hundred Year War. Sometime after the war, seeking a place to belong, she joined Jie and the Denied, a nonbending extremist group that sought to overturn the existing order through violence.

Around 110 AG, Kallik participated in a mission led by Jie, leader of the Denied, to seize the statuette of Sonam from the Southern Air Temple. They ambushed Avatar Aang during his journey to the temple. Despite Aang showing no intent to fight, they continued attacking him so that Hong, one of their comrades, could search through the Avatar's collection. When Hong called out that he had found the statuette, the airbender quickly reclaimed it and ascended to the top of the tower. In pursuit, Kallik followed him to the beams with her rope dart and confronted him there.

During their struggle, an explosive arrow shot by Jie nearly struck Kallik until she was saved by Aang, however, who dropped the statuette to catch her, losing consciousness briefly upon hitting the ground. The ensuing explosion destabilized the tower. Realizing it was about to collapse, Jie and the others fled, shouting for Kallik to grab the scroll that had slipped from the statuette. Though confused that the Avatar had saved her, she obeyed and escaped. As they rushed back to their airship waiting outside, the upper half of the structure began to tilt, threatening to crush the airship. Yet Aang awakened and entered the Avatar State, earthbending it back into place, letting Kallik and her group get away.

Upon discovering the map, Kallik traveled with the Denied across the Endless Ocean to snatch Sonam's staff. During the voyage, she spotted the Avatar and the Fire Lord's airship through a telescope. A brief clash broke out, and just as Tagah was about to crash the Denied's airship, Aang intervened by airbending away all their grappling hooks and unleashing a powerful gust of wind to push the two parties apart. They entered the Immortal Storm, where they lost sight of Team Avatar. As they struggled through the storm for hours, Tagah emerged from the mist, declared the Avatar dead, and promised them a new world where they would have the power. In exchange for their loyalty, he granted airbending to every member of the Denied, including Kallik.

entities.name: Kallika
entities.description:
Kallika was born into a wealthy family in the Northern Water Tribe. As she was a waterbender, she was expected to become a healer due to her place in society. However, Kallika refused to settle in the role being forced upon her.

Every time Kallika's teachers tried to shove her into the role of a peaceful, caring woman, Kallika shoved back three times harder. Eventually, she understood that her family would never understand who she truly was, and what she wanted. She ended up running away from the tribe, and started making her choices, which started to bring her a sense of joy for the first time.

Eventually, she made her way to the Fire Nation colonies. She helped to quell a riot in Machi when the Harmony Restoration Movement fell apart, and met Ginkgo, Ziyi, Toklo, and Chihiro in the process. The five companions were subsequently given a special dispensation by the regional governor to help towns adjust to the fallout of colonization. Kallika soon grew close to Chihiro, and wanted to help her break free of her Fire Nation family's past.

The group later came to Linsho during the Squid Ink Festival. While in town, they watched a conflict break out between the town's Fire Nation Loyalists and Earth Kingdom Restorationists, with each blaming the other for a fire at a Blue Skies Fisheries warehouse. Mayor Leaf tasked the companions with finding the arsonist as quick as possible, while also keeping people safe, as a storm was brewing.

entities.name: Kalyaan
entities.description:
Kalyaan was always talented in comparison to his younger brother. While he took care of Kavik, he also teased him, being physically rough with him during wrestling and throughout their childhood conditioning the younger boy to feel weak and unresponsive in his presence.

During his youth, Kalyaan and the then eight year old Kavik got separated from the rest of the family during a hunt, and were subsequently lost in a powerful snowstorm for nearly a month. Kavik was convinced he had cursed the hunt in some way and began to cry, though Kalyaan told him that everything was going to be alright. At one stage, Kalyaan cut strips from one of his mittens and fed them to Kavik, a desperation tactic to give his younger brother the energy to keep walking in the cold. He subsequently lost two fingers to frostbite from where he had opened his mitten, but told Kavik not to worry about it, as eight was considered a lucky number in the Earth Kingdom and the Fire Nation. The adults who could not find them suspected that the two brothers getting lost was potentially caused by spirits.

Four years later, the family moved to the shang city of Bin-Er after hunts began to sour across the region.

After six months, Kalyaan walked out on his job, having chosen to secretly become one of the errand runner informants common to the shang cities. Early on in his career, he became friends with Henshe, then a low-level administrator, and the pair started working together to secure small advantages and trade them into bigger ones. He used the money from his new job to gift his parents a new house, convincing them that it was better to live closer to the international district, even though the new wooden structure was harder to clean and to keep warm. Not long after, Nuqingaq and Partners had their most critical customers poached by someone with intimate knowledge of the client list and contract renewals, and most lost their jobs, though Kavik and Ujurak stayed on. Kalyaan never came home after this, making it obvious that he was to blame.

entities.name: Kam
entities.description:
Kam, along with Noa and Soonjei, was contracted by Malina and Maliq as part of a construction team they assembled for the reconstruction of the Southern Water Tribe shortly after the end of the Hundred Year War. Sometime during their work at the South Pole, Noa and two other benders encountered Katara and Sokka, whom they warn to stay out of construction sites. The construction crew subsequently attempted to remove the two siblings by force but were subdued by Katara with her waterbending.

Sometime later, the construction crew went to brief Malina, Maliq, and Hakoda about ongoing construction, with each member showing surprise at seeing Katara and Sokka. Later during a festival on Southern Water Tribe grounds, Noa and the construction crew defended Maliq and Malina from an attack by Gilak. During the battle, they were easily defeated by Toph Beifong.

Kam was an accomplished waterbender, able to hold his own against nonbending opponents. However, since he was more accustomed to using his bending abilities for construction work than fighting, he was easily overpowered when faced with a trained bender.
